articles.title: Tulane's Hall is "Concentrating on Us" Leading Up to Duke
articles.excerpt: The first of September brought the first pre-game press conference for the Wave, starting with head coach Will Hall
articles.source_type: Gameweek squads, team news round-ups, deadline reminders
articles.body: Tulane's Hall is "Concentrating on Us" Leading Up to Duke Sep 16, 2023; Hattiesburg, Mississippi, USA; Former Southern Miss Golden Eagles head coach Will Hall gestures in the second half against the Tulane Green Wave at M.M. Roberts Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Chuck Cook-USA TODAY Sports | USA TODAY Sports via Reuters Connect Tulane Football Schedule 2026 Week 1 - Â at Duke , September 5 Week 2 - Â South Alabama , September 12 Week 3 -Â at Kansas State , September 19 Week 4 -Â Southern Miss , September 26 Week 5 - OPEN DATE, October 3 Week 6 -Â at Army , October 10 Week 7 -Â Memphis , October 16 Week 8 -Â UTSA , October 24 Week 9 -Â at Charlotte , October 30 Week 10 -Â Tulsa , November 7 Week 11 -Â at Rice , November 14 Week 12 - North Texas, November 21 Week 13 - at South Florida, November 27 Sign up for the weeklyÂ On Si Tulane "[The season's] been a long time coming, and I know we're really ready to play," head coach Will Hall opened with during Tuesday's press conference. Tulane's first game against Duke is this Saturday at 2:30pm CT , and we'll have much more coverage to come. So stay tuned to On SI Tulane for all of your Green Wave news. The Looming Season What we've seen on social media at On SI is that there is a lot of valid questions regarding this new Tulane team. Travelling into the ACC champion's house and coming out with a victory is no easy feat for any team in college football, so TU will have to be prepared for a gritty, grind-em-out game against the Blue Devils. "(We've) got a tremendous challenge coming this weekend, everybody knows that. Duke (is) a really good team..." is what coach Hall closed his opening statement with. When asked about how he felt about the upcoming season, in general, he replied: "I'm just blessed man... Just trying to take advantage of everyday, and get better every day. That's how I live my life." He continued: "Our guys are going to play hard (on) Saturday. I know that everyone's going to play their tail off for each other. That's what we do at Tulane." Not Just a Rematch Although the Green Wave faced the Blue Devils last season, the rematch really isn't the story here. The story is about two conference champions facing off in week one. We believe it is amplified even more when you take into account that Duke is a P4 champion (ACC), and Tulane is a G6 champion (American). When asked about the perspective of this title heavy bout, Hall had to say, "Maybe so. Honestly, I really don't look at what everybody is talking about. I know we've got a good football team (and) I know we've got to prove that... I know Duke has a good football team... We've got an exciting schedule in front of us, but it's one we're excited about." Speaking to last year's game, Hall acknowledged the story and weight behind last year's match up, specifically regarding Mensah's return to New Orleans after transferring to Duke. More importantly, however, coach Hall was more focused on the here and now, "Obviously (these are) two different teams... The thing we're doing is, we're concentrating on us... We're looking forward to showing what we've got." The Keys If TU wishes to start their season with a statement win in Durham, they'll first have to stop second year running back, Nathan Sheppard We talked about Sheppard extensively during our opponent previews, but if Tulane wants success, they'll have to hold him in check. "[He's] really hard to tackle." Hall said. "We know that we'll have to rally to tackle him, he rarely ever gets tackled by just one person, so he presents a lot of challenges," he finished. Another key will be the quarterback play, which has been of concern for quite some time. Until last Monday , there had been no announcement as to who would start week one for the Green Wave. Ultimately, the job would fall into Zeon Chriss-Gremillion's hands to take the reigns of this Wave offense. Coach Hall said more of the same when it came to Zeon and what he wants out of his starting quarterback. Zeon will need the "right eyes" because if his eyes aren't right, then he's failed the first step at being a good quarterback. Coach Hall repeated what he had said at an earlier press conference this Fall, "There's going to be about five opportunities in every game for a quarterback to win the game." Hall wants his quarterback dialed and locked in with little mistakes. Talkin' Duke "Their head coach ( Manny Diaz ) runs the defense," Hall responded after being asked what stuck out about the Blue Devil defense. "I've got a lot of respect for him... we know they're going to play hard," he finished. When asked about San Jose State transfer and starting Duke quarterback, Walker Eget , Hall said, "He really can (throw the ball)... He made some great throws while he was at SJS, (and) he's coming off an injury." Coach Hall had a lot of respect for the transfer quarterback and his experience, and if the Wave wish to throw him off his game, this young defensive line will have to get active and physical. "(Eget has) seen it before." Hall spoke more to Eget's experience with yet another analogy: "People can tell you what it's like to ride a bike, but until you ride one you just don't understand it, and (Eget has) ridden the bike a lot." articles.title: Nebraska Center Justin Evans Earns Prestigious Honor From Teammates
articles.excerpt: Evans is the acknowledged leader of the offensive line. He was voted a single-digit jersey and even though he can’t wear it, it shows the respect he has earned
articles.source_type: Gameweek squads, team news round-ups, deadline reminders
articles.body: Nebraska Center Justin Evans Earns Prestigious Honor From Teammates Nebraska center Justin Evans is the established leader of the Huskers' offensive line. | Nebraska Athletics Beyond an effective quarterback, running backs and receivers, football offenses â Nebraskaâs included â need a quality offensive line to make the motor purr. Nebraskaâs offensive line dominated much of the offseason talk . Improvements were needed. Money was invested. Leadership of the new offensive line falls on the broad shoulders of center Justin Evans . Centers tend to be O-line leaders, but Evansâ leadership comes from his personality and many other intangibles. He was one of three Huskers who went to Big Ten Media Days in Chicago this summer. He was voted by his teammates to wear the Huskersâ famous single-digit jersey. And even though he canât wear it because of college football rules, the vote shows in what esteem Evans is held. Talking about leadership only goes so far. A tangible act of the single-digit jersey is slam-dunk proof of Evansâ value to the Huskers. âIt just shows how much my teammates respect me and I have so much respect for my teammates,â Evans said at a press conference Tuesday. âFor them to even know that I canât wear a single digit and for them to vote me just means everything to me. And Iâll do anything for this team. âAnd I know itâs just I love my team. So it shows that they just trust me and anything to lead this team.â Justin Evans talks about leadership Evans is a 6-foot-2, 315-pounder from East Orange, N.J., who is in his final year of eligibility. He started all 13 games at center in 2025. He is expected to be a high draft pick in 2027. Evans recognizes his own growth as a leader. Earning the single-digit vote was a great tribute for a player on whom the Huskers are counting on greatly. âIâve grown so much just understanding my team and who Iâm playing with and getting to know them on a another level,â Evans said. âItâs the first important step of leadership is just knowing who youâre playing for and knowing who they are playing for and that brings us together as a team.â New offensive line coach Geep Wade understands leadership and how important for his charges to take charge. He works closely with Evans. âEven now heâs still pushing me to be the vocal guy on the team and just encouraging guys on and off the field, more so on the field, just keeping guys going, you know, when we may get into those lulls in the game and just keeping a voice, a positive voice for the guys in the room,â Evans said. Changes on offensive line Throughout the spring and early summer, the offensive line starters were believed to be set. That changed Monday when Nebraska released its first depth chart for 2026 Nebraska's Gunnar Gottula is the listed starter at right tackle going into the season. | Nebraska Athletics The most notable change? Gunnar Gottula is the starter at right tackle with South Carolina transfer Tree Babalade â the expected starter â now below Gottula. Gottula has been making strides throughout the summer and this starting nod shows that. âGunnar has been, from when he first got here to now, has been another great leader,â Evans said. âHeâs somebody who I look up to in the room. He helps me out a lot and heâs very smart as well. âSo if I have any questions, Iâm going to Gunnar asking him like, âHey, like what do you think I should do here?â âAnd I have nothing but respect for him. Being a hometown kid, all he wants to do is play football here. So Iâm really proud of his progress that he has shown throughout this offseason.â O-line eager to face Ohio The new offensive line will get its first test Saturday against Ohio at Memorial Stadium. âGoing into our first game this week, weâve built a pretty cohesive unit, playing as one with guys coming in from different conferences and played for different coaches,â Evans said. âTheyâve came in and embraced the process with us and itâs been a great long couple of months getting to know those guys and just helping them understand the process of how we do things here at Nebraska.â Clicking with Rhule Evans said he has a good relationship with head coach Matt Rhule. They have a connection. âMe and Coach Rhule, I mean us East Coast guys are always going to stick together no matter what,â Evans said with a smile. Nebraska coach Matt Rhule and center Justin Evans, both East Coast guys, have developed a relationship that goes beyond the field. | Kaleb Henry âI have so much respect for Coach Rhule and how intentional he is with the game and how he wants the players to understand the game. Not just play football, but understand the situations on why we do things or how he wants to put us in better positions of success and heâs always going to put the teamâs best interest first.â Evans said he also has clicked with quarterback Anthony Colandrea. âOur relationship has grown a lot too, you know, from him first getting here to now,â Evans said. âThatâs probably one of my closest friends on the team, and he pushes me to be better, and Iâm going to push him to be better. Itâs a two-way street with us, and Iâm excited to see him go out there and ball.â Stay up to date on all things Huskers by bookmarking Nebraska Cornhuskers On SI , subscribing to HuskerMax on YouTube and visiting HuskerMax.com daily. articles.title: Javonte Williams Leads Group of High-Floor, Safe Mid-Round Fantasy Football Running Backs
articles.excerpt: For Fantasy managers who prefer high-floor and safer options at running back, Javonte Williams and two more running backs are perfect for their selection.
articles.source_type: Gameweek squads, team news round-ups, deadline reminders
articles.body: Javonte Williams Leads Group of High-Floor, Safe Mid-Round Fantasy Football Running Backs Dallas Cowboys running back Javonte Williams (33) runs with the ball in the second quarter against the Philadelphia Eagles at AT&T Stadium. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Sometimes going with the safer option with a high floor in Fantasy Football can lead to a championship-caliber season. Fantasy managers should consider these mid-round running backs, who offer a high floor thanks to their bellcow workload. Javonte Williams Williams RB 16, 35 ADP ) will continue his workhorse usage this season after tallying 287 touches last season. The Dallas Cowboys recently released Jaydon Blue , who figured to be Williams biggest threat to touches this season. With Blue out of the picture, Williams is lined up to carry the bulk of the load among Cowboys running backs.Â In his first season with the Dallas Cowboys, Williamsâ workload consisted of a top-ten 252 rushing attempts , which led to a RB 11 finish in standard formats. With CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens on the outside, Williams will benefit from light boxes in his rushing attempts. Williams benefits the most near the goal line as being the main back led to extensive touches near the goal line. Last season, Williams finished eighth in the NFL in rushing touchdowns. Williams is set to repeat another workhorse season with Blue out of Dallas. Javonte Williams, that man has a family!! pic.twitter.com/mlrgoQS6Yv â Ari Meirov (@MySportsUpdate) December 25, 2025 David Montgomery Montgomery (RB 20, 50 ADP) finally gets the chance to work as a lead back after spending the last three seasons as Jahmyr Gibbsâ backup. In Detroit, Montgomery was used extensively as a goal-line back, finishing with at least eight rushing touchdowns each season. Montgomery gets the chance to continue his goal-line work along with expanded touches outside the red zone in his first season with the Houston Texans. A benefit Montgomery will receive in being the starting running back in Houston is the shorter starting field positions the offense will have thanks to the defense.Â The Texans defense finished first in yards allowed per game and third in turnover forced with 29. Having a shorter average field position will lead to more red-zone visits for the Texans offense where Montgomery truly shines.Â David Montgomery getting shifty in the open field ð pic.twitter.com/9PjJY0Rd41 â Nico (@elitetakes_) August 1, 2026 Quinshon Judkins Judkins (RB 23, 54 ADP) produced a decent rookie campaign that was cut short due to injuries. In his rookie season, Judkins averaged 16.4 rushing attempts per game, finishing with 12.1 FPPG in PPR leagues.Â Judkins' high rushing attempts should continue with new head coach Todd Monken at the helm.Â During Monkenâs tenure with the Baltimore Ravens, running back Derrick Henry was always near the top in rushing attempts Judkins is no Henry, but with Monken running the ship, expect a heavy dosage of Judkinsâ rushing attempts for the Browns offense.Â Judkins' usage is compounded with the lack of efficient quarterback play in Cleveland.Â Itâs no secret that Deshaun Watson and Shedeur Sanders arenât in the upper-echelon on QB play. With lesser QB play around him, Monken will turn to Judkins to be the lead horse back for his offense.Â Fantasy managers can expect a similar work rate of 16.4 rushing attempts per game by Judkins in his sophomore season, making the running back a safe option in the mid rounds.Â Quinshon Judkins so far: 10 rushing attempts 71 yards 1 TD pic.twitter.com/X1fmS0JlJ5 â Underdog NFL (@UnderdogNFL) October 19, 2025 More Fantasy Sports on SI News Add us as a preferred source on Google Follow Published 41 minutes ago | Modified 41 minutes ago JEFF SALCEDO Jeff Salcedo is a writer for Fantasy Sports on SI with extensive experience covering the NFL, MMA, NBA, and soccer. articles.body: DEADLINE DAY LIVE: City agree Fernandez deal and sign Ndiaye with Chelsea set to sign Camara Skip to content News Football Transfer News, Rumours & Gossip DEADLINE DAY LIVE: City agree Fernandez deal and sign Ndiaye with Chelsea set to sign Camara Stay up to date with every transfer completed across the Premier League on deadline day. Mitch Fretton Last Update: 1 minute ago 12 min read Add us as a preferred source on Google Welcome to transfer deadline day on 101GreatGoals. Today, we will be keeping you up to date with every deal in the Premier League as it happens, so keep this page open and make sure to refresh every few minutes. There is a lot still to be decided in the closing hours of the summer window, with Manchester City set to spend big on Iliman Ndiaye and Enzo Fernandez, while there could still be movement at Arsenal , Liverpool, Chelsea, Manchester United and Tottenham. 23:00 – The transfer window is closed Teams who successfully lodged a deal sheet have two extra hours to complete transfers. 22:58 – The Bard heads to Leeds Leeds United have added to their defence, bringing in Melvin Bard on loan from Nice with an option to make the deal permanent. 22:24 – Grealish seals Everton return While Everton’s efforts sign a striker may be falling apart, they can at least take solace in the return of Jack Grealish. The Manchester City man spent last season on loan at the Hill Dickinson Stadium, and he is now back for another campaign. “It feels so good. I’m so happy. I think I’m at my best at everything in life, not just football, when I feel loved,” Grealish told evertontv. “That’s what the manager has given me, what my teammates have given me and especially what the fans have given me. “I feel ready to go. I’m ready to start training tomorrow and prepare for the games.” With reports of a failed medical for Folarin Balogun, Everton were said to have pivoted to a loan move for Joshua Zirkzee, but that has been rejected by Manchester United. 22:18: Fulham sign Larsson Fulham have boosted their midfield with the signing of Sweden international Hugo Larsson. Larsson has joined on an initial loan from Eintracht Frankfurt, with the deal featuring a conditional obligation to buy. The arrival of Larsson follows that of Manuel Angel from Real Madrid. ⁠Welcome to Fulham, Hugo Larsson! 🤍 pic.twitter.com/pHgBn9DJfP — Fulham Football Club (@FulhamFC) September 1, 2026 22:04: Spurs confirm Mudryk loan Tottenham have confirmed the signing of Mykhailo Mudryk on a season-long loan from Chelsea. Spurs have the option to make the deal permanent for £75m. The Ukrainian winger has not played competitive football since November 2024, having resolved a doping case with the Football Association last month. We are delighted to announce the signing of Ukraine international forward Mykhailo Mudryk on a season-long loan ✍️ https://t.co/sTK5X6I4wJ pic.twitter.com/NmK8jJTtm8 — Tottenham Hotspur (@SpursOfficial) September 1, 2026 21:28: Chelsea agree Camara deal Big breaking news from Chelsea, who appear to have filled the void left by Enzo Fernandez. It had been suggested Chelsea might fail to sign a midfielder before the deadline, but Fabrizio Romano has reported they have agreed a deal in principle to sign Lamine Camara from Monaco. 🚨🔵 EXCLUSIVE: Chelsea agree deal in principle to sign Lamine Camara from AS Monaco, here we go! 💣 Fee worth €55m and authorization to travel for medical. Initial agreement done now running in order to complete medical and formal steps in time. pic.twitter.com/DuCBSuZBiN — Fabrizio Romano (@FabrizioRomano) September 1, 2026 21:20 – Sunderland *finally* win Fofana fight The Malick Fofana saga cannot be declared definitively over until Sunderland announce his signature. But it appears they have, finally, won the fight for the winger’s signature. Fabrizio Romano reports his agents have informed all parties of his wish to join the Black Cats, with Crystal Palace missing out. 🚨🔴⚪️ Malick Fofana’s agents have just informed all parties involved in transfer-saga that the player wants to join Sunderland. Fofana, now set to join #SAFC as originally planned this morning. pic.twitter.com/6UaIRtFWVJ — Fabrizio Romano (@FabrizioRomano) September 1, 2026 21:01 – Man City complete Ndiaye signing Manchester City have completed the signing of Iliman Ndiaye from Everton on a five-year deal. “I’ve worked my whole life for an opportunity like this,” he told City’s official website after the completion of a £65m transfer. “City are one of the best clubs in the world and I’ve seen them win everything as I’ve grown up. “To be able to write my own chapter in a story that special is the chance of a lifetime and I’m determined to grab it with both hands. 21:00 – Man United make enquiry for Man City’s Ait-Nouri In clear need of help on the left side of their defence, Manchester United are reported have made an enquiry for Manchester City full-back Rayan Ait-Nouri. However, United’s arch rivals expect Ait-Nouri to stay. 20:57 – Balogun move to Everton in doubt Everton are hoping to announce the signing of Monaco striker Folarin Balogun on deadline day after agreeing a £40m fee for the United States international. But there are multiple reports the deal could be off following Balogun’s medical on Merseyside. 20:15 – Sanchez heads to Como as Chelsea send two players to Strasbourg Following their signing of Emi Martinez from Aston Villa, Chelsea goalkeeper Robert Sanchez has joined Como on a season-long loan. Chelsea have also shipped out two players to Ligue 1 Strasbourg, who are also owned by the BlueCo consortium that controls the London club. Forward Deivid Washington has joined Strasbourg on a permanent deal, while midfielder Dario Essugo has made the move on a season-long loan. 20:05 – North London loans News to bring you of two loan deals involving the Premier League’s North London clubs. Arsenal have confirmed that forward Ethan Nwaneri has joined Borussia Dortmund on a season-long loan. While that deal does not involved a purchase obligation, there is such a clause in Kevin Danso’s loan move from Tottenham to Premier League rivals Sunderland. Danso has completed his move to Wearside in a deal that features a £22.25m obligation dependent on Sunderland retaining their place in the Premier League. The Black Cats have paid Tottenham a £2.5m loan fee for Danso, who will sign a four-year contract if the move becomes permanent. 19:49 – David joins Atletico Having brought in Woltemade, Juventus have allowed the departure of another striker in the form of Jonathan David. The Canada international has temporarily swapped Serie A for LaLiga, joining Atletico Madrid on a season-long loan. David scored eight goals for Juventus last season after joining from Lille. 19:35 – Fofana having medical, but for which team? The craziest story of transfer deadline day is undoubtedly that of Lyon winger Malick Fofana. Crystal Palace appeared to have successfully hijacked Sunderland’s deal to sign the Belgian, only for the Black Cats to come back in with an offer that looked to have swayed him to Wearside. However, there are now reports that Palace have matched the Sunderland package, with L’Equipe claiming the player is undergoing a medical with the Lyon staff, but is unsure for which club he will sign. Meanwhile, Sunderland are progressing with a move for Benfica’s Dodi Lukebakio, while Palace are set to sign Midtjylland forward Dario Osorio on loan with an obligation to buy. The obligation is for €26m plus €4m in add-ons. The loan fee is reportedly €2m. 19:05 – Liverpool sign Brughmans Liverpool have added to their goalkeeping ranks with the signing of 18-year-old Lucca Brughmans from Genk. Brughmans will be loaned back to the Belgian side for the 2026-27 season. We have agreed a deal to sign goalkeeper Lucca Brughmans from KRC Genk 🔴 The 18-year-old has put pen to paper on a long-term contract with the Reds and will now return to Genk for the duration of the 2026-27 season 🧤 pic.twitter.com/9p5z60gE6w — Liverpool FC (@LFC) September 1, 2026 18:55 – Woltemade completes Juventus loan Juventus have completed the signing of Newcastle United striker on a season-long loan. Woltemade joined Newcastle last August in a club-record £69million deal, but a red-hot start to his career on Tyneside petered out and, after losing his place in Eddie Howe’s starting XI, he has remained a peripheral figure in a Magpies side unbeaten this season under new manager Matthias Jaissle. The Magpies will receive a loan fee of £3.5m loan fee. The deal does not include an option to buy. Woltemade has scored 11 goals and provided five assists in his time at Newcastle, teeing up Yoane Wissa’s goal in their 2-0 win at Tottenham last Saturday. A new ⚪️⚫️ frontman has arrived… Welcome, Nick Woltemade! 👋 https://t.co/TWhgWCZb7e Powered by @Jeep pic.twitter.com/LDSFOQgHQs — JuventusFC 🇬🇧🇺🇸 (@juventusfcen) September 1, 2026 18:41 – Beto leaves Everton for Fiorentina Everton have confirmed striker Beto has left to join Serie A side Fiorentina on a permanent deal. The Toffees paid over £25m for the Guinea-Bissau international in 2023, but Beto struggled for goals throughout his time with the club, scoring only six in the Premier League. He now returns to Serie A to join a Fiorentina side without a point after the first two games of the season. We can confirm Beto has joined Serie A side Fiorentina on a permanent transfer for an undisclosed fee. Everyone connected with Everton thanks Beto for his dedication, commitment and service. We wish him all the best for the next chapter of his career in Italy. 💙 — Everton (@Everton) September 1, 2026 17:50 – Sunderland win Fofana tug of war Widespread reports have claimed Sunderland have won the battle to sign Malick Fofana from Lyon. Crystal Palace were previously reported to have hijacked the deal, with Fofana supposedly convinced to make the move to Selhurst Park by Pierre Sage. But Sunderland appear to have successfully revived the deal and are reportedly making preparations for him to have a medical in France. 17:07 – Man City agree British record deal for Enzo Fernandez Manchester City have reportedly agreed a £125million deal to sign Enzo Fernandez from Chelsea. The Athletic’s David Ornstein reported that the two clubs have come to terms on a fee that matches the British record Liverpool paid to Newcastle United to sign Alexander Isak on deadline day last year. Fernandez has been given permission to travel to Manchester for a medical. 15:39 – Juventus sign Sarr from Spurs Pape Matar Sarr has joined Juventus on loan for the 2026/27 season. Good luck, Pape 🤍 https://t.co/HwyKvwWIwR pic.twitter.com/57086nvako — Tottenham Hotspur (@SpursOfficial) September 1, 2026 Tottenham have announced the departure of Pape Matar Sarr to Juventus on loan. The Serie A side will have an obligation to buy the midfielder if conditions are met. 15:03 – Newcastle sign Fernandez-Pardo Newcastle have completed the signing of Lille forward Matias Fernandez-Pardo. The deal is worth £51.4m and he will wear the No.20 shirt. 14:02 – Jesus seals Barcelona move Gabriel Jesus has joined Barcelona from Arsenal. The Brazilian forward leaves a Premier League winner, and will look to add the La Liga title to his collection. 13:41 – Ahanor joins Palace after completing Chelsea move Honest Ahanor has joined Crystal Palace on loan for the upcoming season. The Atalanta defender is set to join Chelsea on a permanent deal next summer. 13:05 – Crystal Palace attempting Fofana hijack Crystal Palace are attempting to hijack Sunderland’s deal for Malick Fofana from Lyon. The decision is now up to the player. 12:50 – Aston Villa complete signing of Harwood-Bellis His time to be a Villan… 🟣 Aston Villa is delighted to announce the signing of Taylor Harwood-Bellis from Southampton 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁥󠁮󠁧󠁿 pic.twitter.com/snU0NgU8y1 — Aston Villa (@AstonVilla) September 1, 2026 Aston Villa have completed the signing of Taylor Harwood-Bellis from Southampton. articles.title: Notre Dame vs. Wisconsin Game Notes - Key Storylines for Season Opener
articles.excerpt: Notre Dame and Wisconsin will battle at Lambeau Field on Sunday. Key notes from both squads to get you ready for the big-time battle.
articles.source_type: Gameweek squads, team news round-ups, deadline reminders
articles.body: Notre Dame vs. Wisconsin Game Notes - Key Storylines for Season Opener DUPLICATE***Wisconsin Badgers wide receiver Danny Davis III (7) drops a pass against Notre Dame Fighting Irish cornerback Clarence Lewis (6) during their football game Saturday, September 25, 2021, at Soldier Field in Chicago, Ill. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect Contrary to popular belief, Notre Dame and Wisconsin will not battle for a rivalry trophy in the likeness of Jack Coan or Barry Alvarez this Sunday night, but will play in one of football's greatest venues - Lambeau Field in Green Bay. It's the second time these two have met in a Shamrock Series game, the first coming in 2021 at Soldier Field in Chicago, when Notre Dame rattled off 31 straight fourth-quarter points to beat the Badgers, 41-13. While that was fun, Sunday promises to be its own chapter as both teams start seasons they hope will define their head coaches careers. For Notre Dame, it's about finally getting over the final hurdle and knocking down the national championship door for the first time since 1988, while for Wisconsin, the growing pains are supposed to be over and a friendlier schedule should allow the Badgers to take a step back in the right direction under Luke Fickell With those storylines in mind, here are a few game notes courtesy of the great folks in both the Notre Dame and Wisconsin sports information departments. Notre Dame vs Wisconsin - All-Time Series History Sunday night will be the 18th all-time meeting between Notre Dame and Wisconsin. The Fighting Irish hold a slight edge, 9-6-2. Notre Dame won the last two meetings, including the 2021 matchup at Soldier Field, 41-13. The meeting previous to that was all the way back in 1964 when Notre Dame routed the Badgers 31-7 at Camp Randall, in Ara Parseghian's first game as head coach. Notre Dame-Wisconsin Coaching Connections Marcus Freeman was Luke Fickell's DC at Cincinnati. The Wisconsin head coach was asked about the Notre Dame coach leading up to their big Week 1 matchup at Lambeau Field. pic.twitter.com/9dG9vBpo2G â Big Ten Football (@B1Gfootball) August 31, 2026 Notre Dame head coach Marcus Freeman was the defensive coordinator on Luke Fickell's staff at Cincinnati before departing for Notre Dame in 2021. Also on that Cincinnati staff were offensive coordinator Mike Denbrock, quarterbacks coach Gino Guidugli, and wide receivers coach Mike Brown. Notre Dame Coaches Who Coached and/or Played at Wisconsin A few more Notre Dame assistants called Wisconsin home in different ways previously. Chris Ash was previously a defensive coordinator for the Badgers while offensive line coach Joe Rudolph held the same position at Wisconsin after starring on its 1994 team that went to the Rose Bowl. Finally, defensive backs coach Aaron Henry was a two-time All Big Ten selection for the Badgers. Notre Dame All-Time vs Big Ten Opponents Sunday will be Notre Dame's 512 all-time game against a Big Ten opponent. It has gone 319-170-22 in the previous 511 and 19-9-3 against Big Ten schools on neutral fields. Wisconsin's Return to Lambeau Field Despite the rich history of the Green Bay Packers, the Badgers don't have much of a history at Lambeau Field. Wisconsin has played just one game there previously, upsetting No. 5 LSU to open the 2016 season, in which Wisconsin would go on to win the Cotton Bowl. New Look Badgers for 2026 Part of the reason for hope for Wisconsin in 2026 after a disappointing 2025 is because of how active the team was in the transfer portal. Wisconsin added 34 players via the portal, the third most of any team in the Big Ten. Former Sun Belt Star QBs Badgers The most important of those 34 players is quarterback Colton Joseph, who comes to Wisconsin after winning the Sun Belt's Offensive Player of the Year award. He threw for over 2,000 yards while rushing for more than 1,000 in 2025. Easier 2025 Outlook for Wisconsin? Wisconsin should get some schedule relief by default in 2026 after facing 10 teams that qualified for bowl games last year. Fixing Wisconsin's Offensive Woes A season ago, Wisconsin's offense was putrid, reaching the 20-point mark just twice all year. Once in a 42-10 rout of Middle Tennessee State, and the other in a 27-10 victory over Illinois. CJ Carr Leads Notre Dame Offense In honor of Childhood Cancer Awareness Month, we remember Chad Carr and the laughter and happiness he brought into the world.ðï¸ @13Cjcarr @ND_HCTI pic.twitter.com/PhHuVrup0k â Notre Dame Football (@NDFootball) September 1, 2026 Notre Dame quarterback CJ Carr enters the year as a Heisman Trophy favorite. His 9.35 yards per pass attempt were second in the nation last season, while his 14.06 yards per completion were fourth best. Notre Dame's Preseason Hype Notre Dame's No. 4 ranking in the preseason AP Poll is the highest Notre Dame has been ranked to start a year since being No. 2 in 2006. Meanwhile, this is the third-straight season Wisconsin has begun the year unranked. Notre Dame's Dominating Close to 2025 Notre Dame won its last 10 games of the 2025 season after starting the year 0-2. It's the first time in over 100 years that a Notre Dame team has won 10 straight games all by 10 or more points (1921 into 1922). Notre Dame's Middle Eight Domination Coaches often talk about the middle eight of a game and how important it is to control the final four minutes before halftime as well as the first four minutes out of the break. Marcus Freeman has discussed this from jump street and his team has followed, outscoring teams 403-117, a +286 margin and average difference of +5.3 points per game since he was named head coach. Nick Shepkowski's Quick Thoughts Some of these numbers matter in regards to what will happen Sunday night while others are nothing more than fun to look at from a historical context. What I was reminded of when going through the game notes for both teams was that too much time spent on any team site will quickly have you thinking 12-0 is a guarantee and that anything short of a trip to the national semifinal will be a disappointment. In the case of Notre Dame in 2026 though, anything less than that should be considered a major malfunction. Add us as a preferred source on Google Follow Loading recommendations... Please wait while we load personalized content recommendations Published 45 minutes ago | Modified 40 minutes ago NICK SHEPKOWSKI Managing Editor for Notre Dame On SI. Started covering Chicago sports teams for WSCR the Score, and over the years worked with CBS Radio, Audacy, NBC Sports, and FOX Sports as a contributor before running the Notre Dame wire site for USA TODAY. articles.body: Fantasy Football Draft Rankings: 2026 QB Tiers (UPDATED) | RotoWire Fantasy Football Draft Rankings: 2026 Quarterback Tiers (UPDATED) Ian Hartitz offers his quarterback tiers for the 2026 fantasy football season and analyzes which QBs to target in fantasy drafts. Check out his updated list. September 1, 2026 Share By: Ian Hartitz @Ihartitz September 1, 2026 Fantasy Football Draft Strategy Mock Draft Simulator Prep for your 2026 Fantasy Football draft with free, unlimited drafts, and real-time grades. This is an updated version of the Quarterback Tiers article that ran earlier this month. Training camp, injuries and the draft market changed fantasy outlooks the last few weeks. So, we're back with an updated list of Quarterback Tiers to guide users in late-summer drafts. Rankings are cool and all, but as any fellow fantasy nerd knows: Tier-based drafting is really where it's at. This is because — get this — sometimes us alleged fantasy experts can be wrong, so it's best to embrace this horrifying reality by grouping similarly ranked players into tiers instead of pretending like we're going to get every single individual ranking correct. Cool? Cool: What follows are my preseason QB tiers along with some quick fun facts as well as one bigger picture question for each individual tier As always: It's a great day to be great. Reminder: You can check out all of Ian's rankings and content with a premium RotoWire subscription Use code "Ian35" for 35% off Tier 1: The Undisputed King of Fantasy QB1 Josh Allen consensus ADP QB1): The all-time leader in QB career fantasy points per game hasn't finished any worse than QB2 since 2020. Question: Has Josh Allen paid off his early-round price tag in the past? Usually! We can get a good idea of this by looking at how often Allen has appeared on ESPN playoff rosters over the years: 2020: 50% (3rd among QBs, ADP QB10-82) 2021: 49% (2nd, ADP QB2-26) 2022: 58.6% This is an updated version of the Quarterback Tiers article that ran earlier this month. Training camp, injuries and the draft market changed fantasy outlooks the last few weeks. So, we're back with an updated list of Quarterback Tiers to guide users in late-summer drafts. Rankings are cool and all, but as any fellow fantasy nerd knows: Tier-based drafting is really where it's at. This is because — get this — sometimes us alleged fantasy experts can be wrong, so it's best to embrace this horrifying reality by grouping similarly ranked players into tiers instead of pretending like we're going to get every single individual ranking correct. Cool? Cool: What follows are my preseason QB tiers along with some quick fun facts as well as one bigger picture question for each individual tier As always: It's a great day to be great. Reminder: You can check out all of Ian's rankings and content with a premium RotoWire subscription Use code "Ian35" for 35% off Tier 1: The Undisputed King of Fantasy QB1 Josh Allen consensus ADP QB1): The all-time leader in QB career fantasy points per game hasn't finished any worse than QB2 since 2020. Question: Has Josh Allen paid off his early-round price tag in the past? Usually! We can get a good idea of this by looking at how often Allen has appeared on ESPN playoff rosters over the years: 2020: 50% (3rd among QBs, ADP QB10-82) 2021: 49% (2nd, ADP QB2-26) 2022: 58.6% (3rd, ADP QB1-21) 2023: 62.1% (1st, ADP QB2-20) 2024: 58.2% (2nd, ADP QB1-23) 2025: 57.5% (1st, ADP QB1-23) That's a pretty great hit rate for a consistent Round 2-3 turn pick! And hey: It makes sense. That range of the draft usually consists of preseason RB2s and WR2s who could certainly work out (see: Smith-Njigba, Jaxon ), but there's usually at least some reason for pause when looking at their profiles — not so much with Allen. Here's the thing about Josh Allen 's fantasy production: The Bills spam the tush push on the goal line as much as anyone outside of Philadelphia . And get this, they've actually posted a higher conversion rate of tush pushes (83.1% vs. 73.2%) than the Eagles the last two seasons. The impact in fantasy land can't be overstated: Jalen Hurts (97.6) and Allen (73.2) are the only two quarterbacks with even 30 fantasy points from rushes at the 1-yard line in this span. It's a weapon in their fantasy toolbelt that simply isn't available to anyone else at the position. Josh Allen is a boat and the other Round 3 picks are mystery boxes. Sometimes you should just take the boat. For up-to-the-minute updates on injuries, news and everything going on around the NFL, head to RotoWire's NFL Fantasy Football News Today or follow @RotoWireNFL on X. Tier 2: Overall QB1 Upside is on the Table QB2 Lamar Jackson (ADP QB2): Responsible for two (2019, 2024) of the position's top-6 all-time best seasons in fantasy points per game. QB3 Drake Maye (ADP QB3): Led the NFL in essentially every meaningful passing efficiency metric last season and now gets to play with a new-and-improved wide receiver room. QB4 Jayden Daniels (ADP QB5): Joined Cam Newton, Justin Herbert , and Robert Griffin as the only rookie QBs to average north of 20 fantasy points per game. QB5 Jalen Hurts (ADP QB6): 2025 (18.7) was the first season as a starter that Hurts failed to average at least 20 fantasy points per game. QB6 Joe Burrow (ADP QB4): Averaged an elite 21.9 fantasy points per game each of the last two seasons that he's been fully healthy (2022, 2024). Question: How important has rushing upside been to posting elite fantasy numbers? We'll define elite as 20-plus fantasy points per game, something that has happened 59 times in the last decade. Among this group of top-scoring signal-callers ... 19 (32%) cleared triple-digit carries in a season. More intriguingly, half of the top-20 overall scores featured QBs with 100-plus rush attempts. A little more than half (51%) averaged 4.5 rush attempts per game, good for a 17-game average of 77 carries. Only nine (15%) ran for less than 100 yards in a season. This group was exclusively made up of more elderly pocket passers — Tom Brady, Ben Roethlisberger, Drew Brees, and Matthew Stafford A quick look at the QB rush attempt leaderboard from RotoWire Projections reveals Jayden Daniels (128), Lamar Jackson (120) and Jalen Hurts (114) are expected to work as the league's most run-heavy quarterbacks in 2026. Note that the Eagles didn't run fewer tush pushes at the goal line overall last season; the problem was their offense simply got to the one-yard line less often than in past years Stay informed with fantasy football news and track usage roles with the NFL depth charts Tier 3: Great Real-Life QBs with Sky-High Fantasy Ceilings QB7 Justin Herbert (ADP QB9): Proven 22-plus fantasy point upside; Herbert could find himself in a VASTLY superior offensive environment thanks to a healthy offensive line and the addition of OC Mike McDaniel. QB8 Caleb Williams (ADP QB7): The NFL's fastest QB was the QB7 in fantasy points per game in year one with coach Ben Johnson. What if Caleb starts hitting his layups? QB9 Trevor Lawrence (ADP QB11): Nobody scored more fantasy points per game in Weeks 10-18 (23), but we probably shouldn't expect nine rushing touchdowns again. QB10 Brock Purdy (ADP QB13): QB11, QB7, QB13 and most recently QB4 in fantasy points per game — here's to hoping Purdy's various elderly playmakers can stay healthy. QB11 Dak Prescott (ADP QB10): The NFC's version of Joe Burrow . Nobody should be surprised if the Cowboys lead the NFL in scoring. Question: Are the high-end QB1s cheaper than ever in fantasy land? Josh Allen is still being priced like Josh Allen , but the rest of QB2-8 options are largely much more affordable than in past years. This is also contributing to the QB9-plus range going earlier in drafts than ever. Of course, this raises the question: Is the newfound pricing structure at QB warranted? Have we seen the upper-middle class of the position struggle to outpace the QB2 range in recent years? Answer: Not really. The difference in fantasy points per game between the QB6 and QB12 (2.2 points) in 2025 was right in line with what we saw from 2021-2024. The QB1 vs. QB6 (1.8) and QB12 vs. QB18 (1.5) differences were lower than usual in 2025, but it hasn't been a steady trend. All that said, if I had to put a single chip down on one of the involved options (at cost), it would be Mr. Justin Herbert . The 28-year-old just ran for a career-high 498 yards while navigating behind a hellaciously banged-up offensive line, something that should be rectified with the returns of Rashawn Slater and Joe Alt in 2026. Throw in the newfound presence of wizard Mike McDaniel, who has continued the Shanahan way of making more with less at QB, and it sure feels like a massive MVP-level breakout could be on the way. Use the fantasy football draft assistant to get custom rankings for your league and follow along with a live draft on most major platforms. Tier 4: Wait at QB and you can still get these guys! QB12 Jaxson Dart (ADP QB8): Only Josh Allen scored more fantasy points from rushing last season, but can Dart overcome an underwhelming group of pass-catchers and Matt Nagy's scheme? QB13 Bo Nix (ADP QB15): QB8 and QB11 fantasy finishes to start his career despite very underwhelming passing efficiency metrics. Hopefully Nix's recovery from his fourth (!) career ankle/foot surgery goes smoothly and the offense benefits from the newfound presence of Jaylen Waddle QB14 Jared Goff (ADP QB16): Leads the NFL in passing touchdowns since 2022. Goff has ripped off three consecutive seasons with at least 4,500 passing yards. The rest of the NFL has *six* combined QB15 Matthew Stafford (ADP QB14): At the risk of being the boy who cried regression: All 23 QBs to post a touchdown rate of at least 7 percent saw their mark fall the following season. Stafford's was 7.7 percent last season. QB16 Patrick Mahomes (ADP QB12): Renewed fantasy excellence in 2025 was almost entirely just thanks to career-high rushing numbers , which we probably shouldn't expect to persist coming off a torn ACL. Question: Is the idea that pocket passers don't possess a ton of fantasy upside true? On the one hand, our previous study showed that many of the top-performing QBs from the past decade possessed at least some level of rushing upside. On the other hand, a look at the leaderboard for most top-5 weekly finishes during the last two seasons sure seems to reveal that some of the league's pocket-passing uncs still got it. Most Top-5 Weekly Fantasy Finishes Among QBs 2024-25: Lamar Jackson - 12 Josh Allen - 11 Jalen Hurts - 10 Joe Burrow - 9 Jared Goff - 8 Matthew Stafford - 8 Patrick Mahomes - 8 Baker Mayfield - 8 Caleb Williams - 8 While history tells us both QBs could see their quality touchdown rates regress, we're also looking at two loaded offenses that have earned the benefit of the doubt the last decade. All things considered: having true late-round options like this and our next tier make me VERY intrigued with waiting as long as possible to get a QB in re-draft land this year. Tier 6: Run Forest Run! QB17 Kyler Murray (ADP QB20): Last season, Murray actually averaged his most rushing yards per game (34.6) since his ACL injury. This is still a dangerous man in the open field QB18 Malik Willis (ADP QB21): Everyone knows Willis can run, but get this: small-sample size be damned, Willis leads the NFL in EPA per dropback and completion percentage over expected the last two seasons. Question: How good have high-volume dual-threat QBs been in fantasy land? Pretty, pretty, pretty good. In fact, of 28 QBs with at least 100 rush attempts, 26 (93%!) managed to post top-12 fantasy numbers on a per-game basis. Notice that last part? Per game! articles.title: Is Devaughn Vele worth adding in fantasy football before Week 1?
articles.excerpt: Alex Hunter analyzes the fantasy value of Saints' wide receiver Devaughn Vele heading into the 2026-27 NFL season. The post Is Devaughn Vele worth adding in fantasy football before Week 1? appeared first on DraftKings Network .
articles.source_type: Captain picks ranked with reasoning, gameweek rankings, DFS targets
articles.body: Is Devaughn Vele worth adding in fantasy football before Week 1? With first-round pick Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) on IR and missing at the least first four games of the season, Devaughn Vele is likely to serve as the Saints’ No. 2 receiver behind Chris Olave to begin the year. Vele is widely available in most fantasy football leagues, but should we be considering him as a potential add with the season quickly approaching? Devaughn Vele Fantasy Outlook A shoulder injury forced Vele to miss the final three games of last season, but prior to this, he and quarterback Tyler Shough were starting to build a solid connection. In Vele’s final five games of the season, the 6-foot-5 receiver saw a target on 16% of his routes, running a route on 84% of Shough’s dropbacks. This route rate ranked second only to Chris Olave for the Saints during this span. Vele garnered some valuable targets, seeing five targets over 20 yards and two red-zone targets. For fantasy purposes, Vele had two strong performances during this five-game run, going off for 23.3 FPTS vs. the Dolphins and posting 11.9 FPTS vs. the Panthers in the game in which he got injured. But he scored single-digit points in the three other games. Devaughn Vele got 🆙 pic.twitter.com/R4Ze4Nf9KO — NFL (@NFL) December 14, 2025 With Tyson sidelined for the first month of the season and possibly more – he has suffered four hamstring injuries since the start of 2025 – Vele should run a route on most of Shough’s dropbacks and command targets at a solid rate. After a great ending to his rookie season, Shough is a candidate to improve in his second season and Vele certainly could be one of the main beneficiaries. Especially in the first two games of the season, when the Saints visit the Lions and the Ravens, New Orleans may be forced to air it out as underdogs. Vele could be busy. Given Vele only scored 0.15 FPTS per snap last season and we only have about 4.5 games of he and Shough playing together, our expectations do need to be tempered. Still, Vele averaging close to double-digit FPTS per game until Tyson returns is a possibility, so picking Vele up is a viable move if your roster is thin at receiver. articles.title: Georgia Bulldogs CFB Win Total & SEC Prediction, Pick
articles.excerpt: A breakdown of the Georgia Bulldogs win total and SEC odds ahead of the 2026 college football season. The post Georgia Bulldogs CFB Win Total & SEC Prediction, Pick appeared first on DraftKings Network .
articles.source_type: Captain picks ranked with reasoning, gameweek rankings, DFS targets
articles.body: Georgia Bulldogs CFB Win Total & SEC Prediction, Pick The Georgia Bulldogs enter the 2026 season as the favorites in the SEC, and with good reason. While the conference is always tough, Kirby Smart has molded the Dawgs into the model of consistency, particularly since Nick Saban departed Alabama. Georgia has won both SEC Championship Games since Saban retired, and three of the last four overall — with the lone loss to ‘Bama in Saban’s final season. Since the 2020 Covid season, UGA has won double digit regular season games in each of the last five seasons. It appears unlikely that streak ends in 2026. Let’s breakdown some futures on the Bulldogs below. Georgia Bulldogs Win Total & SEC Predictions Georgia was riding a 33-game home winning streak into last season’s matchup with Alabama, who went to Athens and ended one of the more impressive runs in college football. Nonetheless, UGA has an absurd 53-2 record at home since 2017. The loss to ‘Bama was the only loss for UGA in the regular season in 2025, finishing with an 11-1 record. The Bulldogs got revenge on the Tide in a dominant SEC title game, but lost their College Football Playoff game coming off the bye for the second straight year — to Ole Miss in 2025 and Notre Dame in 2024. UGA lost road games to Ole Miss and ‘Bama in that 2024 season, going 10-2 in the regular season — but went on to defeat Texas as an underdog in the SEC Championship. Prior to that, Georgia went a perfect 12-0 in the regular season in 2023, 2022 and 2021. Simply put, this program is machine-like. If the five-year sample of dominance isn’t enough for you, removing the shortened 2020 season, UGA went 11-1 in each of the three previous seasons of 2019, 2018 and 2017. The only time Kirby Smart has coached Georgia in a full 12-game season and not won 10 or more games was in his first season at the helm in 2016. That’s eight consecutive 12-game seasons of at least 10 wins — four of them with 11 wins and three of them with a perfect 12 wins. So the question becomes, has this Georgia team dropped off enough to end that streak and win fewer than 10 games? The Bulldogs lost some talent to the NFL as they always do, but return plenty. A total of 14 starters return from 2025, and Smart consistently retains his own recruits, as one of Phil Steele’s highest-ranked homegrown talent rosters. Gunner Stockton returns for his second full season as QB1, along with an extremely experienced offensive line and a loaded running back room, headlined by Nate Frazier. The tight end room is also deep with talent, starting with the senior Lawson Luckie. If we can point to any weakness on the offense, it’s the wide receiver room, but the Dawgs did bring in Isiah Canion from Georgia Tech and Talyn Taylor as a talented freshman. The defensive side of the ball just seems to reload at Georgia. Constantly one of the nastiest defenses in the country, the Bulldogs have a strong secondary and plenty of pass rushers. UGA struggled generating sacks last season, but managed to get by because of the rest of the talent. Smart added some transfers there, and the rest of the unit is a year more experienced. Phil Steele ranks Georgia No. 3 overall in the nation, and in the top-10 in nearly all of his position rankings. Steele has the Dawgs ranked the following at each position nationally: QB (4), RB (6), WR (35), OL (7), DL (9), LB (5), DB (3). Athlon ranks Georgia No. 2 overall in the nation, and top-three at every position in the SEC, outside of WR. It also ranks UGA atop the position rankings in the SEC at OL, LB and DB. Nationally, Athlon ranks UGA’s positions as QB (7), RB (2), OL (2), DL (8), LB (1) and DB (6). Lindy’s might be the lowest on Georgia, still ranking them No. 6 in the country. But other than the WR position, Lindy’s still puts the Bulldogs as a top-10 unit at every single other position. Pick Six Previews has Georgia ranked a top-two unit in the SEC at every position but RB (4) and WR/TE combined (9). Long story short, this team is loaded, and that’s why Georgia is a favorite in all 12 games this season. I mentioned the insane 53-2 record at home, dating back to 2017, and UGA will benefit from only playing four road games on the schedule. The Bulldogs have seven true home games, and the usual “neutral” game against Florida happens to be played in Atlanta this season — on UGA’s other home turf. Georgia is currently -10 against Oklahoma in the DraftKings Game of the Year line in Week 4 , meaning it checks in as a double digit favorite in all eight of those home games. The Dawgs should also be double digit road favorites when they visit Arkansas and South Carolina during SEC play. Basically, if UGA can avoid a loss as a double digit favorite, they reach the 10-win mark. However, I think they can do even better than that. Georgia’s two toughest tasks of the season come when its priced as a -3 favorite at Alabama on October 10 and a -4.5 favorite at Ole Miss on November 7. Both of those games set up as terrific revenge spots, specifically at Ole Miss. While UGA got the last laugh against Alabama in the SEC Championship in December, the Bulldogs will still be looking to get ‘Bama back for snapping that 33-game winning streak in Athens last year. And Ole Miss just so happens to be the team that bounced UGA from the CFP in January, so you know Smart has that one circled. Georgia is in tremendous position to do what it does each and every season — win 10-plus games. Both the talent on the roster and the schedule set up ideally to do so. That will put the Bulldogs in the SEC Championship Game in December in Atlanta, where I’d favor them against anyone in the conference. It’s been one-way money on UGA’s win total so far this summer, with a 99% ticket count and handle on OVER 9.5. That’s a little concerning, but I think bettors are simply identifying that 9.5 is always a play on this team, and that 10.5 is probably the more reasonable number. It’s not like the Bulldogs are being overhyped by the public, as they only have a 12% ticket count to win the SEC and 10% of the bets to win the National Championship (splits as of August 1). My two favorite college football futures for the 2026 season are calling for Georgia to go over their win total and win yet another SEC Championship. Win Total Pick: Georgia OVER 9.5 (-180) SEC Championship Game Pick: Georgia (+280) For more analysis check out our College Football homepage on DraftKings Network. FPL GW3 Wildcard Guide Pros & Cons of Wildcarding in FPL GW3: Pros of GW3 Wildcard: Projections from Fantasy Football Hub Get Haaland in ahead of COV(H) and long term if you started with No Haaland in GW1. Attack Teams with Good Fixture runs and have cheap assets like Newcastle(Wissa, Elanga, Hall, Dedic) and Brighton(De Cuyper, Verbruggen, Gross) Catch good price changes(Eg. Konsa) who might be a starter now or even later at just 4.4 million. Cons of GW3 Wildcard: Chelsea and Arsenal play each other and it will be a really difficult match to call with respect to Goals and Clean sheets. You will want to have Double Arsenal defense and Double Chelsea attack long term but it will be a trickier call to take in GW3 on who to bench/start. You will be up against managers who are likely to have Haaland as Triple Captain vs COV(H). You can’t use more than one chip in a single Gameweek. Wildcard might be needed later for other fixture swings- Like GW6 or around GW15 as highlighted in our Chip Strategy article. Bruno or No-Bruno, Palmer or No Palmer will be a tough decision to make. Bruno has had an absolute massive 23 point in GW2 vs Ipswich courtesy 3 Goals, 1 Assist. But there is an argument that can be made to not captain Bruno Fernandes in the next 5-6 weeks and switch between Palmer and Haaland. No Bruno- Captaincy Ticker: GW3- Haaland vs COV(H) GW4- Palmer vs HUL(H) GW5- Haaland vs SUN(H) GW6- Palmer vs BOU(H) GW7- Haaland vs IPS(H) GW8- Haaland vs AVL(A)/Palmer vs TOT(H) The other alternative is to wait out a week and Wildcard in GW4 after Chelsea and Arsenal have played each other. Here are some of the Pros of a GW3 Wildcard vs Pros of a GW4 Wildcard. GW3 Wildcard vs GW4 Wildcard: GW3 Wildcard GW4 Wildcard Helps you target Manchester City assets ahead of COV(H). Works better in case of no Haaland in GW1 Helps you skip the Chelsea vs Arsenal fixture in GW3 and target them full-fledged in GW4 on Wildcard. Triple up on both Chelsea(Attack) and Arsenal(Likely defense) without them facing each other. Goal Keeper and Defenders: Verbruggen is the Budget GK with a good run of fixtures. Calafiori picks himself with 2 assists and 2 clean sheets and is the next nailed defender in the Arsenal lineup after Gabriel. He is also 2.5 million cheaper than Gabriel, which makes him an easy lock. Konsa is the second Arsenal defender. At just 4.4 million, you have to take up that risk to get an Arsenal defender. He should be first choice in the long term and can play both CB and RB. With Mosquera injured(Watch out for PC updates), He could be in for a start as soon as GW3. Ajer and Hall are two of the total 4 defenders who have hit DEFCON in both games. Ajer is always good for DEFCON when he plays at CB, and Hall also carries an excellent attacking threat(with a good run of fixtures from GW4). Brentford and Newcastle defenders also rotate really well, as seen below. Dedic is also looking really good with 🅰️🅰️🅰️ in 3 games. And just for £4.5. Livramento is back in training, though, but according to Newcastle fans, Livra doesn’t walk in directly, and Dedic is likely to keep starting games at least in the short-medium run. Midfielders: Palmer is an easy lock in most of the GW3 Wildcard Drafts(unless on GW4 Free Hit). Chelsea Bruno Fernandes is coming on the back of 23 points haul courtesy of 3 goals and an assist in GW2 vs Ipswich. He is in red-hot form and has multiple routes to points. Pascal Gross and Szoboszlai are midfielders who have multiple routes to points- penalties, Set Pieces, and DEFCON. On top of it, they also have a good fixture run. Slater is the 4.5 Midfielder enabler in this draft who is a starter for Hull and is also on set pieces. Forwards: Haaland and Joao Pedro pick themselves in every Wildcard Draft. Wissa also should be a lock according to me, as Newcastle have a good run of fixtures playing HUL(H), COV(A) in GW5 and GW6. Calvert-Lewin is also another option to consider if you want a set-and-forget option. Isak is a good shout with good fixtures in GW3 and GW4, but it is a difficult price point to swap later on, and he hasn’t shown much to warrant a gamble. articles.body: Chelsea agree Camara deal following Fernandez departure Skip to content Football News Premier League News Chelsea agree Camara deal following Fernandez departure Nicholas McGee Last Update: 1 hour ago 1 min read Add us as a preferred source on Google Chelsea have agreed a deal in principle to sign Senegal midfielder Lamine Camara from Monaco following the departure of Enzo Fernandez. The Blues earlier on deadline day agreed to part with Argentina international Fernandez, who is set to complete a move to Manchester City for a British record-tying fee of £125million It had been though that Chelsea would be unable to source a replacement, with Monaco reported to have rejected two offers for Camara and Roma boss Gian Piero Gasperini said to have blocked France international Manu Kone from leaving the Stadio Olimpico. But, with under two hours left in the transfer window, Fabrizio Romano reported Chelsea have come to terms on a €55million (£47m) deal for Camara, who has been given permission to undergo a medical. Camara will reportedly sign a contract until 2032 with the option for an additional year. The 22-year-old has made 73 appearances, with 66 starts, for Monaco since joining from Metz in 2024. He has won 49 caps for Senegal, scoring seven goals, and played in all four of the Lions of Teranga’s games at the 2026 World Cup as they exited the tournament in the round of 32. Preseason Trend No. 1: The Mike McDaniel Impact is REAL in Los Angeles Mike McDaniel's ability to largely get the most out of Tua Tagovailoa and the Dolphins over the years has made him a bit of a rock star in the play-caller streets. One of his key schematic principles was the use of pre-snap shift/motion as well as play-action: He easily ranked first in both of these metrics during the 2022-2025 seasons . The other teams near the top of the leaderboard ( Lions Rams 49ers Packers Chiefs ) reflect the reality that offenses consistently clicking these "easy buttons" are among the most well-schemed groups in the league. Well, at least based on our three preseason data points, it sure looks like McDaniel's Los Angeles hasn't fallen far from the tree. This is true for pre-snap shift/motion 2025 Chargers: 64.3 percent motion - 18th 2026 preseason: 83.8 percent - 1st … as well as play-action rate 2025 Chargers: 25.1 percent - 17th 2026 preseason: 36.6 percent - 2nd Hell, we also saw McDaniel REALLY lean into outside size (56.1%, 1st) relative to what the Chargers did last season (17.6%, 29th), and Los Angeles also emerged as a leader in multi-TE formations (37.1%, 4th) just one year removed from ranking 31st in percentage of plays with two or more tight ends on the field. Now, none of this is guaranteed to produce a juggernaut offense — especially if the offensive line (again) struggles to overcome injuries — but hey, it's certainly a good start! I'm holding firm on my bold prediction that the Chargers finish as the league's No. 1 scoring offense this season, and have accordingly loaded up on their fantasy-relevant talents of most shapes and sizes throughout draft season. Last in the league by a whopping 7.5 percentage points. Not great! The Commanders only had a 20.6 percent play-action rate (24th). Here's to hoping Jayden Daniels is ready to put his Superman cape on — he's going to need to shoulder plenty of the load here for this offense to re-reach 2024 heights if the preseason is any indication of what we should expect from this offensive line and scheme. The Bengals' offense has obviously been nothing short of awesome with a healthy Joe Burrow over the years, but there has been a rather startling lack of play-action usage. Consider: The Bengals rank 31st in play-action rate (19.5%) since drafting Burrow first overall in 2020, and they were last in 2025 (17.2%). But then something funny happened this preseason: coach Zac Taylor had the boys embracing some play action for once! Overall, the Bengals' 34.9 percent play-action rate was good for fourth highest in the preseason … though we did see them also post a top-5 mark last August (28.7%, 5th). articles.body: Who Should I Draft: Travis Etienne vs Cam Skattebo | RotoWire Who Should I Draft: Travis Etienne vs. Cam Skattebo (2026 Fantasy Football) Should you draft Travis Etienne or Cam Skattebo? Projections are tight but I really like the upside of Skattebo and here's why. Updated on September 1, 2026 4:23PM EST Share By: Tyler Huntington @tylerhuntington Updated on September 1, 2026 4:23PM EST Who Should I Draft? Mock Draft Simulator Prep for your 2026 Fantasy Football draft with free, unlimited drafts, and real-time grades. Two backs, projected within three points of each other, going within a couple picks of each other in the fourth round of most fantasy football drafts. This is as even as the widget gets - Etienne at 203 half-PPR points, Skattebo at 206 - so the tiebreakers are the whole story, and they point somewhere the projection total doesn't. All half-PPR below. The scoring section matters a little here, because one of these guys catches meaningfully more passes. Travis Etienne Fantasy Outlook vs ADP: RB19 Etienne is the steady vet in this pair, and the projection reflects a real workhorse role: 203 half-PPR points on 226 carries for 1070 yards and seven scores. He even holds a razor-thin edge in total projection and floor, so if your instinct is 'give me the established guy with the known workload,' Etienne rewards it. Alvin Kamara is already expected to miss time in 2026 so the newest New Orleans Saint is locked and loaded for a full time role. The issue is what happens above the median. His 249 point ceiling is nearly 40 points below Skattebo's, because his profile is volume-forward and grounded - lots of carries, modest passing-game work (34 catches), not a lot of week-winning spike. He's a solid RB2 whose best weeks look like everyone else's good weeks. In a vacuum that's a perfectly good pick. Very close floor projection, but it isn't an edge - it's noise, and it's the only row Etienne clearly wins, aside from ADP. Very close floor projection, but it isn't an edge - it's noise, and it's the only row Etienne clearly wins, aside from ADP. Bottom Line: A dead-even projection with a workhorse's carry count, but the lower ceiling and less receiving juice. The safe half of a coin flip. Cam Skattebo Fantasy Outlook vs ADP: RB18 Skattebo is coming off a brutal leg injury, and normally I'm the one waving people off the guys that are riddled with injury histories - but the numbers here earn it. Same projection as Etienne to within a rounding error, and a ceiling of 288 that towers nearly 40 points above him. That gap is built on passing-game work and big plays. Pass-catching backs carry the highest ceilings in fantasy because the receptions stack on top of the rushing floor, and in a modern offense that usage is exactly what turns a fine RB2 into a league-winner. The tool hands Skattebo the coin-flip edge on that ceiling, and he's going a hair earlier than Etienne to boot. He's a risk, and the week-to-week can wobble. But the receiving role is the tell, and it's pointing up. Bottom Line: The same projection with a 40-point-higher ceiling and more pass-game work. The tie-breaking upside is real. Travis Etienne vs Cam Skattebo: The Verdict The tool below has these two in a dead heat on projection - scroll to the ceiling and receiving rows to see what breaks the tie. The tool calls it a coin flip and gives Skattebo the nod on ceiling, and I'm coming down the same way: Skattebo is my pick. When two backs project dead even, I take the one with the pass-catching role, because those catches are both the safer floor and the higher ceiling - it's the profile that wins you a week and rarely craters. Etienne is the pick if you'd rather have the vet's known workload and you're allergic to variance, and I understand the impulse at an even projection. But 'even projection, way higher ceiling, more receptions, going a touch earlier' is four boxes, and Skattebo checks the ones that decide close calls. What flips me: a training-camp signal that Skattebo's receiving role is smaller than projected. Strip the pass-game edge and this reverts to the vet. As long as those targets are real, take the ceiling. Best Ceiling: Cam Skattebo - 295.8, nearly 60 points clear Best Floor: Travis Etienne - by a hair, part of a near-tie Receiving Edge: Cam Skattebo Most Proven Workload: Travis Etienne My Pick: Cam Skattebo Travis Etienne or Cam Skattebo PPR Scoring Skattebo's receiving edge means full PPR widens his lead and makes this pick more comfortable. Standard scoring strips the reception points and pulls the two nearly even on their almost-identical rushing lines - close enough that Etienne's proven role becomes a fair tiebreak. So: Skattebo in half and full PPR. In a standard league, it's a genuine coin flip and I wouldn't argue with the vet. Fantasy Football Tools Everything you need to dominate your draft, in one place. articles.body: 'I know this is the perfect fit' - Ndiaye completes £65m move to Man City Skip to content Football News Premier League News ‘I know this is the perfect fit’ – Ndiaye completes £65m move to Man City City have swelled their attacking ranks on deadline day. Nicholas McGee Last Update: 36 minutes ago 2 min read Add us as a preferred source on Google Manchester City have completed the signing of Senegal winger Iliman Ndiaye from Everton Ndiaye has made the move to the Etihad Stadium on a five-year deal after City agreed a £65million with the Merseyside club. The 26-year-old was at one point set to join Tottenham, with Spurs striker Richarlison going the other way. But City swooped in after that transfer fell through, with Ndiaye delighted to have the chance to prove himself for Enzo Maresca’s side after excelling in his time with Everton. “I’ve worked my whole life for an opportunity like this,” he told City’s official website “City are one of the best clubs in the world and I’ve seen them win everything as I’ve grown up. “To be able to write my own chapter in a story that special is the chance of a lifetime and I’m determined to grab it with both hands. “It’s not always been easy in my career, but I always had the belief that I could play for a team challenging for the biggest prizes and now I’m here. It feels so good. “I love to play with the ball on the floor in an attacking team that wants to score as many goals as possible. That’s why I know this is the perfect fit. “City fans can rest assured that I will give my all to bring more success to this incredible club.” Ndiaye scored 17 goals and provided four assists for Everton after joining from Marseille in 2024. He could make his debut when City host Coventry City this weekend, having won each of their opening two games. Topics Everton F.C. Manchester City F.C. articles.body: Chicago White Sox vs. Houston Astros prediction, pick for Tuesday 9/1/26 We’ve officially passed the end of August and are into September, meaning the MLB’s postseason race is coming down to the wire. The American League is much less competitive than usual this year, but division leaders are division leaders. Tonight, the Houston Astros face the Chicago White Sox again after opening this series with a win at Daikin Park last night. First pitch on Tuesday is set for 8:10 p.m. ET. Let’s dive in with a preview, prediction and pick for tonight’s White Sox vs. Astros game courtesy of odds and lines on DraftKings Sportsbook. White Sox vs. Astros prediction, preview The White Sox are atop the AL Central as they’ve been for much of the season, sitting 72-65 on the year with a +41 run differential. They’ve dropped two straight games now, but remain 6-4 over their last 10; a 31-38 away record isn’t great, though. The Astros are hardly above .500 at 70-68, but it’s enough to protect a slim AL West lead even despite a -40 differential on the year. They’re also 34-25 at home this season. RHP Sean Burke (7-6) starts for Chicago this evening. He’s been one of this club’s best arms, amassing a 3.32 ERA and a 1.15 WHIP across his 149.0 IP. His K% clocks in at 26.3% after punching out 161 hitters, and his BB% is 8.2%. Burke’s ground-ball rate is very low in the 12th percentile, but he does plenty well and has been steady throughout the year. For Houston, RHP Ronel Blanco (0-1) gets the nod after returning from Tommy John surgery five games ago. He’s thrown 23.1 innings with a whopping 7.71 ERA and a 1.46 WHIP, far from what this club hoped for in his comeback. He does have 20 strikeouts for a 19.8% K%, but his BB% sits at 11.9% as well. These offenses have both been quite solid over the season’s second half. Since the All-Star break, the White Sox are seventh in wRC+, 13th in OPS (.718) and sixth in total runs scored (201). They also have a .167 ISO and are one of the better power teams in the sport, though a 24.1% K% is seventh highest. On the full campaign, they slash .237/.318/.404 with a .722 OPS. The Astros aren’t too far behind in production in the second half – they’re 10th in wRC+, 12th in OPS (.719) and 12th in total runs (181). They’re also still among the better teams in terms of hitting for power with a .162 ISO, hitting 51 homers to the White Sox’s 52. The overall number against right-handers does look good, slashing .242/.317/.413 with a .730 OPS on the year. RELATED Miami Marlins vs. Kansas City Royals prediction, pick for Tuesday 9/1/26 White Sox vs. Astros pick, best bet DraftKings Sportsbook lists the White Sox as a -111 Moneyline favorite on the road this evening, with the Astros in play as a -108 underdog at home. The total is set at 8.5 combined runs. There’s no doubt in my mind that Chicago is the team to take tonight. There’s something to be said about working your way back from Tommy John surgery, but Blanco has been straight-up bad since returning at the end of July. He’s lasted no more than 5.1 innings in any outing and has stayed at 4.2 or fewer in four of his five appearances, allowing at least three earned runs and one home run in every single contest. He brings an 11.8% barrel rate into this one and has been shelled for the most part, which the White Sox offense should take advantage of. They’re averaging 4.79 runs per game since the break, so I like this lineup to do some work. articles.body: NFL Injury Report & Analysis: Making Sense of the PUP List and IR | RotoWire Injury Analysis: Making Sense of the PUP List and IR Get the latest NFL injury report with expert analysis. Stay updated on key player injuries and how they impact fantasy football lineups each week. September 1, 2026 Share By: Jeff Stotts @InStreetClothes September 1, 2026 Injury Analysis Mock Draft Simulator Prep for your 2026 Fantasy Football draft with free, unlimited drafts, and real-time grades. NFL teams have trimmed down their rosters to 53 players, with injuries and health influencing countless decisions around the league. For the first in-season NFL injury report, understanding transactional terms used in the process can be beneficial on draft day especially for opportunistic fantasy managers able to draft a player at a discounted rate. The first thing to understand for is the Physically Unable to Perform (PUP) list. With training camp over the Active/PUP list is no longer available to teams. Instead, franchises must now utilize the Reserve/PUP list for these designated players. Players placed on the Reserve/PUP do not count toward the team's 53-man roster and cannot appear in the team's first four regular season contests. This season, players can participate in a 21-day practice period while still stashed on the Reserve/PUP list after the team has played in two regular season games. This allows medical teams to better evaluate players in anticipation of their return following the team's fourth game played. If the player is not activated to the 53-man roster during this window, they must sit out the remainder of the year. Notable players starting the year on the Reserve/PUP include Green Bay's Micah Parsons and Seattle running back Zach Charbonnet . Receiver Alec Pierce was activated off the PUP list late last week and is hoping to be ready for Week 1 after undergoing offseason ankle surgery.
