For the first in-season NFL injury report, understanding transactional terms used in the process can be beneficial on draft day especially for opportunistic fantasy managers able to draft a player at a discounted rate. The first thing to understand for is the Physically Unable to Perform (PUP) list. With training camp over the Active/PUP list is no longer available to teams. Instead, franchises must now utilize the Reserve/PUP list for these designated players. Players placed on the Reserve/PUP do not count toward the team's 53-man roster and cannot appear in the team's first four regular season contests. This season, players can participate in a 21-day practice period while still stashed on the Reserve/PUP list after the team has played in two regular season games. This allows medical teams to better evaluate players in anticipation of their return following the team's fourth game played. If the player is not activated to the 53-man roster during this window, they must sit out the remainder of the year. Notable players starting the year on the Reserve/PUP include Green Bay's Micah Parsons and Seattle running back Zach Charbonnet . Receiver Alec Pierce was activated off the PUP list late last week and is hoping to be ready for Week 1 after undergoing offseason ankle surgery. If a player is ineligible for the PUP list but becomes injured, teams must now consider using the injured reserve (IR). Like the PUP list, any player placed on the IR must miss a minimum of four weeks. A player can only return from an IR designation twice a season, and each team is granted a total of eight IR-to-return designations for the year. The number grows to 10 if they make the playoffs. Like the PUP list, these players can utilize a three-week window to ramp up their activity level. At the conclusion of the 21 days, the player must be activated, placed on season-ending IR, or be released or traded. Several big names were allotted IR designations entering the regular season including James Conner Tank Dell Jordyn Tyson and Christian Kirk IR and PUP list designations may be frustrating, but it does provide a degree of clarity regarding a player's status. Once a player is placed on either list, those willing to invest in him know they will have to proceed without the individual for at least four weeks. The use of the IR can also be used as a good indicator of the health of another player on the team's roster. For example, Conner's designation in Arizona suggests the team feels good about Jeremiyah Love 's availability for Week 1. The rookie running back is working his way back from a high-ankle sprain suffered August 13 but is "progressing really well" according to head coach Mike LaFleur. Turf Burns Emeka Egbuka : The second-year wide receiver has been sidelined since August 12 when he suffered a toe sprain in practice. Toe sprains, particularly those involving the big toe, can be extremely limiting, especially for wideouts. The big toe is crucial in driving the foot off the ground when running or jumping while also withstanding the high amount of stress that comes with weight bearing. Egbuka's Week 1 availability remains in doubt, and I'm moving him down my draft board just a bit. Puka Nacua : The Rams wideout has been limited by soreness in a specific muscle in his core. Nacua's injury involves the psoas muscle. The psoas sits just under the ribs at the lower spine. Its fibers run down through the pelvis, anchoring to the upper femur. It merges with another muscle, the iliacus, to form the iliopsoas, one of the primary hip flexors. Based on this location, a psoas injury can result in pain in the lower back, groin or hip, and be very limiting. Fortunately, Nacua was able to return to practice Sunday, and it looks like he will avoid any missed time. Look for the Rams to handle him conservatively in the days leading up to Week 1. Luther Burden : In Chicago, Burden is recovering from a groin injury sustained in the early days of training camp. The timeline suggests Burden's injury was a more moderate strain. He has resumed limited practice, and the team is optimistic he will be in uniform for Week 1. Chris Olave : Given Olave's checkered NFL injury history, his fans had to hate seeing him leave practice early last week. The team relayed he simply had the wind knocked out of him and it opted to be cautious with his care. He was back at practice the next day and remains the top target in New Orleans. Wan'Dale Robinson : The Titans receiver appears to have avoided a concussion after taking a hard hit in a joint practice with the Bears . The medical staff will monitor his status for any late developing signs or symptoms, but for now he appears okay. Zach Charbonnet : We know Charbonnet will miss at least the first four weeks of the regular season as he recovers from the anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) tear sustained in postseason. The timing of his injury made a Week 1 return unlikely, and an exact target date remains uncertain. Rookie Jadarian Price is expected to start for Seattle with George Holani also set for carries. If Price runs well, the Seahawks could opt for an even more cautious approach with Charbonnet's care to ensure his long-term health. As a result, Charbonnet's fantasy value seems tied to the success of Price. Patrick Mahomes : The former MVP avoided the IR and is on track to start Week 1. As discussed last week, quarterbacks are one of the positions best poised to return to a high level of play following an ACL tear, and I'm bullish on Mahomes entering the year. He may not put up the same numbers he did when he first burst onto the scene, but he remains a reliable fantasy quarterback with a high ceiling. An early season bye in Week 5 should also help him better navigate his comeback. Draft Pass The Draft Pass unlocks this article and every draft tool we build. articles.excerpt: Griffin Wong gives you a preview, prediction and pick for tonight's game between the St. Louis Cardinals and the Los Angeles Dodgers. The post St. Louis Cardinals at Los Angeles Dodgers prediction, pick for Tuesday 9/1/26 appeared first on DraftKings Network .

articles.body: St. Louis Cardinals at Los Angeles Dodgers prediction, pick for Tuesday 9/1/26 Securing a bye past the Wild Card series hasn’t proven to be all that valuable since the MLB playoff format expanded to 12 teams in 2022, as just four of the eight pennant-winning teams in the expanded format had a top-two seed, but any team on the bubble would surely rather not have to play the best-of-three opening round. As a result, despite effectively securing the NL West already, the Los Angeles Dodgers will likely still keep the pedal to the metal, as they currently hold just a 0.5-game lead over the Atlanta Braves for the league’s second seed and an automatic spot in the NLDS. They’ll open September with a critical nine-game homestand, beginning with a three-game series against the St. Louis Cardinals. Tonight’s series opener is set to begin at 10:10 p.m. ET. Michael McGreevy will take the mound for St. Louis, and Eric Lauer will start for Los Angeles. Let’s break down this rematch of the 2021 NL Wild Card Game with some odds and lines DraftKings Sportsbook St. Louis Cardinals at Los Angeles Dodgers Best Bets Los Angeles Dodgers 1st Run of Game (+105) Given that McGreevy, who’s posted a near-6 ERA since the All-Star break will start, Lauer might just have to hold out for one inning before the Dodgers pounce on McGreevy in the bottom half of the inning. Will Smith (LAD) 2+ Total Bases (+135) This also feels like good value for one of Los Angeles’ most reliable hitters over the last couple of seasons. McGreevy likes to throw sinkers to righties, and Smith has a .611 xSLG against righty sinkers in his 52 games. St. Louis Cardinals at Los Angeles Dodgers prediction, preview The Cardinals remain at the fringes of the playoff picture, but with an 18-25 record since the All-Star break, they’re more out than in at this point, trailing the final Wild Card spot by five games. St. Louis wasn’t able to sustain the offense that it enjoyed in the first half of the season, as it’s posted the fifth-lowest OPS since the All-Star break. Jordan Walker has come back to earth a little bit, posting a .267/.316/.418 slash line since the Midsummer Classic, and the Cardinals will also be without slumping rookie JJ Wetherholt (.201/.313/.305) after he landed on the Injured List with wrist tendinitis. Furthermore, their bullpen has collapsed, posting an ERA north of 5 since the All-Star break. All-Star closer Riley O’Brien underwent one complete collapse, as did George Soriano, and Luis Gastelum has had his fair share of bad outings as well. Gordon Graceffo is the only pitcher on the team with at least five innings pitched and a sub-3 ERA, which isn’t exactly a recipe for success. However, St. Louis has arguably found the Dodgers at the right time. Los Angeles has been pretty mediocre for the last two months, as it’s just one game over .500 since the start of July, and it’s had its fair share of disappointing results, including a sweep to Atlanta last week. The Dodgers just haven’t had the offense, ranking only 15th in OPS since the Midsummer Classic, although they’ve just welcomed back both Dalton Rushing and Will Smith, so their production behind the plate shouldn’t be a complete black hole anymore. Los Angeles could also rebound if Mookie Betts, who has a .796 OPS across his last 20 games, keeps up his solid form. Both the Dodgers’ rotation and bullpen have taken slight steps back to start the second half of the season, but Tarik Skubal has been as good as advertised (a 3.00 ERA in five starts), Blake Snell and Tyler Glasnow are both back from IL and pitching well, and All-Star Justin Wrobleski (a likely bullpen piece in the playoffs) was just activated in addition to Rushing and Smith. Los Angeles’ remade bullpen has posted a respectable 3.40 mark this month after putting up an ERA north of 5 in July, and it should get better in the playoffs once Wrobleski, Kris Bubic, and Roki Sasaki presumably settle into new roles. RELATED MLB Betting Splits and Odds for Tuesday, September 1 Nominally, McGreevy is the Cardinals’ ace, but given that he’s pitched to a 3.86 ERA in 26 starts and is coming off of a five-inning, seven-run disaster, that label is tenuous, and his 5.98 ERA since the All-Star break is pretty concerning overall. Advanced stats suggest that that’s been his level all season; he ranks in just the sixth percentile in expected ERA and the fourth percentile in expected batting average. Furthermore, McGreevy has bottom-octile whiff and strikeout rates, and the Dodgers have had some of the best bat-to-ball skills in baseball, still striking out the ninth-fewest times even through their second-half funk. That’ll also put a lot of pressure on St. Louis’ fielders, who, Wetherholt aside, haven’t been very good this season. McGreevy has compounded his mistakes by ranking in the bottom quartile in barrel rate, hard-hit rate, and average exit velocity as well, and it should come as no surprise that Los Angeles ranks in the league’s top 11 in all three power stats. To be fair, McGreevy’s ability to induce grounders should help mitigate one of the Dodgers’ biggest strengths, and the location splits are in his favor, but Los Angeles should still be able to get to him. Lauer is only still in the Dodgers’ rotation because Shohei Ohtani isn’t yet ready to return to the mound, but that speaks more to Los Angeles’ pitching depth than to Lauer’s weakness. In 10 starts and two bulk relief appearances with the Dodgers, Lauer has pitched to a solid 4.00 ERA, giving up three or fewer earned runs in all but two of his starts. Advanced numbers suggest that he has an edge in the starting pitching matchup over McGreevy, though only slightly, as he sports a 21st-percentile xERA. He’s struggled to generate whiffs and strikeouts to an even greater extent than McGreevy, ranking in the seventh percentile or lower in both stats, but Los Angeles has better fielders. Lauer has also struggled mightily to keep the ball down, as he pairs a bottom-ventile ground-ball rate with a sixth-percentile barrel rate, though that shouldn’t be as much of a problem against the grounder-happy, soft-hitting Cardinals. He’s recorded a 2.37 ERA in five starts this season at Dodger Stadium, which should help him effectively counter a St. Louis offense that has been much better on the road. St. Louis Cardinals at Los Angeles Dodgers pick, best bet Best Bet: Los Angeles Dodgers 1st Run of Game (+105) Given how much McGreevy has struggled, especially as of late, this is pretty good value. Of course, the Cardinals will hit first in every inning, and Lauer isn’t exactly an ace, but it would hardly be a surprise if Los Angeles scored in the first inning. Strong Lean: Will Smith (LAD) 2+ Total Bases (+135) Smith will likely don the gear in his first game back, and he was in plenty good form in his 10 games before his injury, recording a .941 OPS in that span. He’s also slugged .563 in his five rehab appearances. TRANSFER DEADLINE DAY – AS IT HAPPENS 22:45 – Melvin Bard (Nice to Leeds United, loan) 22:30 – Robinio Vaz (Roma to Hull City, loan) 22:15 – Jack Grealish (Manchester City to Everton, loan) 22:15 – Brooke Norton-Cuffy (Genoa to Hull City, undisclosed) 22:00 – Tim Iroegbunam (Everton to Hull City, undisclosed) 22:00 – Mykhailo Mudryk (Chelsea to Tottenham Hotspur, loan) Remember him? Mudryk, priced at just £5.4m in FPL, hasn’t kicked a ball in the Premier League since November 2024. 22:00 – Hugo Larsson (Eintracht Frankfurt to Fulham, loan) How many central midfielders do you want, Fulham? Following the arrival of Manuel Angel an hour ago, the Cottagers now have Larsson, Angel, Shea Charles (£5.0m) , Alex Iwobi (£5.5m) and Sander Berge (£5.0m) competing for two places in the engine room. Might we see Iwobi move back to a wide-midfield position, potentially on the right? Fulham only really have Oscar Bobb (£5.5m) out there. As for Larsson, he has been a regular at Eintracht Frankfurt over the last three seasons. The 22-year-old Swedish international joined Frankfurt from Malmo in May 2023. LARSSON’S BUNDESLIGA RECORD WITH FRANKFURT Season Starts (sub apps) Mins Goals Assists DefCons per 90 2025/26 21 (4) 1,820 8.41 2024/25 28 (5) 2,406 9.06 2023/24 21 (8) 1,886 10.17 As the figures above suggest, he’s neither a goalscoring midfielder nor a DefCon magnet. Indeed, the Athletic’s German football correspondent, Seb Stafford-Bloor, describes him as an ‘all-purpose midfielder’ – and thus he’s probably going to be an FPL afterthought. 21:00 – Iliman Ndiaye (Everton to Manchester City, £60m) The biggest deal of the day so far – and one that could have huge FPL implications. Ndiaye, a 14.4%-owned £6.0m midfielder in Fantasy terms, has swapped Merseyside for Manchester for an initial £60m. That fee could rise to £65m with add-ons. Where to begin with this one? The obvious initial observation is that he’s going to really struggle to be the 90-minute man he was at Everton. With Antoine Semenyo (£8.5m), the currently injured Jeremy Doku (£7.4m), Allan Elias (£6.0m) and, for the time being, Phil Foden (£7.0m) as competition out wide, Ndiaye is going to have his work cut out. Even if he becomes a regular Premier League starter, the likelihood of him repeatedly lasting full games and escaping the occasional bit of fatigue-led rotation is slim. He’s losing penalties now, too. Erling Haaland (£15.5m) isn’t going to be giving them up at City. Ndiaye is also surely going to take a hit when it comes to defensive contributions; he’s hit the 12 mark in both Gameweeks this season. Lots to unpack (not to mention the fact that Everton will need a new penalty taker ), so we’ll do it all in more detail in a Moving Target article. 21:00 – Manuel Angel (Real Madrid to Fulham, £3m) Alvaro Arbeloa has returned, for the third time in this transfer window, to his former club Real Madrid to bolster Fulham’s ranks. And once again, following the captures of Gonzalo Garcia (£6.0m) and Cesar Palacios (£5.5m), it’s another academy product Arbeloa is very familiar with. The 22-year-old Manuel Angel was a regular – and captain – under Arbeloa for Real Madrid ‘B’ in 2025/26. And, upon Arbeloa’s promotion to head coach of the senior side, it was the now-Fulham boss who handed the young central midfielder his La Liga debut in March of this year. As you’d expect for someone who’s just made his senior bow in the last six months, he’s very green. Just one senior start in his entire career, although there have been 85 run-outs for the second string. Just three goals in those 85 run-outs for Real Madrid betray his lack of goal threat. DefCons will likely be more forthcoming, although there’s precious little data – 11 contributions in 95 minutes of Real Madrid action – to go off. 20:00 – Kevin Danso (Tottenham Hotspur to Sunderland, loan) Another centre-half to add to the ranks at Sunderland. Dan Ballard (£5.0m), Nordi Mukiele (£5.5m), Omar Alderete (£5.0m) and Luke O’Nien (£4.0m) have all featured there for the Black Cats already this season, with Ballard and Mukiele the DefCon-amassing, clean-sheet-earning pairing in Gameweek 2. O’Nien, a Gameweek 1 starter and fleetingly brief Bench Boost option, suddenly finds himself as low as fifth in the centre-back pecking order. Given the wealth of centre-half options at Regis Le Bris’ disposal, and, you’d assume, the likelihood of Danso only heading to Wearside with the assurances of more game-time, does this mean we’re going to see more of Mukiele at right-back, rather than centre-half? He’ll be in direct competition with veteran Belgian Thomas Meunier (£4.5m), who turns 35 this month, for that role. And, in turn, is Fantasy defender Trai Hume (£4.5m) now simply going to be a full-time winger for the Mackems? Danso, typically a right-sided centre-half, does actually seem like a good fit for Sunderland. He had eye-poppingly good DefCon numbers in 2025/26, indeed, with the best rate of any defender (11.59 per 90 minutes, below) who logged more than 1,000 minutes of pitch-time: Alas, he’s priced up at £5.0m in FPL, so there’s no cheeky £4.5m bargain to be had here. Still, a repeat of those historic DefCon figures and £5.0m will still represent good value. 19:00 – Lucca Brughmans (Genk to Liverpool, £30m) Considering the 6ft 7in goalkeeper only made his senior debut less than five months ago, there’s not much to say about his 15 appearances and six clean sheets – though there was clearly enough to impress Liverpool’s scouts. This is big money for an 18-year-old stopper, but he’s staying on loan at Genk for one season, seemingly part of the long-term plan to replace Alisson Becker (£5.5m). Should the Brazilian leave next summer, either Brughmans or Giorgi Mamardashvili (£5.0m) can take over. 15:00 – Matias Fernandez-Pardo (Lille to Newcastle United, £51m) Completing an incredible turnaround, Newcastle can realistically claim that they have ‘won’ this summer window, with Fernandez-Pardo being the bow on top. An exciting attacker who they long thought was an unrealistic target, they’ll be delighted to sign the Belgian. As a consequence, it allows Nick Woltemade (£5.9m) to depart on loan, hoping to fix his career. As for the 21-year-old Fernandez-Pardo, he delivered eight goals and 10 assists in all 2025/26 competitions for Lille (including two penalties). Initially based on the left flank, he became more of a centre-forward as the season developed, racking up 68 attempts, 30 shots on target and 36 successful dribbles. Of all under-21 players across Europe’s biggest five leagues, Fernandez-Pardo ranked second for big chances (21). “Matias is a highly technical player with explosiveness in his game. He can score and assist, he has courage, and he has the ability to take players on. We’re sure our supporters will enjoy watching him play.” – Matthias Jaissle So, while Matthias Jaissle might have a couple of ideas, the initial thought is that he’ll be the Magpies’ centre-forward, with Yoane Wissa (£6.1m) deeper. articles.title: Should you draft George Kittle in 2026 fantasy football after his Achilles injury?
articles.excerpt: Bryan Armetta breaks down whether fantasy managers should draft injured San Francisco 49ers tight end George Kittle this season. The post Should you draft George Kittle in 2026 fantasy football after his Achilles injury? appeared first on DraftKings Network .
articles.source_type: Captain picks ranked with reasoning, gameweek rankings, DFS targets
articles.body: Should you draft George Kittle in 2026 fantasy football after his Achilles injury? Few teams in football have had worse injury luck in recent years than the 49ers. That’s held true once again this summer, with wide receiver Ricky Pearsall (knee) already ruled out for the season. Fellow pass catcher George Kittle is an even bigger piece of the puzzle for San Francisco. The tight end tore his Achilles tendon during the second round of the playoffs in Philadelphia. That leaves his status up in the air for Week 1 of the 2026 NFL regular season. Should fantasy football managers take a risk and draft Kittle, or is the veteran better off on someone else’s team? RELATED Can Parker Washington become a weekly 2026 fantasy football starter? George Kittle 2026 Fantasy Football Outlook There’s no denying that Kittle is a force…when healthy. The 33-year-old was his usual, productive self in 2025, contributing to an above-average San Francisco offense. Over the course of 11 games, he managed to snag 57 catches for 628 yards and seven touchdowns, displaying impressive chemistry with quarterback Brock Purdy. The seven-time Pro Bowler is usually a solid bet, delivering four straight campaigns of 14 games or more prior to last season. With that being said, Father Time is undefeated; there’s no guarantee Kittle avoids the injury bug upon his return. Speaking of which, when exactly will the tight end make his season debut? Kittle was activated off of the 49ers’ Physically Unable to Perform (PUP) list on August 23rd, a positive sign. Consider general manager John Lynch among those who are optimistic. “George is pushing, and he’s got tremendous energy each and every day, and I think that helps come back from something like this,” Lynch told KNBR 680’s “Murph & Markus . “The way he’s approached this rehab has been tremendous, so we’ll see where it goes, but it certainly has us encouraged.” Still, there’s no guarantee that Kittle will be at 100%. That’s especially true when considering the severity of his injury. However, that price already appears factored in to the future Hall of Famer’s price tag. In PPR leagues, his ADP is hovering around the 95th overall pick. That places Kittle as the TE10, just below Travis Kelce and right above Dalton Kincaid. There’s two schools of thought here. A pessimistic manager might consider looking elsewhere, considering the unusually high amount of quality tight ends in drafts this year. More optimistic managers could view him as a proven performer at fantasy football’s most volatile position. It’s worth noting that San Francisco brought aboard Mike Evans in the offseason. The former Buccaneers wide receiver should serve as the team’s top option in the passing game. Still, that alone doesn’t hinder Kittle’s potential production, We’ve seen the Iowa alum deliver numbers before alongside target monsters such as Deebo Samuel and Brandon Aiyuk. Purdy can sling it, but he’s also willing to play it safe with several short passes to his favorite safety blanket. Whether or not someone drafts Kittle comes down to preference. He remains an upper echelon tight end when healthy, and to many that alone makes the risk worth it. As an added safety measure, fantasy football managers might want to double down at the position within the next round or two. Having a ‘safer’ fill-in could lessen the sting if Kittle misses the first few weeks of the season. At his current cost, San Francisco’s stalwart has never been more affordable. More DraftKings Network Fantasy Football Content Fantasy Football Mock Draft: 10-Team PPR Can Marvin Harrison Jr. finally become a fantasy WR1 in 2026 fantasy football? Is Jordan Mason or Aaron Jones the Vikings’ No. 1 RB heading into Week 1? The 19-year-old, who in 2022 became the youngest player in Premier League history when he made his debut at 15 years and 181 days, is set for another temporary spell away from North London after spending the second half of the previous campaign on loan at Marseille. Nwaneri, who has scored 10 goals in his Gunners career and netted twice for Marseille last term, joins a Dortmund side that suffered a significant setback after new signing Giannis Konstantelias suffered a torn ACL on his debut against Hamburg last Saturday. Lars Ricken, Dortmund’s Managing Director of Sports, told their official website : “By signing Ethan on loan, we’ve succeeded in bringing in a very talented and technically gifted midfielder. “Given Giannis Konstantelias’s extended absence, it was important for us to be able to strengthen our roster at short notice. “For us, signing Ethan was the best possible solution from a sporting perspective. We’re pleased that we were able to finalise this deal just before the transfer window closed.” Topics Arsenal F.C. articles.title: Best MLB player prop bets for Tuesday 9/01/26
articles.excerpt: Dan Johnson shares his top player prop bets for today's MLB slate, including home run, HRRs, and more. The post Best MLB player prop bets for Tuesday 9/01/26 appeared first on DraftKings Network .
articles.source_type: Captain picks ranked with reasoning, gameweek rankings, DFS targets
articles.body: Best MLB player prop bets for Tuesday 9/01/26 Tonight’s card really wants to see the ball keep leaving the yard, so we’re being aggressive with Dinger Tuesday expectations here. You can find a bunch of my home run parlays in the MLB Dugout Betting Group on your DraftKings app (make sure you play your straights! round robin when necessary, etc.!). The following five plays are the ones I’m heaviest on today in terms of stake. Here’s how I’ll play the slate. I’ll be pumping out props and predictions for individual games all season, with plenty of coverage here on DraftKings Network . Follow my handle @dansby_edits for more betting plays. Best MLB player prop bets today Player prop pick Odds Why I like it Drake Baldwin 2+ total bases -130 Drake Baldwin has cleared two total bases seven times in 10 games. His 91.8 mph EV meets Jake Irvin’s 5.62 ERA & Washington’s collapsing bullpen. Fernando Tatis Jr. 2+ total bases -145 Fernando Tatis Jr. is slugging .573 against lefties with 92.8mph EV, and Nick Lodolo’s 6.58 xERA should get destroyed in 94-degree Great American with a 122 homer factor and an 8.57 bullpen ERA behind him. Junior Caminero to hit a home run +275 Junior Caminero’s 37 homers and .516 pitch-weighted xSLG against Manaea’s arsenal meet a middling starter on a skid; Manaea’s given up four-plus runs in three straight starts. Cal Raleigh to hit a home run +360 Cal Raleigh’s got seven homers in 10 games and 98.7mph EV against Paez’s pitch mix, whose three MLB innings yielded 23.1% barrels and a .786 xSLG. Munetaka Murakami to hit a home run +300 Munetaka Murakami has bludgeoned 23 homers in 307 PAs against righties. Ronel Blanco, on the other hand, has a 7.71 ERA, and has allowed .589 slugging to lefties. This includes three Triple-A homers surrendered in 7.1 innings during his didn’t-figure-it-out demotion. In-depth analysis below. Best MLB player prop bets today: analysis Drake Baldwin 2+ total bases (-130) Second-year player though he may be, Drake Baldwin has reached the point where he’ll rake consistently, and the matchup only needs to cooperate. Baldwin owns a 91.8 mph average exit velocity, 51.5% hard-hit rate, and 12.8% barrel rate on the season. He’s churned through 21 total bases across his last 10 games, and cleared this very line seven times, hence the disappointing juice. His SL .300/.382/.493 slash against righties makes this recent surge so much easier to trust at this beggar’s price point. Jake Irvin gives me confidence this won’t blow up in our faces. Irvin’s logged a 5.62 ERA, 1.40 WHIP, and 1.54 HR/9. After a particularly rough one last time out, his home ERA has climbed above 7.00. Baldwin carries a .530 pitch-weighted xSLG against Irvin’s arsenal. He has slugged .525 against four-seamers and .506 against sinkers, with hard-hit rates above 56% against both shapes. Washington cannot reliably extinguish Baldwin after Irvin leaves, either. Its bullpen owns baseball’s worst recent ERA, while the temperature should reach the low 90s. Baldwin also projects atop Atlanta’s order, creating a strong chance at five plate appearances. It’s worth the cost. Fernando Tatis Jr. 2+ total bases (-145) Fernando Tatis Jr. enters Cincinnati having bent the summer toward his very own superstardom, just not with the intensity of, say, a PCA. He owns a 92.8 mph average exit velocity and 53.7% hard-hit rate on the season, after a start that saw him go on a biblical home run drought. His SLG% against left-handed pitching sits at .573. And big lefty Nick Lodolo offers no pitch that materially weakens Tatis’s pure swing. His premier spot in the Padres lineup should also deliver four or five swings. Tatis boasts approximately a .500 wxSLG against Lodolo’s full pitch mix/arsenal. It hasn’t been a great year for Lodolo: he’s allowed a .496 xSLGa and .384 xwOBA while pitching to the cacophonous tune 6.58 xERA. His second-half ERA is now 7.83. His fastball gets obliterated when it misses locations, and his breaking pitches have stopped looking juicy to hitters. Great American Ball Park, too! We love that. Temperatures are forecasted around 94 degrees, and the park’s home-run factor even in neutral weather sits around 122 on the season. Cincinnati’s bullpen affords even longer leash for this bet to hit even after Lodolo gets the hook. It ranks 28th entering the slate, and posted an 8.57 ERA over the previous week. Tatis has averaged 2.2 total bases across his last 10 games. He can clear this with one swing, yet his speed and line-drive pedigree, as always, preserve multiple-hit paths. Junior Caminero to hit a home run (+275) Junior Caminero’s sitting pretty on 37 home runs for the season, and we’ll take him to go yard again even against Sean Manaea tonight. SL, Caminero is batting .282 with a .536 slugging percentage. He’s currently on a 14-game hitting streak and is one of the AL’s best power hitters. He’s easy to click. As far as his opponent’s arsenal goes, Sean Manaea attacks with four-seamers 38.3% of the time, sweepers 30.8%, sinkers 19.7%, and cutters 7.7%. Caminero’s xSLG against those pitches, respectively, is elite except for the sweeper: .620, .401, .511, and .537. Go ahead and average/weight those results out against Manaea’s usage, and you get a .516 matchup xSLG for the matchup tonight. Manaea’s had a good second half, and he’s lowered his ERA to 4.55, but still has an expected ERA closer to 4.80. Even with the improvements, he’s allowed at least four earned runs in three straight starts. His fastball remains especially meaty against Caminero’s swing path. Only Manaea’s sweeper, his best counter, could erase Caminero completely tonight. And, even still, Caminero’s done decent damage against it. Give me a souvenir. Cal Raleigh to hit a home run (+380) When Boston replaced Sonny Gray with Jedixson Paez, Raleigh’s chances to keep his power surge going improved drastically. Paez has thrown only three major-league innings, so calling that a certainty would be a silly thing to do. But, in fairness, across those innings hitters still went nuts: 95.3 mph exit velocity, 23.1% barrel rate, .786 xSLG, and zero strikeouts. His minor-league profile is that of a flamethrower, so this isn’t all a perfect square. Paez struck out 30.8% of hitters and walked only 2.9% across 61.1 innings in the minors this year. He also, however, allowed a 19.6% HR/FB rate. So, sure—he can mow lineups down, but once he gets solved, the ball gets tattooed. Enter Raleigh, who’s finally obliterating mistakes after PCA slapped the Big Dumper—Big Dumper’s dumper, I suppose—in August. His last 10 batted balls have yielded a 98.7 mph EV, 70% hard contact, 40% barrels. Six of those ten have been in the air. He’s gone yard seven times in the L10 games, and averaged 3.3 total bases. Cool, damp Fenway weather trims my enthusiasm considerably, but not all the way. Still, all he’s gotta do is clear the Monster. Munetaka Murakami to hit a home run (+300) Munetaka Murakami’s recent box scores look quiet and potentially figured-out—I know. But the underlying power is still there. Let us not for get that, on his rookie season, which has included an injury stint, he has hit 29 home runs across 447 plate appearances. Against right-handed pitching, that drills down to 23 homers in 307 trips, a 7.49% home-run rate per plate appearance. Ronel Blanco might help the box score look better for Mune tonight. Blanco’s got an outright-bad 7.71 ERA, 5.42 xERA, 11.8% barrel rate allowed, and .469 xSLGA. Left-handed hitters like Murakami’ve clocked a .589 SLG against him this year. His figure-it-out demotion earlier in the summer solved little, maybe even nothing. Blanco surrendered 12 earned runs and three homers across 7.1 AAA innings. Murakami’s pitch-weighted xSLG against Blanco’s full arsenal lands near a stratospheric .542. However, Blanco throws four-seamers and curves almost half the time, and those are precisely the two shapes Murakami still sees the best. In his last ten batted balls in play against those two pitches, Mune’s got a 97.5 mph EV, 60% hard-hit rate, 50% blasts, and 30% barrels. Two home runs in that sample size, too. Ignore the strikeout rate for tonight. If anything, it helps narrow Murakami’s successful outcomes toward serious damage of the souvenir variety. articles.title: Patterson Signs For Torino
articles.excerpt: Nathan Patterson has left Everton, signing for Serie A club Torino on a permanent deal for an undisclosed fee. The 24-year-old full-back joined the Blues from Rangers in January 2022, playing 68 times for the Club across all competitions. Patterson made his Toffees debut in an FA Cup fifth-round victory over Boreham Wood in March 2022, and the following year, played 19 Premier League matches in his first full season on Merseyside. A highlight of that campaign arrived when the young Scot started in Everton’s emphatic 5-1 victory at Brighton & Hove Albion in May 2023, when Patterson excellently tamed tricky winger Kaoru Mitoma. On the international stage, the defender helped Scotland qualify for this summer’s 2026 FIFA World Cup finals, where he earned caps against Haiti, Morocco and Brazil. Everyone at Everton thanks Nathan for his commitment to the Club across the past four-and-a-half years and wishes him all the best for the next step in his career.

articles.body: MLB DFS Picks: Top Fantasy Baseball Value Plays for Tuesday 9/1/26 Note the start time for tonight’s nine-game featured MLB DFS slate on DraftKings. It’s 7:40 p.m. ET. You might even have time to squeeze in a quick meal with your loved ones before you then spend all night making lineups and watching baseball. Let’s break down a couple values for Tuesday’s action on the diamond. Top MLB DFS Value Plays Angels SP Grayson Rodriguez ($7,000) vs. Yankees Royals 1B Vinnie Pasquantino ($3,900) vs. Marlins Dodgers OF Kyle Tucker ($3,400) vs. Cardinals Set your DraftKings MLB DFS lineups here: MLB $150K Bat Flip [$50K to 1st] SP Grayson Rodriguez, Los Angeles Angels vs. New York Yankees, $7,000 I don’t think I’d go so far as saying I trust Grayson Rodriguez again, but the former top pitching prospect is coming off a very encouraging month. In his five starts in August, Rodriguez managed a 2.93 ERA and a 2.76 FIP across 27.2 innings. That span also included a 25.7% strikeout rate, which is far more in line with the version of Rodriguez we saw back in Baltimore in 2024. The man is getting healthier, and he’s registered a 27.6 FPTS performance within the past two weeks. I shouldn’t have to sell you on his ceiling. Let’s also not forget that we don’t have to fear the Yankees at the moment, as it pertains to a DFS matchup. Still missing Aaron Judge (rib), New York struggled throughout August, sitting in the lower-half of the league in batting average (.231), wOBA (.308) and wRC+ (96). Here’s the kicker. The Yankees also own the AL’s highest strikeout rate since August 1 at 25.7%. How fitting. 1B Vinnie Pasquantino, Kansas City Royals vs. Miami Marlins, $3,900 This doesn’t have to be too complicated. Pasquantino is simply too cheap tonight. The 28-year-old returned from the IL on August 17 and the proceeded to slash .341/.442/.636 to close out the month with a 200 wRC+. It’s not the largest sample size in the world, but we’re talking about someone that hit 32 home runs last season. We all know what Pasquantino is capable of at the big league level. As for matchup, Tyler Phillips ($5,800) will toe the rubber for the Marlins. Phillips owns a 4.95 FIP as a starter in 2026, while he’s also struggled a great deal when pitching away from LoanDepot Park. Phillips has conceded a massive 47.1% hard hit rate to opposing LHBs, so it’s not a stretch to believe he’ll have his issues with the red-hot bat of Pasquantino. RELATED MLB DFS Picks: Starting Pitcher Rankings for Tuesday 9/1/26 OF Kyle Tucker, Los Angeles Dodgers vs. St. Louis Cardinals, $3,400 This isn’t the lowest Tucker’s price has been all season — that would be Sunday’s $3,300 tag against the Tigers — but I think we’ve finally reached the point where the salary is small enough that you have to consider the veteran as a viable value. I mean, how often can you a guy who was going top 10 in redraft this close to $3,000? I’ll tell you. Almost never. There aren’t many redeeming stats for Tucker’s tenure in Los Angeles, so let’s just focus on the matchup. Michael McGreevy ($6,500) might be having a decent campaign on the surface, but goodness are the underlying stats not a fan of this RHP’s work. McGreevy combines a fourth percentile opponent expected batting average (.282) with a 12th percentile opponent barrel rate (10.0%). McGreevy’s 5.41 xERA is nearly two runs higher than his 3.86 ERA, and regression starting kicking in last week when he surrendered 10 hits and seven earned runs to the Orioles. Anticipate something similar this evening. Garion Thorne All views expressed are my own. I am an employee of DraftKings and am ineligible to play in public DFS or DKSB contests. articles.title: Ryan Poles Defines Bears' Trade of Gervon Dexter as Ideal Timing
articles.excerpt: The Bears GM has learned how to get rid of drafted players who may not fit, and getting back something in return made trading their defensive tackle possible.
articles.source_type: Gameweek squads, team news round-ups, deadline reminders
articles.body: Ryan Poles Defines Bears' Trade of Gervon Dexter as Ideal Timing Shedeur Sanders pulls away ffrom Gervon Dexter but falls for a sack last year at Soldier Field. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The confluence of several factors made it possible for GM Ryan Poles to trade defensive tackle Gervon Dexter for a fifth-round pick and cornerback Clark Phillips III. The major one was obviously defensive tackles Jordan van den Berg and Jayden Loving making huge statements, but it's obvious the Bears had no intention of paying a big contract in the future for Dexter, who has only flashed his talent at times throughout three seasons. "That deal was more about timing than anything," Poles said Tuesday during his annual post-preseason state-of-the-team address. "Timing and fit. "You know we had some young guys really pushing that came in this year with Jordan and Loving. They did a really good job, and we felt like it was a good fit as we moved forward." Final thoughts on the Gervon Dexter trade. The Gervon Dexter trade was about Dexter the rookies just made it easier. Dexter wanted an extension. Chicago didnât want to pay him, solid pass rusher. Not great vs the run. His 44.0 PFF run D grade ranked 107th/134 IDL. For aâ¦ pic.twitter.com/2Pe0Eny0I5 â Clay Harbor (@clayharbs82) September 1, 2026 The timing in this case was the Bears owed Dexter a huge deal by next year and at this point felt they could afford to lose a player chosen in Round 2 because they're looking at using lower-priced, promising players this year. The money in the future will be needed for something important, like an extension for quarterback Caleb Williams. Also, the trade now could bring back a little more than a trade at the deadline, and maybe a lot less then if Dexter had been injured. Confident in current group None of that would matter if the Bears GM and coach Ben Johnson thought they lacked the defensive tackles to shut down the run or rush from the interior. They are convinced about both van den Berg and Loving, but also the veteran group including Grady Jarrett, Neville Gallimore and Kentavius Street. Also, they have added back veteran defensive tackle James Lynch to the roster, for now, at least. Ryan Poles said the Gervon Dexter trade was largely due to Jordan van den Berg and Jayden Loving looking great in camp. pic.twitter.com/owVDoIztDw â Caleb Williams Fan Club (@CalebFC18) September 1, 2026 "I have a ton of confidence in those guys," Poles said. "They did a good job this preseason. I still think itâs a unit thatâs going to have to work together, whether itâs our blitz packages or the twists and games that we play. Those guys bring it, they have really good motors and they have the skillset to get into the backfield and get some pressure on the quarterback, and the defense is going to have to play as one unit. Thatâs important." As for the trade itself, Poles admitted he has gained the ability dump off parts who may not fit or who failed. In this case, that's Dexter. Still, it doesn't say much for the GM when they've been dumping off draft picks after a year or two. "I think I've been pretty quick to, if there's something that doesn't work out, I think we are pretty good about being honest about that and moving on," Poles said. "I don't think we are an organization, or I'm a GM, that's going to hold on just because it was a draft pick or a trade that you made and now I have to make it work and we are just going to keep that player here when it's not working. That will hurt the team. "I think I mentioned before that the locker room always knows. So we hold true to that. We want to put the best group together regardless of how they are acquired." In Ryan Polesâ first 4 years (2020-2024) heâs had 16 picks from 2nd-5th round Thereâs 7 on the roster at this moment Kyler Gordon Braxton Jones Roschon Johnson Tyrique Stevenson Noah Sewell Austin Boooker Tory Taylor Name one thatâs even an average starter or healthy #Bears â Jake (@Jake_B30) August 30, 2026 It's obvious Phillips was a throw-in on the deal from the way Poles talked about the cornerback addition. He couldn't classify him as a fit for a specific spot. "Most of his tape in Atlanta was outside (as opposed to slot)," Poles said. "In college, he was inside. I liked what that tape looked like, too. Heâs capable of both, but since heâs been in the league, heâs been outside. So weâll see where we start him off and go from there..â Phillips could get a look at slot The obvious need right now is at slot cornerback. The Bears are going with rookie Malik Muhammad, another player who has been outside for the most part. Poles even mentioned they have given safety Xavier Woods a look there and also Cam Lewis and Wrookie safety Dillon Thieneman for a few downs. "I really love this guy as a player. I don't know how anybody can look at this and see any sort of downside" - @adamrank on Clark Phillips #thesickpodcast pic.twitter.com/VS4NdA9rEf â The Sick Podcast with Adam Rank (@sickpodadamrank) September 1, 2026 What he's certain of is they don't have starter Kyler Gordon for now, as he works through his injury. Through the trade, the defensive line has shaped up. Health is returning, although Poles can't yet say defensive end Austin Booker will be available for Week 1 or when defensive tackle/end Shemar Turner will be back from knee surgery. Turner is in the later stages of his rehab, though, Poles added. The defensive line has been labeled a weakness throughout the offseason and losing a veteran player with talent can't be construed as a victory for this season. What the Bears have to hope now is they have benefited in the long run by giving two younger players a chance for playing time earlier in a rotation than they might have had, as they mix with one of the NFC's less impressive veteran tackle groups. While the Bears have been working on cutting down the roster to 53 players, I watched some film on cornerback Clark Phillips III. Here are some clips from his Week 18 performance against the Panthers in the 2024 season. 1 vs 1 against Xavier Legette. pic.twitter.com/TVhR9VXtRe â Nicholas Moreano (@NicholasMoreano) August 30, 2026 Add us as a preferred source on Google Follow Loading recommendations... articles.title: Danso: ‘The sky is the limit’
articles.excerpt: Kevin Danso is relishing the opportunity to begin his Sunderland journey after completing a season-long loan move from Tottenham Hotspur. The 27-year-old centre-back arrives on Wearside with a wealth of domestic and European experience, having made 128 appearances for RC Lens and 52 for Spurs. An Austria international, Danso also featured in all four of his country’s matches at the 2026 FIFA World Cup and has earned 36 caps. Now, the defender is looking forward to getting started in red and white and experiencing the atmosphere at the Stadium of Light. “It feels amazing to be here and I can’t wait to get started,” Danso said. “Growing up in England, Sunderland has a rich Premier League history and I’m so excited to be a part of that journey. “I hope I can bring my experience to the group and help the lads both on and off the pitch. “First and foremost, I’d describe myself as a warrior. articles.body: Can Dontayvion Wicks Become Jalen Hurts’ Second-Best Fantasy Receiver in 2026? Philadelphia Eagles’ Offense The strongest argument for Wicks begins with Philadelphia’s redesigned offense. Under Kevin Patullo last season, the Eagles ranked 27th in pass-play percentage, 26th in passes per game and 23rd in passing yards per game. They also finished 29th in motion rate, while Hurts had the league’s lowest under-center dropback rate among qualified quarterbacks. Hurts was effective. He completed 64.8% of his passes for 3,224 yards with a career-high 25 touchdowns, six interceptions and a 98.5 passer rating. But the passing game lacked consistency. Sean Mannion’s new system is emphasizing motion, under-center play-action, timing routes and wide-zone concepts. Mannion worked with Wicks in Green Bay, while new run-game coordinator Ryan Mahaffey previously coached Packers receivers. Combined with Chris Kuper replacing longtime offensive line coach Jeff Stoutland, this is a legitimate schematic change rather than a minor tweak to last season’s playbook. It should create more defined reads for Hurts, which can definitely benefit Wicks. Wicks’ 2026 Fantasy Football Upside Despite Wicks’ lackluster personal production, his opportunity will still do most of the heavy lifting. He followed a promising 39-catch, 581-yard rookie season with 415 yards in 2024 and career lows of 30 receptions, 332 yards, and two touchdowns last year. His 1.39 yards per route run and 19% target-per-route rate were ordinary, and one Thanksgiving breakout accounted for 94 yards and both of his touchdowns. The Eagles still traded two draft picks for him, gave him a $12.5 million extension, and have seen him develop early chemistry with Hurts. A.J. Brown’s departure removes the player who commanded 121 targets last season, and Wicks is currently listed as a starter. The problem is that those opportunities vacated by Brown will be heavily contested. DeVonta Smith is the unquestioned lead receiver after producing 77 catches for 1,008 yards, while Dallas Goedert recorded 60 catches, 591 yards, and 11 touchdowns. Philadelphia also signed Hollywood Brown, who posted a 49-587-5 line last year, and used the 20th overall pick on Makai Lemon, another WR with some upside. Lemon’s missed camp time gives Wicks an early advantage, but his draft capital makes him a serious threat to Wicks’ role as the season progresses. Wicks can definitely become Hurts’ second-best receiver in fantasy this season, and is probably the early favorite for the job, but he hasn’t come even close to securing the spot. At the very least, Wicks knows the offense, has Hurts’ trust, and should have a decent role to kick off the season. He’ll be an appealing late-round swing. articles.title: 2026 NFL Win Total Prediction, Pick: Tampa Bay Buccaneers
articles.excerpt: Sean Barnard shares his prediction and best bet for the Tampa Bay Buccaneers win total ahead of the 2026-27 NFL regular season. The post 2026 NFL Win Total Prediction, Pick: Tampa Bay Buccaneers appeared first on DraftKings Network .
articles.source_type: Captain picks ranked with reasoning, gameweek rankings, DFS targets
articles.body: 2026 NFL Win Total Prediction, Pick: Tampa Bay Buccaneers The Tampa Bay Buccaneers fell short of the postseason last year for the first time since 2019. They finished with an 8-9 record, tied with both the Falcons and Panthers for the best record in the NFC South, but the head-to-head tiebreaker left them on the outside looking in on the playoff action. After winning the division four consecutive seasons before this, the Buccaneers will be eager to improve this year and get back to their expected standard. But the NFC South is expected to be competitive, with all four teams holding +400 odds or shorter to win on DraftKings Sportsbook , making it the only division in the NFL where this is the case. Below is my pick and prediction for the Buccaneers’ 2026-27 regular season, including a win total bet on DraftKings Sportsbook Tampa Bay Buccaneers 2026/27 NFL win total odds The Buccaneers’ win total for the 2026/27 NFL regular season is set at over/under 8.5 wins on DraftKings Sportsbook Tampa Bay holds -136 odds of the win total remaining under the line and +115 odds of going over. Tampa Bay Buccaneers 2026/27 season prediction The most notable loss of the offseason for the Buccaneers was Mike Evans. The future Hall of Fame wide receiver has been a staple of the franchise for the past 12 years. Evans saw his streak of 11 consecutive seasons with 1,000+ receiving yards snapped last season after he was limited to just eight games due to injury. Last year’s 19th overall pick, Emeka Egbuka, showed promise in his rookie season and will look to improve his production further. Chris Godwin will be making his return from injury, while Jalen McMillan and Tez Johnson will also be asked to play significant roles. At running back, Rachaad White elected to leave in free agency, forcing Bucky Irving into the clear lead back role while Kenny Gainwell was brought in as a free agent as well. A major storyline that has hung over Tampa Bay across training camp has been the looming contract outlook for Baker Mayfield. The former first overall pick has looked the part of a franchise quarterback since putting on a Buccaneers jersey and expects to be paid like one. He is entering the final year of his three-year, $100 million contract and has elected to pause negotiations to play out the deal. Mayfield put a self-imposed deadline of training camp for extension talks to be halted, and was unable to reach an agreement with the organization before this passed. Mayfield will be eager to play his best football and maximize his chances of securing his desired contract, but this storyline could also serve as a distraction. There will be some expected changes in the play style, as Tampa Bay fired offensive coordinator Josh Grizzard following last year’s postseason absence. Zac Robinson has taken over this role after previously serving as the Falcons’ offensive coordinator across the past two seasons. Danny Smith also stepped in as the new special teams coordinator for the Buccaneers. RELATED 2026 NFL Win Total Prediction, Pick: Dallas Cowboys The biggest changes on this roster were evident on defense this offseason. Tampa Bay finished last season ranked 20th in opponent points allowed and 19th in total yards conceded. They also ranked 27th in passing yards allowed and 23rd in passing touchdowns given up. The organization also lost star linebacker Lavonte David after he elected to retire following his 14 years in the league. The Buccaneers selected Rueben Bain Jr. with the 15th overall pick in the NFL Draft, who is expected to be an impact edge rusher from day one. They also selected LB Josiah Trotter in the second round and spent later-round picks on a cornerback and defensive tackle. In free agency, Alex Anzalone will likely be their most impactful addition. A five-year team captain with the Lions, Anzalone will likely be asked to quarterback the defensive side of the ball and brings a level of coverage skill the Buccaneers have not had at the linebacker position in quite some time. DT A’Shawn Robinson, EDGE Al-Quadin Muhammad, and S Miles Killebrew are also expected to play key roles. Vita Vea also had some frustrations over his contract with the organization leading into this season, which even led to a trade request from the star defensive talent. But the two sides worked out an agreement, and Vea will remain a foundational part of this Buccaneers team. Tampa Bay Buccaneers win total pick It had been four years since the Buccaneers had failed to win the division and six since they last missed the playoffs. The organization clearly didn’t let that slide, and it made major changes this offseason. New offensive coordinator Zac Robinson is known for elevating a running game, and Bucky Irving has flashed as a talent, though his production hasn’t matched it so far. Expect a breakout season for the 24-year-old, with more touches expected in this new system and with less competition on the roster. This commitment to the running game should also help open the entire offense, which has become a bit too pass-dependent at times. But expect Baker Mayfield to be committed to wearing his heart on his sleeve every game with his contractual uncertainty in mind. Mayfield has never been shy about showing his emotions or leaning on extra motivation, and that will be evident all season. It has been an impressive career revival in Tampa Bay for the two-time Pro Bowler. The Buccaneers have been one of the league’s most dynamic offenses with Mayfield at the helm, and he will be eager to get the team back to that form this season with the big-picture implications in mind. In addition, the Buccaneers boast a top-three ranked offensive line and several young wide receivers who appear poised to take a big step forward. More questions remain about Tampa Bay’s defensive outlook. But the organization did its best to address needs and added some high-profile talent at key positions. The secondary could be problematic, but the Buccaneers should feel confident about generating a more consistent pass rush and winning in the trenches on this side of the ball. Tampa Bay also has the 12th-easiest strength of schedule, which should help their path to wins. The NFC South is one of the NFL’s more unpredictable divisions this season. There is fair reason for optimism based on how the Saints finished last season, how Bryce Young showed progress with the Panthers, and whether the Falcons can get consistent, competent quarterback play; if so, they have a window to win the division as well. But this Buccaneers team has a production floor and expectation that none of these other teams do. With Mayfield as motivated as ever, some key additions to the overall roster, and some necessary shakeups on the coaching staff, expect the Buccaneers to burst out of the gates this season and win over 8.5 games. Before last season, Tampa Bay had won nine or more regular season matchups in five straight years. They lost four of their last five games last season, each by four points or less, and six of their nine losses came by one possession or less overall. Expect a more focused effort in winning by the margins, and 8.5 wins should be a comfortable bar for the Buccaneers to clear as they return to their desired standard as a franchise. articles.body: Juventus complete loan deal for Newcastle record signing Woltemade Skip to content Football News Serie A News Juventus complete loan deal for Newcastle record signing Woltemade Woltemade had struggled to nail down a regular starting spot at Newcastle. Nicholas McGee Last Update: 58 minutes ago 2 min read Add us as a preferred source on Google Juventus have completed the signing of Newcastle United forward Nick Woltemade on a season-long loan. The Bianconeri have paid a £3.5million loan fee to the Magpies to secure the services of Woltemade, who joined Newcastle last August for a club-record £69million fee. Woltemade hit the ground running following his move from Stuttgart, scoring six goals in his first 11 games for the club. But his form petered out and Woltemade struggled to nail down a place in former manager Eddie Howe’s starting XI. He finished his debut season with Newcastle with 11 goals and four assists to his name, but has now made the temporary switch to Turin after struggling to make an impression in new manager Matthias Jaissle’s system. Newcastle are unbeaten in their first three games under Jaissle but, though Woltemade provided an assist for Yoane Wissa in last Saturday’s 2-0 win at Tottenham, the Germany international has appeared an awkward fit for Jaissle’s style of play. Juventus will hope Woltemade will find Serie A more to his liking, with the 24-year-old joining a side fourth in the early table after winning each of their opening two games. Woltemade joins Juve as another of their strikers, Jonathan David, departs for pastures new. David joined Juve last summer following the expiration of his contract at Lille. However, the Canada international scored just eight goals in 46 appearances. Juve will reportedly cover 50 per cent of David’s salary. The loan features an option to buy worth €25 million. articles.title: New Orleans Saints over/under wins prediction for 2026-27
articles.excerpt: Bryan Armetta shares his favorite New Orleans Saints over/under win total bet ahead of the 2026-27 NFL regular season. The post New Orleans Saints over/under wins prediction for 2026-27 appeared first on DraftKings Network .

articles.body: New Orleans Saints over/under wins prediction for 2026-27 It’s easy to forget now, but the Saints were firmly in contention for the first overall pick of the 2026 Draft. New Orleans managed to win four of its final five games, finishing with a middling 6-11 record. That end of season hot streak was made possible in large part by quarterback Tyler Shough. The rookie impressed during nine starts, and now comes into this year as the team’s undisputed starter. That’s not the only reason for excitement; new running back Travis Etienne should give the Saints a serious boost out of the backfield. Still, is all that enough to turn this middle of the road club into an NFC South contender? Will Shough take the leap from intriguing quarterback to franchise signal caller? Below is my pick and prediction for New Orleans’ 2026-27 regular season, including a win total bet on DraftKings Sportsbook RELATED 2026 NFL Win Total Prediction, Pick: Atlanta Falcons Saints win total pick for NFL regular season It’s never wise to over simplify a futures bet. Still, New Orleans’ chances at flirtin with the division, let alone finishing above .500, likely come down to Tyler Shough. All things considered, the second-round pick lived up to the hype. Through 11 games (nine starts), he threw for 2,384 yards, ran for 186 more, and recorded 13 total touchdowns. Those numbers aren’t jaw-dropping, but a clear step up from backup QB Spencer Rattler. Even more important, the Louisville alum started in five of the team’s six wins. Shough already possesses great chemistry with top wideout Chris Olave. The former Pro Bowler finished last season with 100 catches, 1,163 yards and nine touchdowns. Unfortunately, rookie Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) is estimated to miss an extended period of time. That means more opportunity for lesser known names such as Devaughn Vele and sixth-round rookie Barion Brown. Tyson’s injury could push head coach Kellen Moore towards a run-first approach on offense. New Orleans’ offseason moves seem to suggest a renewed commitment towards pounding the rock. In addition to the previously mentioned Etienne, former Bills guard David Edwards signed a four-year deal this offseason. New Orleans’ defense lacks star power, especially compared to some other clubs in the NFC. With that being said, don’t let the lack of big names overshadow an above-average unit. Former Chargers head coach Brandon Staley is one of the league’s better defensive coordinators, and it showed last season. The team finished tenth in EPA per play, driven in large part by their work against the run. The Saints allowed 4.0 rush yards per attempt, seventh-best in the NFL. Defensive tackle Bryan Bresee (knee) is out for the year, but there’s enough depth up front to hold the fort. Plenty of pressure will be on edge rushers Carl Granderson and Chase Young; the duo combined for 16.0 sacks in 2026. If there’s a major knock on the Saints, it’s that most of their wins came against the NFL’s worst squads. It’s not exactly wrong; that final stretch of the season saw them play the Panthers, Jets, Titans and Buccaneers twice. However, this year’s gauntlet isn’t the most intimidating either. According to winning percentage from 2025, New Orleans owns the second-easiest schedule in football this season. Early matchups with the Raiders , Falcons, Giants and Browns present an opportunity to finish the first half above .500. From there, who knows what the future holds for this group. Best Bet: Saints over 7.5 wins (-120) It’s fair to express some skepticism with the Saints, especially following Tyson’s injury. However, that feels a bit short-sighted. Etienne and Olave alone are among the NFL’s better weapons, giving Shough a pair of difference-makers on offense. On the other side of the ball, this defense should remain (at minimum) league average. That’s enough to contend in a weak NFC South division. Don’t be shocked if New Orleans sneaks its way into the playoff picture. articles.excerpt: Check out a preview, prediction and pick for tonight's Miami Marlins vs. Kansas City Royals game on Tuesday's MLB slate. The post Miami Marlins vs. Kansas City Royals prediction, pick for Tuesday 9/1/26 appeared first on DraftKings Network .

articles.body: Miami Marlins vs. Kansas City Royals prediction, pick for Tuesday 9/1/26 We’ve officially passed the end of August and are into September, meaning the MLB’s postseason race is coming down to the wire. The Miami Marlins are four games shy of an NL Wild Card berth and clawing to get back into the mix; tonight, they take on the Kansas City Royals for the second game of this interleague series. First pitch is set for 7:40 .m. ET at Kauffman Stadium. Let’s dive in with a preview, prediction and pick for today’s Marlins vs. Royals game courtesy of odds and lines on DraftKings Sportsbook. Marlins vs. Royals prediction, preview The Marlins were one of the hottest teams in the MLB prior to the All-Star break, but ever since, they’ve been near the bottom of the sport in winning percentage. They’ve gone 17-24 over the season’s second half and are now 69-69 on the year with a +12 run differential – four games out of the NL Wild Card. The Royals’ season virtually ended long ago, and they’re just 62-76 on the campaign with a -83 run differential. With that said, they’ve actually posted the fifth-best record in baseball since the break at 24-17 and are 8-2 over their last 10 contests. Miami starts RHP Tyler Phillips (3-6), who has bounced between a bullpen role and that of a starter. He brings a 3.59 ERA and 1.37 WHIP into this matchup, producing 86 strikeouts over 105.1 IP. His K% and BB% aren’t great at 18.9% and 9.9%, but he does have an above-average grade in chase and whiff rate as well as ground-ball rate. For Kansas City, it’s RHP Randy Dobnak (2-2) on the mound tonight. His ERA is 1.92 with a 1.37 WHIP over his 51.2 IP, so run suppression has been a strength over his 10 games. He’s struck out just 34 batters for a low 15.4% K% and a 9.5% BB%; however, a 95th-percentile barrel rate and 93rd-percentile ground-ball rate both stand out at elite levels. Over the season’s second half, the Marlins’ offense has far underperformed compared to the first half. Since the break, they’re 26th in runs scored (158) with a .678 OPS that ranks 24th. The club’s ISO has never been particularly high this year, but a .128 mark is lower than the season-long mark. They’re also 25th in wRC+. On the full campaign, the Marlins slash .254/.330/.406 with a .735 OPS against right-handed pitching. Looking at the Royals, their own offense has improved over the second half. They’re 14th in total runs scored (179) with a .729 OPS that sits 11th in the sport, also logging a .159 ISO while improving the plate process – they have a low 19.8% K% over this span. Kansas City is 11th in wRC+ since the break as well. On the full year, the club slashes .247/.317/.404 with a .721 OPS. RELATED Milwaukee Brewers vs. Chicago Cubs prediction, pick for Tuesday 9/1/26 Marlins vs. Royals pick, best bet DraftKings Sportsbook lists the Royals as a -120 Moneyline favorite at home this evening, with the Marlins in play as a +100 underdog on the road. The total is set at 9.5 combined runs. In my opinion, this total feels a little bit high. Neither of the starting arms are stars by any means, or really anywhere close to it, but they’ve pitched well on the full season and as of late. Dobnak’s ERA was 2.81 over his 25.2 IP last month and he doesn’t allow many homers; Phillips’ 3.86 ERA over his 21.0 IP in August was really solid given that he allowed one or fewer earned runs in three of his five starts. Yes, the Royals’ bullpen remains a problem and the Marlins’ hasn’t been good in the second half, either. They’re producing staff ERAs of 4.49 and 4.78 over this span and have been particularly vulnerable to the long ball with the fourth and fifth-worst HR/9 marks of any club. Assuming the starters don’t collapse early, though, there’s still room for the under on 9.5 runs to cash, especially with Miami’s bats inconsistent at best at the moment. Best bet: Under 9.5 total runs (-106) Keagan Smith I am a promoter at DraftKings and am also an avid fan and user and may sometimes play on my personal account in the games that I offer advice on. articles.title: Seattle Mariners at Boston Red Sox prediction, pick for Tuesday 9/1/26
articles.excerpt: Griffin Wong gives you a preview, prediction and pick for tonight's game between the Seattle Mariners and the Boston Red Sox. The post Seattle Mariners at Boston Red Sox prediction, pick for Tuesday 9/1/26 appeared first on DraftKings Network .
articles.source_type: Captain picks ranked with reasoning, gameweek rankings, DFS targets
articles.body: Seattle Mariners at Boston Red Sox prediction, pick for Tuesday 9/1/26 Last season, the Seattle Mariners and the Boston Red Sox didn’t get to meet in the postseason because of the way the bracket shook out; the fifth-seeded Red Sox played the fourth-seeded New York Yankees for the right to play the top-seeded Toronto Blue Jays, with the second-seeded Mariners sitting on the other side of the bracket from the AL East gauntlet. If Seattle makes the playoffs this season, it’ll likely look similar; Boston and New York seem locked into the fifth and fourth seeds, while the Mariners will either enter as the third-seeded AL West winner or the sixth-seeded Wild Card, awaiting on the other side of the bracket. But it’s getting late early for Seattle; the Red Sox took the opener of the teams’ three-game series in Boston last night, and the Mariners have no more margin for error if they want to make the postseason. Tonight’s middle game, which is set to begin at 6:45 p.m. ET, is a must-win affair for the visitors. Bryan Woo will start for Seattle, and the Red Sox will counter with Jedixson Paez. Let’s break down this plausible (but now highly unlikely) ALCS preview with some odds and lines DraftKings Sportsbook Seattle Mariners at Boston Red Sox Best Bets Boston Red Sox Moneyline (-123) Given that Boston has played like a 114-win team over the last two months, -123 is pretty friendly odds, especially since Woo has not looked like the same pitcher he was last season, when he finished fifth in Cy Young Award voting. Over 7 (-122) Similarly, it’s just not worth backing a low-scoring game when one pitcher has a near-6 ERA on the road and the other is an untested rookie with six earned runs in three career innings. Each of the Red Sox’s last three games have gone over. Seattle Mariners at Boston Red Sox prediction, preview For months, AL West has been right there for the taking, and at 48-49, the Mariners were right in the thick of it at the All-Star break, with FanGraphs giving Seattle roughly a 50-50 chance at ultimately claiming the division. In fact, the Mariners were favored at FanGraphs every day until July 24. However, Seattle went just 11-16 in August, posting the league’s third-worst OPS across the month, and with a six-game deficit in the division and a 5.5-game deficit in the Wild Card race, any rally might well be too little, too late. Even Cal Raleigh’s late-season bounce-back — he’s posted a .324/.425/.971 slash line with seven homers in his last 10 games — hasn’t been enough to lead to wins. In part, that’s because the Mariners’ pitching has been a disaster; their starters have posted a 5.05 ERA since the Midsummer Classic, and their relievers (6.38) have been even worse. A few outliers, including a 22-0 disaster against the Milwaukee Brewers, make the raw numbers look worse than they’ve been on a game-to-game basis, but Seattle’s staff certainly hasn’t been good. Top prospect Kade Anderson has helped stabilize it with two solid starts, but closer Andrés Muñoz needs to get back on track after blowing a save last night. Boston, by contrast, has had a lot more stability over the last couple of months, as a franchise record-tying 15-game winning streak in July vaulted the Red Sox into the playoff picture and they haven’t looked back. In July and August, Boston combined for a 38-16 record, and while catching the Tampa Bay Rays atop the AL East feels unrealistic, the Red Sox still have a shot at securing home-field advantage in the Wild Card series with the Yankees, who they trail by three games. In August, Boston had baseball’s second-best OPS, even though new acquisition Adley Rutschmann has struggled at the plate, and Roman Anthony’s long-awaited return from injury should help sustain that form even when Jahmai Jones (1.363 OPS in 22 games since joining the team) inevitably cools off. Furthermore, the Red Sox have sported both a top-10 rotation and a top-10 bullpen for the season as a whole, with Sonny Gray turning back the clock to serve as the staff ace and Aroldis Chapman maintaining form as one of baseball’s most untouchable relievers at the age of 38. Additionally, Brayan Bello, who was horrendous as a starter, has posted a 1.53 mark across 13 appearances (59.0 innings) as a long reliever. RELATED MLB Betting Splits and Odds for Tuesday, September 1 Woo posted a sub-3 ERA in both 2024 and 2025, finishing fifth in Cy Young Award voting in 2025, but he hasn’t been the same so far this season. In 25 starts, he’s pitched to a 4.36 ERA, including a 5.27 mark since the start of June, and he allowed six earned runs in just four innings in his most recent outing. Still, advanced numbers suggest that he’s gotten somewhat unlucky, as he sports a 67th-percentile expected ERA and 87th-percentile pitching run value. Like he did last season, he’s peppered the zone, ranking in the 95th percentile in walk rate, and that should help limit a Boston team that has earned free passes at a below-average rate. Woo ranks in just the 10th percentile in hard-hit rate and the 21st percentile in average exit velocity, but that might not hurt him too much against the Red Sox, who have thrived on soft contact. However, his location splits are an issue; he’s posted a near-6 ERA away from pitcher’s paradise T-Mobile Park this season, and Boston’s offense has been somewhat more impactful at home. Thankfully for the Mariners, Páez is a completely untested starter. He’s pitched just three innings in MLB, giving up six earned runs across three separate outings with the Chicago White Sox, but since returning to the rotation with Triple-A Worcester, he’s been solid, recording a 2.92 ERA across three starts. Additionally, the Venezuelan made a few solid starts in Double-A, and he had a 2.79 mark across seven starts for High-A Greenville in 2025. He’s enjoyed a relatively high strikeout rate in the minors, fanning 10.9 batters per nine innings in Double-A and Triple-A this season, and that could play well against the whiff-prone Seattle offense. However, Páez has also been slightly more homer-prone than average this season, and despite their overall offensive struggles, the Mariners still have a few mashers, especially with Raleigh seeing the ball well. Páez was significantly better at home across all levels (although he’s never pitched at Fenway Park), and Seattle has had baseball’s fifth-worst road offense. I don’t expect a star-level performance from Páez, but four innings and two earned runs seems like a reasonable expectation. Seattle Mariners at Boston Red Sox pick, best bet Best Bet: Boston Red Sox Moneyline (-123) Even with a potentially shaky Páez on the mound for his starting debut, I trust the Red Sox’s bullpen to step up once the starters leave the game, and Woo’s road form is quite poor. Strong Lean: Over 7 (-122) Páez likely won’t escape entirely without damage, and 15 of Woo’s 25 starts have included at least seven runs. Even for the Mariners, seven total runs is a low bar. articles.title: Is Jordan Mason or Aaron Jones the Vikings’ No. 1 RB heading into Week 1?
articles.excerpt: Alex Hunter analyzes the Vikings' backfield of Jordan Mason and Aaron Jones heading into Week 1 of the NFL season. The post Is Jordan Mason or Aaron Jones the Vikings’ No. 1 RB heading into Week 1? appeared first on DraftKings Network .
articles.source_type: Captain picks ranked with reasoning, gameweek rankings, DFS targets
articles.body: Is Jordan Mason or Aaron Jones the Vikings' No. 1 RB heading into Week 1? Once again, it’s a debate on who will be the lead back for the Vikings this season between Mason and Jones. Jones sits atop the depth chart, but will the 31-year-old actually be the RB1 over the 27-year-old Mason heading into the regular season? First off, let’s look at how these backs were used and performed last season. Last Season Jones has always been one of the most efficient rushers in the league during his career, but he slowed down in his ninth season in 2025, averaging a career-worst 4.2 YPC. Mason was more effective at 4.8 YPC, but this was also a career-low for the 27-year-old. Despite Mason being more productive on the ground, Jones held an edge in rushing usage. In the 11 games these two backs played together, Jones out carried Mason 105-85. However, Mason was trusted more in the red zone, outcarrying Jones 15-10 in that area. As a result, Mason rushed for six touchdowns while Jones only found the paydirt twice with his legs. In the passing game, Jones was the unquestioned primary receiving back over Mason. Jones saw 33 targets on 175 routes, whereas Mason only saw eight targets on 65 routes. Overall, Jones outsnapped Mason 331-207. As you can see, when both these backs were healthy last season, Jones was the lead back in every department, outside of red zone rushing, but will this continue this season? Week 1 Outlook After being the lead back last season, Jones drew the start in the lone preseason game that he and Mason both were active for this summer. That being said, these two backs usage was nearly identical. Jones saw three carries and one target on five snaps while Mason saw three carries on four snaps. Albeit a preseason game, this may be an indicator that Jones and Mason are going to split the rushing workload pretty evenly this season, which makes sense, after Mason was the more productive rusher a year ago. If Mason will see more carries, it’s hard to imagine he doesn’t retain his role as the primary rusher in the red zone, giving him more touchdown equity over Jones. Although, Jones should continue to be the main pass catching back for this offense, given the major difference in their receiving usage last season and simply because Jones has always been a reliable pass catcher throughout his career, compared to Mason, who has never done much in this department. This should once again be a two-man backfield with positive game scripts favoring Mason and negative game scripts favoring Jones. For next Sunday’s regular season opener vs. the Packers, the Vikings are a 1.5-point home favorite on DraftKings Sportsbook . This is an optimal setup for Mason to produce. Minnesota will likely want to rely on their run game if they get ahead and while it likely won’t be by much, Mason should finish this game with more touches, even if Jones technically gets the start. Make no mistake, though, this backfield will be tough to predict on a weekly basis when both Mason and Jones are healthy, and even if Mason begins 2026 with a better performance in Week 1, that doesn’t mean he is the Vikings’ RB1 for the season.
