articles.body: 2026 NFL Win Total Prediction, Pick: Atlanta Falcons Mediocrity has been a consistent theme for the Atlanta Falcons in recent years. For the first time in a while, though, the team knocked the hiring of a head coach out of the park and could be positioned to turn things around. There are plenty of standout pieces on offense, but the quarterback and the defense do remain more uncertain when evaluating team success. Now, the question is whether Kevin Stefanski will live up to his status as a two-time Coach of the Year winner. Here’s a look at the Falcons’ win total over/under for the 2026-27 NFL season with a top betting pick. Atlanta Falcons 2026 win total, best bet When the Falcons hired Kevin Stefanski as the franchise’s new head coach, there was plenty to be excited about. The two-time Coach of the Year kept the Cleveland Browns relevant for several years even despite operating with his hands tied at times, and he’s well-regarded as one of the NFL’s better names in terms of the coaching hierarchy. Giving him Bijan Robinson, Drake London and Kyle Pitts had, and still has, many fans salivating. It’s tough to not get excited, but then you consider the rest of the context surrounding this team. The quarterback play is a massive unknown. Incumbent starter Michael Penix Jr. didn’t live up to expectations in the pros before tearing his ACL again, so how he fares coming off the injury is anyone’s guess. The team signed former Miami Dolphin Tua Tagovailoa to compete for the starting job, but his limitations are known and his preseason performance was one for the ages – not in a good way, either. When some fans are clamoring for an UDFA like Jack Strand, it says a lot about the situation under center. Then there’s the defense. Atlanta has been relatively pedestrian in that regard over the last few years, ranking 15th in yards per game (326.6) and 19th in points per game allowed (23.6) last season. While the Falcons’ pass rush was excellent with a franchise-record 57 sacks in 2025, two key EDGE talents are facing shortened campaigns – Jalon Walker tore an ACL and will miss the full season while James Pearce Jr. will serve an eight-game suspension to begin 2026. The club signed help in the front seven, adding Za’Darius Smith, Christian Harris and Samson Ebukam at linebacker while trading for defensive tackle Gervon Dexter Jr.; losing a combined 16 sacks between Walker and Pearce is tough, though. On the back end, A.J. Terrell and Jessie Bates reprise their roles as the top to players in the secondary. Drafting Avieon Terrell, the brother of A.J., also brings a high-upside pick into the mix. There’s room for this unit to improve this year, especially with Stefanski in the mix and Jeff Ulbrich retained at defensive coordinator. They’ll just have to prove it while overcoming the loss of Walker and weathering the storm of Pearce’s suspension. RELATED 2026 Fantasy Football Rankings: Top 160 players for PPR drafts and redraft leagues DraftKings Sportsbook lists the Falcons’ over/under total at 7.5 wins, with the under favored at -140 odds and the over at +120. Atlanta does see the benefit of playing in a weak NFC South, so that’s a bit of a boost in terms of the win total. No team in this division was above .500 last season, with all three of the Carolina Panthers, Tampa Bay Buccaneers and Falcons finishing 8-9. The New Orleans Saints also went 6-11 last year. There’s not a strong case for improvement from Carolina, but it’s fairly easy to see a world where both Tampa Bay and New Orleans wind up with a winning record. Due to that weak division, the Falcons do have the fourth-easiest schedule in 2026 based on opponents’ 2025 winning percentage (0.465). That certainly sets the team up to play competitive football, but the question is twofold – can they trust either of these quarterbacks, and can the defense stay afloat without two of its top talents on the edge. Those tasks may be easier said than done. Assuming the Saints and Bucs get back to winning games in the NFC South, the Falcons should stay under this win total of 7.5 in 2026. articles.title: Beto Departs Everton
articles.excerpt: Everton can confirm Beto has left the Club to join Serie A side Fiorentina on a permanent transfer for an undisclosed fee. The 28-year-old striker – who signed for Everton in August 2023 – played 113 times across all competitions for the Toffees, netting 25 goals and proving a popular figure with Evertonians. After signing from Udinese three years ago, Beto scored on his Blues debut against Doncaster Rovers in the Carabao Cup. His first of 20 Premier League goals arrived in December 2023, striking against Newcastle United in a memorable 3-0 victory at Goodison Park. In February 2025, Beto – a Guinea Bissau international – opened the scoring in Goodison’s last-ever Men’s Merseyside derby – a dramatic 2-2 draw on an iconic night under the lights at the Grand Old Lady. Everyone connected with Everton thanks Beto for his dedication, commitment and service throughout his time at the Club and wishes him all the best for the next chapter of his career in Italy.

Sign up Odds by TRANSFER DEADLINE WATCH: Premier League transfer deadline show Premier League Videos The 2 Robbies Multiple reports: Enzo Fernandez to sign for Manchester City in huge $169 million transfer Joe Prince-Wright Joe Prince-Wright Published September 1, 2026 05:06 PM Facebook Twitter Email Enzo Fernandez is finally heading to Manchester City, as multiple reports claim a British record-equalling transfer fee of $169 million has been agreed with Chelsea on transfer deadline day. Alexander Isak’s move from Newcastle United to Liverpool last summer set that record, and Fernandez’s move is set to equal it. Per David Ornstein Fabrizio Romano Sky in Italy and Sky in Germany , Enzo Fernandez has now been given permission by Chelsea to travel to Manchester to complete his medical at Man City and sign his new contract. The Argentina international, 25, has been linked with a move to City all summer and it looks to finally be happening. What will Enzo Fernandez bring to Manchester City? Fernandez will link up with his former boss at Chelsea, Enzo Maresca, and completes City’s massive overhaul of their midfield after they already spent $260 million on Elliot Anderson and Ayyoub Bouaddi this summer. He is a fine individual player and City are constructing a totally different midfield — legends Rodri and Bernardo Silva left for Barcelona and Real Madrid respectively this summer — as they aim to get back on track and win the Premier League this season. Having Fernandez’s goals, assists and tenacity driving them forward from central midfield will certainly be a huge part of a new era at City. While Anderson’s poise on the ball and Bouaddi’s energy and ability to win the ball back will mesh so well with Fernandez’s main strengths. In theory, City now have one of the best midfield trios in the game. And they should because it’s cost them $430 million this summer. Sign up Odds by TRANSFER DEADLINE WATCH: Premier League transfer deadline show Premier League Videos The 2 Robbies Report: Everton’s move for USA’s Folarin Balogun in doubt ahead of transfer deadline Joe Prince-Wright Joe Prince-Wright Published September 1, 2026 05:06 PM Facebook Twitter Email A report from L’Equipe in France says that Folarin Balogun’s potential deadline day move to Everton could be off. And another report from RMC Sport in France says that it is due to Balogun failing a medical at Everton. As of right now, Balogun’s deal potentially collapsing means that Monaco won’t be able to sign Mexican international Erik Lira from Cruz Azul as they won’t have enough non-EU roster spots available. A report in Mexico from TNT Sports also states that with Balogun’s departure from Monaco now looking unlikely, Lira can’t arrive at the Ligue 1 club. It was expected that Balogun’s departure would allow Lira to arrive, but something has obviously hit a snag with Everton’s potential move for Balogun. MORE — USMNT transfers: Where are USA stars playing in Europe? Everton have already sold striker Beto to Fiorentina on deadline day to make way for Balogun’s arrival, so it could be quite a disappointment on deadline day for David Moyes’ side. Especially if star playmaker Iliman Ndiaye moves on to Manchester City too and their attack is further depleted. Even with Jack Grealish reportedly arriving on loan, Everton’s attack would still be lighter than at the start of the summer. Is this a good move for Balogun? Yes, this is a very good fit for him and if he’s going to head back to the Premier League he has to be playing regularly. Balogun scored 18 goals with four assists for Monaco between Ligue 1 and the UEFA Champions League, last season and he scored thrice for the USMNT at the World Cup, adding an assist against Australia. He would automatically become Everton’s top striker, playing in front of Thierno Barry. Barry is a fine striker and gets into some great positions, but he is still young and raw and his finishing isn’t of the same standard as the USMNT star. For many years now Everton have been creating lots of chances but haven’t been able to put them away. Balogun’s clinical and calm finishing would be perfect for them. After coming through the ranks at Arsenal but never quite being able to break into the first team, Balogun’s move to French football has worked out really well after prolific spells at Reims and AS Monaco. Now seems like the perfect time for him to move back to England’s top-flight and take the next step in his career after his superb World Cup for the USA this summer. The Dolphins announced the signings of eight players to their practice squad, including a pair of former first-round picks. Pass rusher Clelin Ferrell and defensive lineman Mazi Smith entered the NFL as first-rounders. The Jets cut Smith on Sunday, and Ferrell was with the Dolphins in training camp before his release. The Dolphins also signed inside linebacker Liam Anderson, edge Amari Gainer, defensive lineman Jordan Miller, wide receiver Will Sheppard, cornerback Jaylin Simpson and tight end Tre Watson to their practice squad. Sign up AFC East Buffalo Bills Miami Dolphins New England Patriots New York Jets AFC North Baltimore Ravens Cincinnati Bengals Cleveland Browns Pittsburgh Steelers AFC South Houston Texans Indianapolis Colts Jacksonville Jaguars Tennessee Titans AFC West Denver Broncos Kansas City Chiefs Las Vegas Raiders Los Angeles Chargers NFC East Dallas Cowboys New York Giants Philadelphia Eagles Washington Commanders NFC North Chicago Bears Detroit Lions Green Bay Packers Minnesota Vikings NFC South Atlanta Falcons Carolina Panthers New Orleans Saints Tampa Bay Buccaneers NFC West Arizona Cardinals Los Angeles Rams San Francisco 49ers Seattle Seahawks AFC East Buffalo Bills Miami Dolphins New England Patriots New York Jets AFC North Baltimore Ravens Cincinnati Bengals Cleveland Browns Pittsburgh Steelers AFC South Houston Texans Indianapolis Colts Jacksonville Jaguars Tennessee Titans AFC West Denver Broncos Kansas City Chiefs Las Vegas Raiders Los Angeles Chargers NFC East Dallas Cowboys New York Giants Philadelphia Eagles Washington Commanders NFC North Chicago Bears Detroit Lions Green Bay Packers Minnesota Vikings NFC South Atlanta Falcons Carolina Panthers New Orleans Saints Tampa Bay Buccaneers NFC West Arizona Cardinals Los Angeles Rams San Francisco 49ers Seattle Seahawks Rumor Mill Peacock PFT Shop Jeff Hafley excited for the chance to develop young players Josh Alper Josh Alper Published September 1, 2026 05:00 PM Facebook Twitter Email After the Dolphins hired head coach Jeff Hafley and General Manager Jon-Erik Sullivan, it quickly became clear that the two men were charting a new course for the organization. They have salary cap space taken up by a number of veterans who were traded or released during the offseason and the replacements on the roster all skew much younger. The Dolphins had the youngest initial 53-man roster in the league, which fits with Hafley’s stated priorities for his first year in Miami. Hafley said his goal is to build “something real powerful moving forward” and that the team’s ability to do that will matter more than their won-loss record . Hafley returned to the theme of development during a Tuesday press conference when asked about having such a young roster. “My expectation as we started this thing, I would say that I figured we would be young,” Hafley said, via a transcript from the team. “Whether or not how young, I really didn’t get into, but yeah, we knew we’d be a young team. And that’s all along, we’ve talked about developing and I’ve talked about the process and I’ve talked about the foundation and I’ve talked about the culture. Usually you start those things and you’re pretty young. I mean, you can look at that and say, ‘oh, we’re so young.’ I look at that and I’m excited about that. We are excited to develop that. We’re excited for the hunger that they have. You mix in some good vets in the pieces that I’ve said all along that we already have here, and I’m excited to get the process started. And again, that’s with the intent to win games, right? I think everybody has misconstrued that with the end result, winning, but it’s going to be fun to get these guys going.” A full evaluation of the job Hafley and Sullivan did in setting the kind of foundation needed for future success won’t come until the end of the season, but the ride will be an easier one if there are some early signs that the Dolphins are on the right path. articles.body: Milwaukee Brewers vs. Chicago Cubs prediction, pick for Tuesday 9/1/26 The Cubs (78-60) took care of business in dominant fashion on Monday. Chicago racked up 17 runs and a whopping nine homers during a blowout win over the Brewers (85-53). Milwaukee, responsible for the best record in baseball, will be eager to turn the page on Tuesday. Can the visitors even up this series tonight at Wrigley Field? The Cubs are favorites (-123) over the Brewers; the over/under is set at ten runs . Below, I’ve laid out my preview, prediction, and best bet for Tuesday’s showdown between Milwaukee and Chicago on DraftKings Sportsbook Brewers vs. Cubs pick, best bet today Cubs ML (-123) : Chicago, fresh off of Monday’s rout, looks the part of a World Series contender. It’s difficult to envision baseball’s highest-scoring offense slowing down tonight at home against a middling arm such as Gasser. Brewers vs. Cubs prediction, preview Robert Gasser will get the nod this evening for the visitors. Over 82.1 innings of work (15 starts), the right-hander has notched a 4.59 ERA, 1.30 WHIP and 78 strikeouts (8.5 K/9). Despite middling numbers, the 27-year-old isn’t a complete pushover on the mound. He’s allowed three earned runs or less in six of his last seven appearances. Still, it’s difficult to get too excited when it comes to Gasser’s chances tonight. He ranks inside the 40th percentile or worse in xERA (4.22), xBA (.253), chase rate (29.4%) and ground ball rate (32.8%). That last statistic could prove consequential on Tuesday. Gasser’s inability to keep the ball on the ground doesn’t bode well heading into today’s matchup. The Cubs are one of baseball’s most power-happy clubs, leading the majors in home runs (196). In fact, the North Siders smacked 62 dingers during August. That’s a National League record for one club over the course of a single month. Chicago hitters have posted a 29.0% fly ball rate, third-highest in baseball. Gasser’s knack for giving up the long ball (1.4 HR/9) makes navigating tonight’s opponent a difficult task. MVP candidate Pete Crow-Armstrong and third baseman Alex Bregman are both swinging hot bats. RELATED Best Home Run Props for Tuesday 9/1/26 As for the other side, Matthew Boyd will take the hill tonight. The former All-Star has battled injuries for much of 2025. However, when healthy, he remains an above-average arm. The southpaw has notched a 3.99 ERA, 1.22 WHIP and 76 strikeouts (7.1 K/9) during 97.0 innings of work. That’s not to say the veteran has been perfect; he’s surrendered at least four runs in three of his last five appearances. However, he remains above-average when it comes to limiting free passes (2.8 BB/9). Whether or not he’s at his best, Boyd should provide Chicago with some length. The lefty has tossed six innings or more in nine of his previous ten outings. Milwaukee’s lineup, while unorthodox, gets the job done. Despite a lack of home run power, this group is at its best when stringing together base hits. The Brewers are third in runs scored (686), third in batting average (.255) and second in on-base percentage (.338). However, tonight’s contest could present some difficulty for the NL Central leaders. The Brew Crew have put up a .700 OPS against left-handed pitching, 13th-worst in the big leagues. Best Bet: Cubs ML (-123) Gasser doesn’t inspire much confidence. His propensity for fly balls should have this homer-happy Cubs lineup licking its chops on Tuesday. Boyd is far from an ace, but this isn’t the most intimidating matchup. The Brewers haven’t been the most dangerous group at the plate against lefties. Equipped with the superior starter and deeper lineup, Chicago makes plenty of sense this evening at home. articles.title: FPL Gameweek 2 Review – Analysis of Every Fixture
articles.excerpt: FPL Gameweek 2 Review – Every Fixture Analysed Greetings all, and welcome to a full, detailed, and indeed hopefully helpful review of FPL Gameweek 2. It was certainly a high scoring week. I (Joe) know that because everyone around me seemed to be scoring 100+ pts, while I meandered along with my pedestrian 88pts. Bruno […] The post FPL Gameweek 2 Review – Analysis of Every Fixture appeared first on Full90 FPL .
articles.source_type: Gameweek previews, transfer tips, captaincy corner, fixture focus
articles.body: FPL Gameweek 2 Review - Analysis of Every Fixture Skip to content FPL Gameweek 2 Review - Every Fixture Analysed Greetings all, and welcome to a full, detailed, and indeed hopefully helpful review of FPL Gameweek 2. It was certainly a high scoring week. I (Joe) know that because everyone around me seemed to be scoring 100+ pts, while I meandered along with my pedestrian 88pts. Bruno and Haaland – i.e. 2/3 of the most highly owned players (JP being the other), and the two captaincy options – obviously made for the bulk of that. We also got returns from a ton of other widely-owned fellas though – Raya, Calafiori, Gabriel, Mbeumo, Rogers, Palmer, JP himself, DCL, and so on and so forth. If only all of the players that loads of us own would score every week, this game would be easy. Anyway, enough faffing about. Let’s get on with the Gameweek 2 review! FPL Gameweek 2 Review In an incredible stroke of creative genius, I’ve decided to go through all the weekend’s games in order. Crazy, I know, but it just might work. Here are the main FPL takeaways for every Gameweek 2 fixture. Crystal Palace 1 – 4 Man City I wouldn’t read too much into this game for Palace City got off to a slow start this season, between GW1 and the community shield, but they’re obviously one of the best attacks in the league, so getting battered by them doesn’t really mean anything. It’s not exactly great to still have not scored a goal for themselves (this one being an OG) after 2 games. But Everton away, then City, aren’t the easiest opening fixtures. We’ll learn a lot more about them in the next few games – Fulham, Ipswich, Leeds, Forest – against sides far more on their level. I will also note that their schedule gets very busy, very quickly now. They’ve got a League Cup game after next weekend, and Europa League games consistently thereafter, so they’re basically playing twice a week for ages now. I would be… concerned about how they balance that with the Prem, since their squad isn’t great, and they could well be a great team to target once the Europa League does start up . Losing these two games doesn’t immediately make that so, however. As noted, City’s attack was always going to click sooner rather than later, and here it clicked in style. I thought no- Haaland was ridiculous before the season, and him grabbing two goals here – ahead of an incredible fixture next week – hardly changed my mind. Given that he has Man U’s crap defence, Sunderland home, then Liverpool’s crap defence coming up too, I’d get him in immediately, if you went without to start the year. Cherki is unsurprisingly one of the most transferred-in players right now, and I’ve got no problem with it. Benching him for the first game was bizarre, but that’s not happening again any time soon. If you’ve got a City spot free, he’d be my number one target on their team, and one of my top targets overall. I won’t be moving Semenyo to him myself… but I wish I’d just picked him to start with, right now. I’d also stick by the City defence . They haven’t cleaned yet, but they have held both opponents to less than 1xG… and obviously you have to start them all against Coventry anyway. I wouldn’t panic on Anderson either. He hit 14 DC’s this week, and has a solid 0.34 xGI/game so far, so attacking returns should come to back up those DefCon points. (And, again, you shouldn’t be selling any City players before Coventry at home… obviously). Liverpool 2 – 2 Notts Forest I can’t say Liverpool’s actual production looks any different under Iraola. They started last season all over the place, relying on pretty late goals (in that case, to get wins), and they’re doing the same thing again. The defence still looks crap. 4 goals conceded in their first 2 games, and they gave up a whopping 2.88 xG to Forest (including a pen, obviously). Unfortunately, they also play Ipswich next week. I doubt they’ll clean in that game either, based on how rubbish they are at the back and Ipswich scoring 2 goals in both their games so far, but you probably have to just hold onto Virgil anyway and pray. They looked better going forward in this game than against Newcastle (not that they could’ve looked much worse). Isak even remembered how to put the ball in the net! Admittedly it was absolutely put on a plate for him, but hey, we don’t care about how easy the chances are in FPL, as long as our forwards score. I’m holding him for Ipswich and Fulham, then will strongly reassess when their fixtures turn drastically. Wirtz looked better too, and I’d also hold him. He had one goal disallowed, hit the bar with another shot, and got the assist for Munoz’s goal. Speaking of – I like the look of Munoz quite a bit. I didn’t actually think he looked that amazing when he came on against Newcastle, but he still got the ‘assist’ (won a pen), and took his goal very well here. He looks very good value at 6.5, particularly as he’s presumably nailed there with Barcola to play on the left. I’d be hesitant about bringing him in though – since again you only get 2 good fixtures – unless you’re planning a wildcard around GW5 or 6. Finally, Szobszlai is driving me crazy as a non-owner. First he gets bailed out of a GW1 blank by a last minute pen. Then he gets shifted to RB this game after Frimpong went off (which helped his DC’s last season) and promptly hit on DefCons. Sigh. Obviously you’re holding him if you’ve got him. And if I’d known the Frimpong experiment was going to last less than 2 games, I’d have got him too. I just wanted to have a little moan. (I’ll be saying this a lot, but…) it’s too early to judge Forest yet. Glasner is a good manager, and I’d assume they’ll finish around midtable, and be a solid team. They did well here… but they also just lost two games in a row to Leeds (including in the League Cup), not scoring a goal either time, so let’s wait and see. MGW is obviously great, and I’m somewhat wishing I’d taken him over Semenyo for 0.5 less. He gets Spurs at home next, Villa away (meh), but then Coventry home and Palace. If you are desperate to rid yourself of an Mbeumo type, for example (not that I would be), he’d probably be my 2nd choice after Cherki. I’d also have Neco Williams on the early wildcard watchlist. No clean sheets yet obviously, but he did have an assist here and hit on DC’s, and is only 5.0 (the same price as stupid Van Hecke, for example, who this idiot picked instead). Coventry 0 – 1 Hull One for the bench boosters out there… and that’s about it. Coventry are the worst team in the league right now, and we should target them mercilessly. Hull haven’t been as bad as we all expected so far… but let’s not get carried away. It’s been two games, and I’d still also have them pencilled in as one of the best matchups around until we’ve seen them prove us wrong a few more times. Bournemouth 1 – 1 Everton Bournemouth have been the unluckiest team so far this season, losing 4pts already in extra time. It’s too early yet to decide whether losing Iraola has actually affected them or not. They’ve been fine in both games, and had plenty of shots here (15, for a 2.26 xG). I’d still roughly have them pegged as a good-not-great team, and a tricky matchup when they’re at home, until further notice. It’s too early to actually consider Scott , but he’d be somewhere on my budget midfielder watchlist going forward. He hit a very good 386 DC’s last season, and got 5 attacking returns on a 6.74 xGI. One to keep an eye on, especially if you’re looking to wildcard around GW 7 or so, when their fixtures get better and we’ll have several more weeks of data on him. All hail James Tarkowski , our FPL Defensive Lord and Saviour. You just have to love him. He cleaned in his first game, and missed his DC’s by 1. He hit on DC’s this game, and got an injury time goal, and got 2 bonus points, good for a whopping 12pts total. He is currently the 14th-highest owned defender, miles behind the likes of VVD who costs 0.5 more. I am baffled. Aside from that, I’d only note the return of Garner for Everton. He only got 61mins here, as he continues to work back from injury, but still managed to rack up 10 DC’s in that time. He’ll almost certainly be in my wildcard team, whenever that happens. Spurs 0 – 2 Newcastle I’d love to pile on Spurs , but they weren’t exactly awful here. They actually looked pretty good going forward, and got 16 shots off, with 5 on target. Newcastle got 2 shots on target… and scored with both. I thought they’d be fine defensively before the season, after their heavy spending there. Obviously, as of now, I was wrong. I still think they’ll gel and be fine before too long, but for now they’re definitely one of the better teams in the league to target, as they were for much of last season. More on them next week in general, once their latest avalanche of transfer dealings have been settled, and we begin to have some vague idea of who’s actually going to start for them – particularly up top. Newcastle are basically the anti-Spurs. They also made tons of signings, most people thought they’d struggle this season, and they’ve actually been fine. I thought they played very well against Liverpool, and were incredibly unlucky not to win. Now they’ve come and nicked a 2-0 away to Spurs – nice! They’ve also got a few intriguing FPL options already. Hall is currently only 5.0 (though will definitely rise), which is cheap in today’s FPL. He’s hit on DC’s in both games so far, has had 0.34 and 0.35 xGI, and even got 3 bonus points at the weekend. Obviously the latter isn’t going to happen often, but if he’s going to get DefCons and threaten attacking returns, at that price, he’ll be a great pick. They’ve also got good defensive fixtures basically all the way through to Arsenal in Gameweek 11. I like him a lot… and it’s very tempting to bin stupid Van Hecke for him right now. I don’t know what the hell’s gotten into Elanga , but I like it. He was awful last season, and has been brilliant in both games so far. They’re basically just constantly pinging balls over the top for him, which – given that he’s rapid – is working out very well. Two goals already, super cheap at only 6.1, and their upcoming fixtures are good for attackers too. He’d probably be my top pick among budget mids right now. Wissa also appears to have been resuccitated. He was excellent against Liverpool (1 xG, 1 assist, and his all-round play was very good), and took his goal brilliantly here. He’s also super cheap, at 6.1, and obviously has those same very good fixtures. I’d just about take him over DCL right now if you had neither, given those fixtures, but wouldn’t actually make that move obviously. Chelsea 4 – 3 Brighton There’s not much I can say here that you don’t already know. Chelsea’s attack is brilliant and their defence is rubbish. 7-5 aggregate score, across their first two games – ridiculous. All three of the big hitters – Palmer, JP, and Rogers – look great. I still wouldn’t bring them in for Arsenal away (though I’m sure many, many people will), but would gladly load up on as many of them as you can straight after that… particularly as ‘straight after that’ in this case means Hull at home. The defence will (probably) get better, especially when Caicedo is fit again. For now it’s obviously a complete stay-away though, regardless of fixtures. I’d continue to back Brighton as being very good this season. Obviously they dismantled Villa, and they got 14 shots off here, 5 on target, and had a ridiculous 75% of the ball. I still don’t particularly fancy any of their players in FPL (though congrats to the Gross owners for getting completely bailed out at the end!). But I do think they have to rank as one of the harder matchups to go against right now, especially for your defenders (and let’s not forget they were excellent defensively last season too). If he doesn’t have one before the season starts, he’s not sure if he’ll be on the field. Asked today if he’ll play Week One without a new deal, Porter was noncommittal. “I don’t know. I would have to talk to the guys upstairs and my agents about that one,” Porter said. Some of Porter’s answers to reporters’ questions were contradictory: Porter was just activated from the physically unable to perform list, and when asked if he’ll play if he’s healthy, Porter answered, “Yeah, for sure, maybe.” Porter did participate in today’s walk-through practice but said that’s not any indication of what he’ll be doing when the Steelers open the season on Sunday, September 13, against the Falcons. “I really can’t speak too much to the future, but today I was out there, running with the guys, still trying to get back fully, but we’re going to try to take it day by day for the most part, and that’s the same page me and coach have been on so far,” Porter said. Porter said his contract situation has weighed on him but he thinks he has the support of the people in the Steelers’ facility. “It’s been tough, not going to lie,” Porter said. “It’s my first go around this, but I mean, it’s been also great because I have all my guys with me, all the coaches and players really on my side, understand everything about the business side of things. . . . It’s been a little bit tough, but at the end of the day, it is what it is.” The Steelers say they won’t negotiate with Porter during the regular season, which means they have less than two weeks to get a deal done. And Porter is sending a message that if they don’t get a deal done, he may not be there when the season starts. Add favorite players, teams, and leagues with an NBCUniversal Profile Continue

Sign up No. 5 Cobolli rallies from two sets down at the US Open as play picks up after a morning of rain Associated Press Associated Press Published September 1, 2026 04:32 PM Facebook Twitter Email NEW YORK, NEW YORK - SEPTEMBER 01: Flavio Cobolli in action against Francisco Comesana during a Men’s Singles match on Day Three of the 2026 US Open at USTA Billie Jean King National Tennis Center on Tuesday, September 1, 2026 in Flushing, NY. (Photo by Jeff Dean/USTA via Getty Images) USTA via Getty Images NEW YORK (AP) — Flavio Cobolli rallied from two sets down to win his first-round match at the U.S. Open on Tuesday, avoiding another early upset on the men’s side. The No. 5 seed and French Open runner-up beat Francisco Comesana 3-6, 2-6, 6-3, 6-4, 6-4, finishing his match that lasted 4 hours, 12 minutes not long after some sun had broken through the clouds and allowed play to start on all the outside courts after a morning of rain. Cobolli made his first career two-set comeback to avoid joining No. 4 seed Novak Djokovic and No. 10 Arthur Fils among early losers in a men’s draw that was already missing top-ranked Jannik Sinner, Cobolli’s fellow Italian who was unable to play in the tournament because of a right knee injury. He said he took a bathroom break after the second set and decided to change everything. “So I changed all the dress that I started with today and it works,” Cobolli said. “In Grand Slams it’s never done. You have to fight until the last point.” No. 9 seed Taylor Fritz, the 2024 runner-up, rolled to a 6-3, 6-2, 6-4 victory over 18-year-old fellow American Darwin Blanch. Madison Keys was the only other player to move into the second round early in a tournament where rain threatened to hamper the schedule for a couple days. Showers that began Monday night and would possibly be on and off through the middle of the week delayed play on all the outer courts, allowing for action only in Arthur Ashe Stadium and Louis Armstrong Stadium, which have retractable roofs. Keys, the No. 22 seed, beat 19-year-old Alina Korneeva 7-5, 6-4 in the leadoff match in Ashe. The 2017 U.S. Open runner-up was knocked off in the first round last year in Flushing Meadows. “It’s always tough playing someone young and up and coming, and they’re going after their shots,” Keys said. “And it’s so hard to play a first round of a Grand Slam, so nervous and just wanting to do so well. So, really happy I was able to kind of fight through that and win today.” Play finally began outdoors in the middle of the afternoon. Among those who finally got going were No. 2 seed Elena Rybakina, No. 12 Belinda Bencic and No. 32 Maria Sakkari. Rybakina has multiple routes to the No. 1 ranking at the U.S. Open. She was facing American Thea Frodin, a 17-year-old from California who was the body double for actor Demi Singleton, who played Serena Williams, in the 2021 film “King Richard.” Coco Gauff, the 2023 U.S. Open champion, No. 17 Alex Eala, and men’s No. 1 seed Alexander Zverev were scheduled at night on the third and last day of the first round. Keys was broken when serving for the match with a 5-3 lead but recovered to break back in the next game and finish up the match. The American lost to Sloane Stephens in the 2017 U.S. Open final and returned to Flushing Meadows last year after winning the first major title of her career by beating No. 1 Aryna Sabalenka in the Australian Open final. But what started out as a great year fell flat at the finish after Keys was stunned by Renata Zarazua of Mexico in the first round of last year’s U.S. Open after committing 89 unforced errors. Chelsea are shipping out an underwhelming duo, but why are Spurs so eager to take them? (Image credit: Getty Images) Facebook Pinterest Email Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Even after relegation scares in back-to-back seasons, the most pessimistic of Spurs supporters probably wouldn't have predicted being rock bottom after two games, with a -5 goal difference. Or perhaps they would have, from recent trauma build-up. Still, Tottenham Hotspur ’s summer incomings have been impressive, and arrived with an expectation of achieving European football this season. But the North London club, at best, could be considered slightly overzealous in regard to its expenditure this summer, and their haste in helping to solve Chelsea ’s wage bill issue is worrying, to say the least. Tottenham Hotspur secure services of Chelsea duo, but why? Spurs are in the process of signing Tosin Adarabioyo (Image credit: Robbie Jay Barratt - AMA/Getty Images) Ahead of Tuesday’s transfer deadline at 11pm BST, Spurs look set to secure the services of Chelsea duo Mykhailo Mudryk and Tosin Adarabioyo. Their London rivals are willing to shift the pair in an effort to solve their wage bill issues, and Spurs seem all too eager to aid them in this regard. Xabi Alonso has a fine squad to work with this season, and he's successfully shifted deadwood (Image credit: Getty Images) Mudryk will sign on a season-long loan, while Adarabioyo is expected to move on a permanent transfer for around £7 million — combined, they recorded zero goals and zero assists in 23 Premier League appearances last season. Chelsea, in contrast to the North London club, are fourth in the Premier League table, having taken two wins from two against Brighton and Fulham — blockbuster 3-2 and 4-3 victories. The best features, fun and footballing quizzes, straight to your inbox every week. Last season, they finished in 10th, accumulating just nine additional points to Spurs’ tally of 41, which saw them capable of being relegated all the way until the Premier League’s final gameweek. If you stare hard enough, you’ll find that there was likely an expectation for the two clubs to perform as peers this season, yet Tottenham Hotspur have, rather alarmingly, found themselves vacuuming the crumbs up off the floor in Chelsea’s kitchen. And that should worry fans of the North London club — after an initially serious summer in which Spurs secured the services of Sandro Tonali, Mateus Fernandes, Savio, Jan Paul van Hecke, Omar Marmoush, and further Premier League-proven talent, this is a concerning sign. Omar Marmoush has also arrived on loan, but that is entirely different (Image credit: Alamy) It’s one thing to take players from Manchester City ; Enzo Maresca’s men will likely challenge for the Premier League title this season, and the Savio-Marmoush duo bring multiple top-level seasons of experience under Pep Guardiola’s wing to London. But a pair of 'B squad' players from Chelsea with little observable Premier League impact? What benefits could this duo bring that outweigh the positive impact it will have on the Blues’ wage bill, and their rivals’ ability to compete? How good can Mudryk and Tosin possibly be, for paying £7m and the pair’s wages, to prevent Chelsea from getting the last laugh here? During a summer in which Spurs appeared determined to turn a page, their performances on the pitch have scarcely improved, and their transfer business will conclude on a sour note. And while fans of the North London club will surely stay focused on seeing the likes of Fernandes, Tonali, Savio and Marmoush come good, they should keep a closer eye on the duo that Chelsea appear overwhelmingly likely to have fleeced them for. articles.title: BREAKING: Man City agree £125million deal to sign Chelsea star Fernandez
articles.excerpt: City are matching the British transfer record to sign the Argentina international.
articles.source_type: Weekly five-players-to-buy and players-to-avoid pieces, injury-doubt round-ups
articles.body: BREAKING: Man City agree £125million deal to sign Chelsea star Fernandez Skip to content Football News Premier League News BREAKING: Man City agree £125million deal to sign Chelsea star Fernandez City are matching the British transfer record to sign the Argentina international. Nicholas McGee Last Update: 54 minutes ago 3 min read Add us as a preferred source on Google Manchester City have reportedly agreed a £125million deal to sign Enzo Fernandez from Chelsea The Athletic’s David Ornstein reported that the two clubs have come to terms on a fee that matches the British record Liverpool paid to Newcastle United to sign Alexander Isak on deadline day last year. Fernandez has been given permission to travel to Manchester for a medical. City’s pursuit of Fernandez has been one of the defining sagas of the transfer window, with the club determined to reunite former Chelsea boss Enzo Maresca with the Argentina international to complete their midfield rebuild. Table of Contents City end saga by completing midfield rebuild Will Chelsea fill Fernandez void before deadline? City end saga by completing midfield rebuild Chelsea imposed a deadline of August 14 for City to lodge a bid for Fernandez meeting their £120m valuation and indicated they expected him to remain at Stamford Bridge after their Premier League rivals did not do so. But City did not drop their interest in Fernandez, who, after making a substitute appearance in Chelsea’s season-opening win at Fulham, was left out of their EFL Cup victory over Luton Town and last Sunday’s defeat of Brighton and Hove Albion. Now Fernandez will become City’s ninth signing of the transfer window and their midfield arrival as their engine room has been overhauled. City paid £116m to sign Elliot Anderson from Nottingham Forest before bringing in Ayyoub Bouaddi from Lille for £86m. Former midfielder lynchpin Rodri left to join Barcelona, with Nico Gonzalez moving to Newcastle United and Bernardo Silva and Tijjani Reijnders signing for Real Madrid and Al Qadsiah respectively. The signing of Fernandez will be City’s last of another busy transfer window, but his exit leaves Chelsea with work to do ahead of the fast-approaching deadline. Will Chelsea fill Fernandez void before deadline? Fernandez joined Chelsea from Benfica in 2023 and developed into an instrumental player for the Blues. He has scored 31 goals and provided 29 assists in his time at Stamford Bridge, a spell in which he won the Conference League and FIFA Club World Cup under Maresca. Chelsea have thrived in their first three games under new head coach Xabi Alonso despite Fernandez only playing a cameo role in one. They have scored nine goals as a front three of Joao Pedro, Cole Palmer and Morgan Rogers has hit the ground running, though their five goals conceded across two league fixtures points to worrying defensive concerns. Still, even with their strong start to the campaign, Chelsea will feel the need to quickly fill the void left by Fernandez, and two names have emerged as apparent targets. Monaco’s Lamine Camara and Roma’s Manu Kone have both been linked with moves to Chelsea. However, Monaco are reported to have rejected two offers for Camara while Roma boss Gian Piero Gasperini is said to have blocked the departure of France international Kone, who caught the eye with his performances at the World Cup. They hope to sign him back to the practice squad. Dallas named Sam Howell the backup to Dak Prescott and left Milton temporarily out of work after the Cowboys claimed running back Emari Demercado and needed a roster spot. Cowboys coach Brian Schottenheimer and executive vice president Stephen Jones both said Tuesday that they want Milton back on the practice squad as the team’s third quarterback. Milton’s departure would necessitate signing a different third quarterback. The Cowboys are waiting to see if Milton clears waivers. “Joe obviously played really good in the preseason games,” Jones said on All DLLS Cowboys. “We really liked his performance. Sam did as well. But at the end of the day, when you took the full body of work in training camp, the practices against other teams, the coaches thought — albeit really close — Sam was the best choice for the team to go with as two now. We’d love to have Joe back. A lot of teams in this league figure out ways to carry three and four [quarterbacks]. We’ve got a lot of stress on our roster with this new defense and things that we’re doing that we can carry two [quarterbacks]. We’re in talks with Joe. We’ll see if he gets claimed. If he doesn’t, we’d love to have Joe back as our three and on the practice squad.” In three preseason games, Milton completed 29 of 43 passes for 378 yards and three touchdowns with no interceptions. He added 12 carries for 14 yards and a rushing touchdown. The Cowboys traded a fifth-round pick to New England for Milton in the 2025 offseason, and he served as Prescott’s backup last season. It clearly bothered him When head coach Todd Monken subsequently named Watson QB1 to start the season, fans found more ways to show their displeasure While Watson didn’t play in the Browns’ preseason finale last Thursday, he was on the sideline and spent most of his time with a towel over his head — perhaps trying to be as incognito as possible. But does it bother Monken that Cleveland fans clearly have not wholly embraced his choice for starting quarterback? “Absolutely not,” Monken said in his Tuesday press conference, via transcript from the team. “Would I prefer that we would all be on the same page? Yeah, but that has nothing to do with my decision, and it can never have anything to do with my decision. “My decision has got to be about what’s best for the Browns in Week 1 and all the way through the season, and as long as I’m the head coach here.” To that end, Monken said he has confidence Watson will be able to push the ball down the field to create explosive plays. “You’re not going to be elite on offense and score points if you can’t create explosives,” Monken said. “It’s so hard to drive the football the length of the field without an explosive. You can look at the studies in terms of percentage of scoring a touchdown or getting a field goal with one explosive in a drive. Obviously, that comes after you’ve gotten the first first down. Every coordinator is going to say we’re chasing explosives, and everyone runs with, ‘Oh [you’re] chasing explosives.’ Well, no shit. Everyone’s chasing explosives and trying to not to turn it over. And that’s what you’re trying to do. What’s the defense trying to do? Turn you over and not allow explosives. That’s really the big chess match is that. The ways that you win. “So, obviously having explosive players helps that. Being able to scheme it up against certain looks and then being able to execute because your protection has to hold up when you get those opportunities. I’m confident in Deshaun and our ability to push the ball down the field, otherwise we wouldn’t be starting him.” Add favorite players, teams, and leagues with an NBCUniversal Profile Continue

The 76ers announced Wednesday that they have signed Tacko Fall, Jameer Nelson Jr., and Saint Thomas to contracts. we have signed Tacko Fall, Jameer Nelson Jr., and Saint Thomas. ✍️ pic.twitter.com/1vIxBv5QBe — Philadelphia 76ers (@sixers) September 1, 2026 Those are Exhibit 10 contracts, which are training camp contracts where a player can get a bonus (up to $85,000) if they sign to play with Philadelphia’s G League affiliate, the Delaware Blue Coats. All three of Fall, Nelson and Thomas have two-way eligibility left, and the 76ers do have one open two-way contract spot they could give out if someone stands out in training camp. Fall, the 7'6" fan-favorite center, spent two seasons in Boston and one in Cleveland, but has been out of the NBA since 2022, playing overseas. He also played in the NBA All-Star Friday Night Celebrity Game last February in Los Angeles. Nelson is the son of former NBA player and current 76ers Executive Vice President of Basketball Operations Jameer Nelson. He was in the Spurs’ training camp two years ago and then with their G League team, then in the Kings’ training camp last season and played for their G League affiliate, the Stockton Kings. Last season with Stockton, he averaged 19.9 points and 3.7 assists per game. Thomas, a 6'7" wing, was in training camp last season with Philadelphia and averaged 12.5 points and five rebounds a game for the Blue Coats when he played with them. Unlike the NFL or other sports, there are very rarely training camp battles for a roster spot in the NBA, and in this case, Philadelphia’s roster is set. It has 14 players under contract for next season and plans to enter the season at that number, deciding whether to add a 15th player down the line. ARS 6.9m 27/08 Hincapie ARS 5.4m 27/08 Madueke ARS 6.4m 27/08 P.M.Sarr TOT 4.9m 27/08 Sarr CRY 6.4m Community How ‘The Great and The Good’ did in FPL Gameweek 2 September 1 307 comments 1 September 2026 307 comments Fantasy Football Scout community writer Greyhead returns with his series of ‘The Great and The Good’ articles analysing the Gameweek 2 strategies of some well-known Fantasy Premier League (FPL) managers ‘The Great and The Good’ this season are the FPL Godfather Mark Sutherns , BlackBox pair and Andy North , Scouts FPL General Tom Freeman and Joe Lepper , defending ‘Great and The Good’ champion Huss E , FPL celebrities FPL Harry LTFPL Andy Pras and Zophar , plus Hall of Famers Fabio Borges Thomas Brønsby Ben Crellin Elevenify and Tom Dollimore Alongside these, of course, are last year’s mini league winner Andrew McKinnon and invitational champ Ben McCrum “We should definitely talk about Bruno” And so we arrive at Gameweek 2 — the difficult second album. The week where absolutely nothing happens because every member of ‘The Great and The Good’ has spent the summer building a meticulous 10-week plan involving fixture swings, price changes, captaincy permutations and enough spreadsheets to make Excel ask for annual leave, well in theory at least. Yet, the dark clouds of uncertainty have already begun gathering over FPL. The unexpected form of predicted cannon-fodder Hull City, the heavy hitters all heavy hitting making those swaps more problematic, and, of course, the transfer window have led to widespread second-guessing amongst our managers. Tottenham Hotspur have approached the transfer window like Auntie Pat at the dessert section of an all-inclusive holiday. Initially claiming she’s “just having a look” , before emerging with too many new signings and a stomach ache. And Iliman Ndiaye (£6.0m) appeared to be desperately looking for a transfer with the same energy as an FPL manager trying to change their captain five minutes before the deadline, while their phone is on 1% battery and the Wi-Fi has mysteriously stopped working. Then there was Bradley Barcola (£8.0m), Enzo Fernandez (£6.9m), Daniel Munoz (£5.4m), Cody Gakpo (£7.0m) and Richarlison (£5.9m). I was half expecting Jim White to explode with all the excitement. There were already plenty of early Wildcard twitches. Particularly amongst those brave souls who decided they could survive without Erling Haaland (£15.5m) ahead of Coventry City in Gameweek 3. OVERALL PERFORMANCE Big Scores, big benches and big arrows in this week’s instalment of the FPL big show. 15 of the 18 managers hit centuries, with Bench-Boosting Az and newbie Andrew McKinnon on the front foot with 130 and 129. They both had the essential Fab Four of Bruno Fernandes (£12.0m), Haaland, Joao Pedro (£7.6m) and Riccardo Calafiori (£5.6m). Ben McCrum was the best of those not using a chip. He probably wished he had pressed his boost this week with 21 left on the sidelines, thanks mainly to Pascal Gross (£5.5m). Ben had a couple of differentials to the rest of ‘The Great and The Good’ in Phil Foden (£7.0m) and Alexander Isak (£9.0m). He has managed this by keeping it cheap elsewhere, not hampered by the need to Bench Boost. After last week’s captaincy points famine, this week was a feast. The majority of ‘The Great and The Good’ went for Bruno. However, Mark and Huss E stuck their necks out for Haaland after deciding to go without the United midfielder. In the end, the swing was brutal. After most of ‘The Great & The Good’ decided to get their Bench Boost out of the way in Gameweek 1, it was finally time for the FPL Blackbox Avengers to assemble. Mark Sutherns, Az and Andy North all suddenly developed an intense appreciation for Coventry defensive assets. Newcomer Andrew McKinnon also joined the party with a triple-up on Lampard’s lads at the back. All apart from Mr Sutherns got a decent return. Elsewhere, Rayan Cherki (£7.7m) produced an eye-catching performance James Tarkowski (£6.0m) reached 18 points from two games, while Morgan Gibbs-White (£7.9m) dropped in price and then immediately hauled. They are collectively owned by only two of ‘The Great and The Good’. This will soon change. The Newcastle United attackers are also beginning to look rather tasty with some decent short-term fixtures ahead. Chelsea meanwhile are doing their best to make a triple-up on their attack feel inevitable from Gameweek 4. Cole Palmer (£9.6m), Joao Pedro and Morgan Rogers (£7.5m) continue to impress. Yet the planned shift away from Manchester United players may take more courage than previously anticipated. TRANSFERS None. Nada. Keiner. Not a single transfer. TEMPLATE Unsurprisingly, the template has barely shifted. But enjoy it while you can. Because the Manchester City Tsunami is coming. There will be plenty of knee-Cherking! WHO WON THE BOOST? So, who won the battle of the boosts between Gameweeks 1 and 2? Well, it was a score draw with averages of 16.6 vs 15.25. Again, the range of scores from 7 to 32 shows the heavy hand that lady luck plays on this chip in a single Gameweek. Let’s see how those who have kept their powder dry do later on. CONCLUSION Next week will be a moving week, with all of them having two transfers and a whole world of options opening up; this is shaping up to be an exciting season. Anyway, that’s all from me for now and remember, don’t have nightmares. articles.title: Liverpool take last minute plunge on Bundesliga star as Mohamed Salah replacement: report
articles.excerpt: Liverpool are attempting a last-minute transfer raid, targeting VfB Stuttgart in their efforts to sign a replacement for departed superstar Mohamed Salah. The Reds have overseen a transfer window of mixed outcomes — on the one hand, they experienced a mass exodus of veterans in Salah , Andrew Roberton and Ibrahima Konate this summer, and nearly lost Cody Gakpo to a strong Manchester City bid; on the other, they recently secured the services of PSG superstar Bradley Barcola. The Frenchman will join Alexander Isak, Florian Wirtz, a soon-to-be-fit Hugo Ekitike and summer signing Victor Munoz in a revamped Liverpool attack, but Andoni Iraola ’s men are looking to see another forward join their ranks, now targeting the Bundesliga . Liverpool target electric Bundesliga winger Jamie Leweling Liverpool are looking to raid Stuttgart. According to Sky Germany , both Liverpool and Everton are after Stuttgart forward Jamie Leweling, with the former deeming him a potential Salah replacement. The 25-year-old is contracted to the Bundesliga side until 2029, meaning he will not come for cheap, or easily, however, his contributions during the 2025-26 season could make the late plunge worth it. (Image credit: Getty Images) Facebook Pinterest Email Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Liverpool are attempting a last-minute transfer raid, targeting VfB Stuttgart in their efforts to sign a replacement for departed superstar Mohamed Salah. The Reds have overseen a transfer window of mixed outcomes — on the one hand, they experienced a mass exodus of veterans in Salah , Andrew Roberton and Ibrahima Konate this summer, and nearly lost Cody Gakpo to a strong Manchester City bid; on the other, they recently secured the services of PSG superstar Bradley Barcola. The Frenchman will join Alexander Isak, Florian Wirtz, a soon-to-be-fit Hugo Ekitike and summer signing Victor Munoz in a revamped Liverpool attack, but Andoni Iraola ’s men are looking to see another forward join their ranks, now targeting the Bundesliga Liverpool target electric Bundesliga winger Jamie Leweling Liverpool are looking to raid Stuttgart. According to Sky Germany , both Liverpool and Everton are after Stuttgart forward Jamie Leweling, with the former deeming him a potential Salah replacement. The 25-year-old is contracted to the Bundesliga side until 2029, meaning he will not come for cheap, or easily, however, his contributions during the 2025-26 season could make the late plunge worth it. Barcola favours the left flank. (Image credit: Getty Images) Leweling bagged 11 goals in all competitions for Stuttgart during his latest campaign, seven of which came in the Bundesliga, and recorded 12 assists, nine of which were in the German top-flight. The German was clinical in his finishing, missing just one Opta-defined Big Chance in the Bundesliga season, and scoring his seven strikes from an xG of 4.31. The best features, fun and footballing quizzes, straight to your inbox every week. He also created the joint second-most Big Chances for Stuttgart, tied for ten with Angelo Stiller and Maximilian Mittelstadt. Outside of goal contributions, Leweling proved underwhelming from a take-on perspective, recording just one dribble p/90. His physicality was a level above, recording nearly seven duels won p/90, at a success rate just shy of 50%. Roma have displayed significant interest in recent hours regarding Leweling, however, no deal has yet been completed, with both Everton and Liverpool retaining interest. Munoz also favours the left, arriving this summer before Barcola. (Image credit: Getty Images) Should the 25-year-old join in a last-minute transfer to Anfield, he would operate as a natural replacement for Salah on the right flank. Additionally, he brings left wing experience. Conversely, new signings Munoz and Barcola favour the left flank; in the absence of Leweling, it is Gakpo who would likely be turned to in times of need, should Liverpool fail to fill Salah’s vacant position. The Reds have also exhibited interest in Ismaila Sarr and Yankuba Minteh, both Premier League-proven talents, however, neither deal appears likely at this stage. If they are to obtain Leweling, it is near certain to cost a significant premium. TOPICS Kedar Bayley Freelance Writer Kedar Bayley is a trained journalist specialising in culture reporting. articles.title: Roberto De Zerbi and Tottenham Hotspur receive major transfer deadline day boost
articles.excerpt: Tottenham Hotspur have been handed a lift on transfer deadline day as Swedish international Dejan Kulusevski returned to full team training, 477 days after suffering a complex knee injury. The 26-year-old forward has not featured in a competitive fixture since May 2025, when a challenge during a Premier League defeat to Crystal Palace left him with patella cartilage damage in his right knee. While initial diagnoses suggested a minor knock, subsequent scans revealed significant cartilage damage requiring surgery. Dejan Kulusevski returns to Spurs training after 477 days (Image credit: Getty Images) His rehabilitation was heavily disrupted by setbacks and because cartilage lacks a direct blood supply, the joint failed to heal naturally under increased workloads, forcing Kulusevski to undergo a second surgical procedure to clean out the affected area. In total, the Swede's 15-month ordeal has forced him to sit out well over 60 matches for club and country. Dejan Kulusevski (Image credit: Getty Images) From the sidelines, Kulusevski has watched a turbulent chapter in Spurs ’ recent history unfold. Former manager Ange Postecoglou departed, Thomas Frank arrived and left, then so did Igor

Former manager Ange Postecoglou departed, Thomas Frank arrived and left, then so did Igor Tudor. New head coach Roberto De Zerbi has since taken the reins, but Kulusevski has been out of action for so long, he has missed Tottenham's 2025 Europa League title, as well as the entirety of last season's domestic struggles, including a 17th-place Premier League finish. He was also forced to miss Sweden’s 2026 World Cup campaign. The best features, fun and footballing quizzes, straight to your inbox every week. For De Zerbi, who has faced a frustrating start to the 2026/27 campaign following consecutive losses to Brentford and Newcastle , Kulusevski’s return provides a boost to Tottenham’s attacking options. The versatile attacker’s ability to operate as a direct right-winger or more of a central playmaker offers De Zerbi the options his side has lacked for quite some time. Given that Kulusevski has spent 477 days away from first-team action, realistic expectations must be maintained. Re-integrating into high-intensity Premier League football following two surgical procedures and a prolonged period of inactivity will require significant patience from Spurs supporters, and it will inevitably take time before he recovers full match sharpness and rhythm. Plenty has changed at Spurs since Kulusevski last featured, including the personnel (Image credit: Getty Images) Nevertheless, stepping back onto the training pitch alongside his teammates is a significant milestone. "After 477 days I came back to full team training," Kulusevski wrote on social media. "Everything is impossible until is [sic] not. Want to see a miracle. Be one. See u soon." Joe's ' Mastermind ' specialist subject is 2000s-era Newcastle United having had a season ticket at St. James' Park for 10 years before relocating to Leeds and later London. Joe takes a keen interest in youth football, covering PL2, U21 Euros, as well as U20 and U17 World Cups in the past, in addition to hosting the industry-leading football recruitment-focused SCOUTED podcast. He is also one of the lucky few to have 'hit top bins' as a contestant on Soccer AM . It wasn't a shin-roller. The police report strongly suggests that the video includes images of the alleged assault. On Tuesday, Packers G.M. Brian Gutekunst was asked at a press conference whether the team has seen it. We have not seen the video ,” Gutekunst said, via Rob Demovsky of ESPN. “Again, those are legal things going on right now, so we’ll let those play out. That’s really not for us, but in the appropriate times, if those things become available, we’ll figure that stuff out when that time comes.” Gutekunst also was asked whether the team needs to see the video before making a decision about Jacobs’s future with the team. “Again, we’re going to lean on the legal process and let that happen, but we’ll take things as they come,” Gutekunst said. The situation brings back memories of the weeks preceding the release of the notorious Ray Rice elevator video. The league, as of August 2014, had not seen the video. We argued that it would be easy for the league to get it. It was part of his case file, and Rice ultimately controlled his case file. If the league told Rice he couldn’t play until his lawyer made the video available for review, the league would have quickly gotten it. It sparked a somewhat spirited debate by phone with a league official. The conversation ended with this prediction: “If you don’t get that video, TMZ eventually will.” (By early September, TMZ had gotten it — and then all hell broke loose.) In this case, it would be even easier for the league or the team to inspect the video. It came from Jacobs’s house. He owns the footage. Why wouldn’t the Packers want to see it? Coach Matt LaFleur recently said regarding Jacobs, "[W]hat he tells me, I believe him and I trust him. I’m going to do that until proven otherwise.” One way to be proven otherwise, or to have LaFleur’s current belief confirmed, would be to tell him to produce the video. articles.excerpt: Newcastle have landed a player they coveted back in May right at the end of the transfer window.
articles.source_type: Weekly five-players-to-buy and players-to-avoid pieces, injury-doubt round-ups
articles.body: Newcastle sign 'top target' Fernandez-Pardo in £51m deal Skip to content Football News Premier League News Newcastle confirm £51million signing of ‘top target’ Fernandez-Pardo Newcastle have landed a player they coveted back in May right at the end of the transfer window. Nicholas McGee Last Update: 5 hours ago 4 min read Add us as a preferred source on Google Newcastle United have completed the signing of Belgium forward Matias Fernandez-Pardo from Lille Fernandez-Pardo has signed a five-year contract with the Magpies, who struck a deal worth €60million (£51m) plus add-ons with the Ligue 1 club for the 21-year-old. He becomes Newcastle’s eighth signing of a transfer window that has seen the squad undergo a major revamp. Newcastle will hope his arrival will serve as a major boost to Newcastle’s forward line, with Fernandez-Pardo able to play on both wings, as a number 10 and as a central striker. His signing comes as Newcastle forward Nick Woltemade, their club-record signing of last summer, is set to join Juventus on a season-long loan. Fernandez-Pardo joined Lille from Gent in 2024. He scored 12 goals and provided nine assists in two seasons with Les Dogues, helping them to a third-placed finish in Ligue 1 last term. His performances earned him a place in Belgium’s squad for this summer’s World Cup, where he made three appearances as a substitute in the group stage as the Red Devils reached the quarter-finals. Table of Contents Newcastle boss key to Fernandez-Pardo signing Newcastle land ‘top target’ Newcastle boss key to Fernandez-Pardo signing Newcastle have made an excellent start to the new season, despite losing three key players in the form of Bruno Guimaraes, Sandro Tonali and Anthony Gordon and seeing Eddie Howe’s celebrated tenure as manager come to an end in late July. Matthias Jaissle was appointed as Howe’s successor and is unbeaten in his first three games in charge. Newcastle drew 2-2 in their opening Premier League game with Liverpool and were only denied all three points by a last-gasp penalty for the Reds. They subsequently beat West Brom in the EFL Cup before a 2-0 league win at Tottenham last Saturday in which several new signings impressed as Tonali struggled to make an impact for new club Spurs. Jaissle has already received significant plaudits for his influence not just on the new recruits, but also on Newcastle players who endured difficult 2025-26 campaigns, with Anthony Elanga and Yoane Wissa — goalscorers against Tottenham — looking rejuvenated under his management. And Fernandez-Pardo credited Jaissle as being key to his decision to join Newcastle. “I’m really, really happy to be here and very proud to be at such a big club,” Fernandez-Pardo told Newcastle’s official website “I spoke to the head coach and he really showed how much he wanted me to be here. In terms of my own career progression, it made complete sense to come so I didn’t hesitate at all. “I know the club, I know about the stadium, I know it’s a fantastic atmosphere. I’ve followed the team. What I’ve seen is a team that’s very ambitious, wants to attack, get forward, really chase teams and go after them, and that’s really something I want to take part in as well. “I’m still young, I’m still hungry, and that’s why I’m here, and I want to make that progress with Newcastle. I can’t wait to start the wonderful adventure here.” Jaissle said: “I am very happy to welcome Matias to our club. We were all delighted when we knew we could complete this deal. “Matias is a highly technical player with explosiveness in his game. He can score and assist, he has courage, and he has the ability to take players on. We’re sure our supporters will enjoy watching him play. “He has already shown in Lille that he can perform on the big stage, and we will work closely with him to keep developing his game further. We are excited to see him in a Newcastle United shirt.” Newcastle land ‘top target’ The sales of Guimaraes, Tonali and Gordon have enabled Newcastle to rebuild their squad, with the club investing heavily in young players with significant potential. All eight of their signings are aged 24 or under, with Fernandez-Pardo joining goalkeepers Lukas Hornicek and Ewen Jaouen, right-back Amar Dedic, winger Bazoumana Toure and midfielders Sean Steur, Aladji Bamba and Nico Gonzalez in making the move to St. James’ Park. But in Fernandez-Pardo, they have landed a player whom sporting director Ross Wilson claims was the top target right at the start of the summer. “Matias is a really important signing for us,” Wilson said. “As I said last week, we waited patiently on Nico Gonzalez, and this time we’ve done the same – only longer. “Matias is a strong example of how a transfer window can unfold with twists and turns along the way. Back in May, he was our top target and we always remained engaged with him. “Now, at the end of the window, he becomes our eighth addition to a refreshed Newcastle United, and we are excited to welcome him.” Topics Lille OSC Newcastle United F.C. Loan moves to Millwall, Bristol City and Everton soon followed before a permanent switch to Apollon Limassol in Cyprus, where she scored 19 goals in 19 games. Rosella returned to England to re-sign for the Robins for a season before joining Spurs at the start of the 2019/20 campaign. Across six years in North London scored 12 goals in 109 appearances and also helped the side to a Women’s FA Cup final against Manchester United in 2024. Rosella also brings international experience into the group, having played 35 times and found the net 11 times for Morocco. Caserio said in July and again on Tuesday that the team has had talks with the 2023 first-round pick about a new deal, but that those talks will be put on hold when the Texans face the Bills in Week 1. “If we don’t get it figured out before the season starts, then it’ll be something we address in the offseason ,” Caserio said, via DJ Bien-Amie of ESPN.com. The Texans have already picked up their option on Stroud’s contract for 2027, so the quarterback will remain under contract regardless of how things play out on the field this year. A strong season would make it harder for the Texans to continue playing the waiting game, but anything resembling Stroud’s postseason performance from last season would lead to a lot of questions about the future of the quarterback position in Houston. The 19-year-old did not appear in the squad for the Gunners’ 3-0 pre-season victory against Manchester City in the Community Shield, missing out alongside Gabriel Martinelli. Nwaneri also scored against Dortmund for Arsenal in pre-season, during a 3-2 loss in the Emirates Cup — and converted his penalty in the post-match shootout. Since making his Premier League debut for the North London club in 2022, aged just 15, Nwaneri has failed to break into a side that has competed for the English top-flight title in four successive seasons. He has made 51 appearances for Arsenal, scoring 10 and assisting two, with Mikel Arteta confessing in August that he would like the 19-year-old to stay, but that he needs to receive further opportunities. The club reportedly weighed up the benefits of selling their youngster outright, however, a loan period has been agreed. articles.title: Under-17s off to winning start in Premier League Cup
articles.excerpt: AFC Bournemouth under-17s got off to a winning start in the U17 Premier League Cup, thanks to a 3-2 victory over Southampton. Goals from Leyland Waite, Denzel Decardi-Nelson and Fikayo Solanke secured the three points for the Cherries. It ensures the Cherries get off to the strongest possible start in a group that also contains Chelsea and West Ham United. After the game, under-18s assistant coach, Elliot Head, spoke to afcb.co.uk: "The first half was a tight game with chances for both teams. "We regained the ball high up the pitch a few teams that lead to some good chances which we weren't quite able to capitalise from." The Cherries went into the interval level at 0-0, after tight first-half. Scoring in the 50th and 55th minute, the Cherries were then forced back into their own half, as Southampton brought the score level. The winner came in the 88th minute and secured all three points for the Cherries. Head continued: "The lads showed fantastic attitude throughout the game and had to dig deep after coming off the back of four games in ten days." The next under-17 cup game is away at Chelsea on 15th September.

articles.body: Barcelona complete signing of Gabriel Jesus from Arsenal Skip to content News Football Transfer News, Rumours & Gossip Barcelona complete signing of Gabriel Jesus from Arsenal Gabriel Jesus has joined Barcelona. Mitch Fretton Last Update: 1 hour ago 3 min read Add us as a preferred source on Google Barcelona have completed the signing of Gabriel Jesus from Arsenal on a permanent deal for a reported fee of £8.6m. The 29-year-old had fallen down the pecking order at Arsenal in recent seasons amid a series of injury problems, while Kai Havertz and Viktor Gyokeres had become the club’s preferred options at centre-forward. Napoli had also shown an interest in Jesus, but the former Manchester City striker has opted to continue his career in Spain. Jesus joined Arsenal from Manchester City in 2022 and scored 32 goals while providing 22 assists in 123 appearances for the Gunners. Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta confirmed before his side’s win over Aston Villa that Jesus was no longer training with the first-team squad. Jesus becomes Barcelona’s third signing from a Premier League club this summer, following the arrivals of Anthony Gordon from Newcastle and Rodri from Manchester City. GJ is blaugrana. 🤙 pic.twitter.com/brzvMFKTJb — FC Barcelona (@FCBarcelona) September 1, 2026 Table of Contents When does the summer transfer window 2026 close? What time does the Premier League transfer window shut on transfer deadline day? When does the summer transfer window close around Europe? When does the 2026/27 winter transfer window open? Can Premier League clubs sign players outside of the window? When does the summer transfer window 2026 close? The window opened on Monday June 15 and will shut on Tuesday September 1. After that, every Premier League club can register a squad of up to 25 players, 17 of whom are allowed to be non-Home Grown Players. A Home Grown Player has been registered with any club affiliated to the English or Welsh Football Association for three entire seasons or 36 months across their career before his 21st birthday, or the end of the season during which they turn 21. Under-21 players do not count towards the 25-man limit. What time does the Premier League transfer window shut on transfer deadline day? The deadline is 23:00 BST in the Premier League, but clubs can have an extra two hours to file the remaining documentation if they submit a deal sheet confirming that an agreement has been reached. The deal sheet must arrive fully completed before the transfer window closes. For international transfers, clubs also have to comply with the FIFA Transfer Matching System deadline of midnight. When does the summer transfer window close around Europe? There are slight variations between the major European leagues. Here’s when they shut. League Date BST close Premier League Sept 1 23:00 18:00 15:00 LaLiga Sept 1 22:59 17:59 14:59 Serie A Sept 1 19:00 14:00 11:00 Bundesliga Aug 31 19:00 14:00 11:00 Ligue 1 Aug 31 19:00 14:00 11:00 When does the 2026/27 winter transfer window open? The Premier League winter transfer window opens on Friday January 1, 2027 and closes on Monday February 1, 2027 at 23:00 BST. Can Premier League clubs sign players outside of the window? Clubs can only add players outside of transfer windows who are free agents and if they have room in their 25-man squad. Premier League teams can still announce deals with other clubs, but those players will not be registered to play until the window re-opens. This means there is usually little to no movement when the window closes, with four months to wait until the window re-opens. Players can be released by Premier League clubs at any time, but the usual rule is that they cannot sign for another side outside of the market. When nothing materialized, Richardson reported to the offseason program and has been competing to be the team’s backup behind Daniel Jones with Riley Leonard. Richardson’s feelings may or may not have changed. But at this point, the Colts do not intend to trade him. “He is going to be an Indianapolis Colt this year ,” General Manager Chris Ballard said in his Tuesday press conference. Richardson, 24, has continued to make strides in his development, Ballard said. “We forget how young he is sometimes. Really proud of his growth,” Ballard said. “ There were two times in camp where I thought, OK, he’s starting to really show some poise. So the two-minute against New England, we’re backed up, I think it was 38 seconds left on the clock. Gets us in field-goal range to give us a chance to get points. And then during the Atlanta scrimmage, he had a tremendous two-minute [drive] also. “So, it’s been fun to watch Anthony’s growth.” Ballard did not declare whether or not Richardson, the No. 4 overall pick of the 2023 draft. will serve as the backup, deferring to head coach Shane Steichen. But when it comes to Richardson’s status with the team at large, Steichen said the quarterback is “in a good spot.” “He’s a phenomenal teammate — and I don’t use that word lightly,” Ballard said. “Like, he is a great teammate. He likes to be around the team. He likes being part of the team. There’s never been a point — even going back into last year when he didn’t win the job — there’s not been one point where I’ve seen him hang his head and get salty. Sign up France’s Tronchon sprints to Vuelta stage win and Mas retains lead gifted by Pogacar’s crash Associated Press Associated Press Published September 1, 2026 01:04 PM Facebook Twitter Email Highlights: 2026 Vuelta a España, Stage 10 September 1, 2026 02:30 PM Relive the top moments from Stage 10 of the 2026 La Vuelta a España, where riders took on a 184.7km journey through the hills from Alcaraz to Elche de la Sierra. ELCHE DE LA SIERRA, Spain — French rider Bastien Tronchon got a career best result winning Stage 10 of the Spanish Vuelta, and Enric Mas retained the leader’s red jersey he was gifted by Tadej Pogacar’s race-ending crash. The 24-year-old Tronchon sprinted clear over the final 20 yards of a hilly 115-mile stage between Alcaraz and Elche de la Sierra. Magnus Cort was second and Thibau Nys placed third. Wout van Aert was fourth. Tronchon put his right hand to his helmet in surprise crossing the line and sobbed tearfully when his Groupama-FDJ United teammates congratulated him. Mas retained his overall lead of 1 minute, 18 seconds ahead of Primoz Roglic, the 36-year-old Slovenian who is chasing a record fifth Vuelta title. Felix Gall stayed 1:39 back in third. The Vuelta was upended over the weekend when Pogacar, the leader and overwhelming favorite to win the three-week race, crashed out and fractured his left collarbone. Stage 10 crested three third-category climbs and let a seven-man breakaway, only one of them within an hour of Mas’s overall time, build a lead of more than two and a half minutes. The peloton reeled in the last of the breakaway inside the final 3.5 miles and caught further attempts by riders to steal away for the win. Stage 11 is a flat stage suiting the sprinters over 96 miles from Cartagena to Lorca. The Vuelta finishes in Granada on Sept. 13.
