Previously, they fell to the Cityzens in 2022/23 after leading for the campaign’s bulk, again in 2023/24, then to a Mohamed Salah-led Liverpool in 2024/25. The Gunners , who secured the English top-flight crown with 85 points in May, have never retained the Premier League title, however, their quest to do so now appears slightly easier, and less expensive, following an accidental discovery versus Aston Villa Do Arsenal really need a left winger? Eze put in a solid shift at Villa Park (Image credit: Getty Images) Mikel Arteta’s men emerged victorious on Monday evening, taking home three points following a 1-0 victory at Villa Park. New signing Christos Tzolis, who began his Gunners career with two assists in Arsenal's Community Shield final victory versus Manchester City , was hooked at half-time against Villa, with the score tied at 0-0. Tzolis may have to fight for his position (Image credit: Getty Images) In came Eberechi Eze, who featured on the left wing for the second half’s duration, in which Arsenal took the lead, and then maintained it, through Bukayo Saka. Arteta’s side are not short on attacking depth, despite the loss of youngster Ethan Nwaneri to Borussia Dortmund on loan , and the departure of Gabriel Martinelli to Saudi Arabia. The best features, fun and footballing quizzes, straight to your inbox every week. That was evidenced by both players being absent from the Community Shield final squad, in which the North London club ran riot from an offensive perspective, scoring three in under 50 minutes. On the bench that day were Eze, Saka, Viktor Gyokeres and Declan Rice, with Kai Havertz, Noni Madueke, Bruno Guimaraes and Tzolis handed starts versus Enzo Maresca’s side. And with Eze’s appearance against Villa, it appears that any fears regarding reinforcement on the left flank have been alleviated, with the Englishman well-adjusted to challenge for the role. Arsenal's depth is staggering, however, late outgoings threatened their left flank (Image credit: Getty Images) The statistics painted a clear picture: 80% pass accuracy, three duels won, seven carries for a total distance of almost 100 metres, one of which being progressive, and six kilometres covered. And, more importantly, three points for the Gunners after a dominant second half — limiting the chasing Villans to 0.24 Expected Goals (xG) while Arteta’s side racked up 0.7, and bagged the deciding goal. Much has been made of Arsenal’s strength in the position, yet Eze’s appearance now certainly warrants consideration as an alternate to Tzolis. The Gunners reportedly tried their luck with Malick Fofana at Lyon , but were rebuffed after low-balling for the player. That appears to have allowed Sunderland to sign the winger for a price the French club deem more acceptable, in one of the strongest deals of the summer transfer window Positioned second in the Premier League table, and yet to concede a goal, the future appears bright for Arteta’s side. And fans would be forgiven for interpreting Eze’s cameo as a firm statement — Arsenal can retain their top-flight title, and they already hold all the necessary keys to do so. On Tuesday, Romo posted a statement on Instagram. In the message, he discloses that he has pleaded no contest. He also explains that pain medication from multiple back surgeries created an “over-reliance” on alcohol. Romo also vows to return to CBS, “in time.” It’s unknown wheter CBS is on board with that part of the plan; the network placed him on leave eight days after the incident, and it has promoted J.J. Watt into Romo’s spot on the top NFL broadcast team. Here’s the full text of Romo’s statement: “Football has shaped nearly every meaningful part of my life. I played for more than 20 years, including 14 in the NFL with the Dallas Cowboys. After my retirement, CBS gave me the profound honor of staying close to the game through broadcasting. “Playing taught me the power of relationships, the strength of a team, and the toughness to face failure head-on with honesty, resilience, and the determination to do better. “This is one of those moments when I am leaning on everything football taught me. “This morning, I faced a recent personal failure by pleading no contest to a civil offense for OWl in Wisconsin. I own this completely. “Multiple back surgeries ended my career earlier than I expected and left me with constant, debilitating pain. That pain led to a dependence on pain medication, and my efforts to get off those medications led to an over-reliance on alcohol. “As I have taught my three young sons: when you fall short, you stand up and take full responsibility. This is an important first step. The harder and more important step is examining the path that brought you here and making the changes necessary to move forward. “That path requires honesty. “None of this is an excuse. These are my failures, and I take responsibility for them. “The past month has been difficult, but it has also been personally significant. It has required me to confront and own my mistakes fully — to the Lord, to myself, to my family, and now to the public. “I am working closely with a team of doctors to address my health and make the necessary changes. I am deeply grateful for the support of my family, my friends, and the NFL community including players, coaches, and owners. Your encouragement has meant more to me than you know. “As I turn my attention to my health, my family, and, in time, my return to CBS, I kindly ask for privacy during this period.” We wish Romo the best as he addresses the issues that led to the OWI charge. And we applaud him for speaking on the issue directly, and not through an unnamed P.R. firm. Owning the situation is perhaps the biggest step toward resolving it. Whether Romo’s candor resolves the situation with CBS to his satisfaction hinges entirely on CBS. Add favorite players, teams, and leagues with an NBCUniversal Profile Continue

Sign up NBC Olympics Olympics on Peacock LA 2028 Team USA Benjamin Karl, after epic shirtless gold medal celebration, reverses retirement decision Nick Zaccardi Nick Zaccardi Published September 1, 2026 12:43 PM Facebook Twitter Email Austrian Benjamin Karl, who won Olympic snowboarding gold at age 40, then became a global sensation for his shirtless celebration, is reversing his decision to retire after the 2026 Olympic season. Karl, who races parallel giant slalom, plans to compete in the 2026-27 season, highlighted by a home World Championships in Montafon in March. “It has been a long and difficult journey from competing in regional races all the way to the very top of the sport,” Karl said, according to a social media post . “I have been snowboarding for 30 years, and over time, many things started to feel almost like a given. But my recent experiences have shown me that nothing should ever be taken for granted. “I have learned to appreciate again just how much support I have received over all these years — support that is anything but a given. Now I am really looking forward to continuing my career.” At the Milan Cortina Games, Karl broke the record for oldest individual Winter Olympic gold medalist. Later in the Games, 41-year-old American Elana Meyers Taylor broke Karl’s record with monobob gold. Karl considered a switch to cycling after the Games. “However, a number of things happened over the summer that I simply could not have foreseen,” Karl said in the post. “At the same time, I increasingly came to realize that, quite simply, I am a snowboarder who loves riding his bike.” Karl previously won Olympic medals in 2010 (silver), 2014 (bronze in parallel slalom) and 2022 (gold). He is a five-time world champion between parallel slalom (no longer on the Olympic program) and parellel giant slalom, the most recent title in 2021. 40 YEARS OLD. BACK-TO-BACK GOLD. articles.title: Anthony Gordon explains why LaLiga is less forgiving than Premier League
articles.excerpt: Anthony Gordon says the demands of Spanish football can be more punishing than the Premier League.
articles.source_type: Weekly five-players-to-buy and players-to-avoid pieces, injury-doubt round-ups
articles.body: Anthony Gordon explains why LaLiga is less forgiving than Premier League Skip to content Football News LaLiga News Anthony Gordon explains why LaLiga is less forgiving than Premier League Anthony Gordon says the demands of Spanish football can be more punishing than the Premier League. Mitch Fretton Last Update: 3 hours ago 2 min read Add us as a preferred source on Google Anthony Gordon admits he is still adapting to the demands of Spanish football after revealing that mistakes can be punished more quickly in LaLiga than in the Premier League. The England international joined Barcelona from Newcastle this summer and has made a positive start, registering three assists in his first three league appearances. Gordon says the move has required him to adjust to a more tactical and technical style of football, with less room for error. “I loved playing in the Premier League and it played a huge part in my development,” Gordon said. “But Spanish football demands a different level of tactical and technical intelligence. “In England, the intensity can sometimes mask a mistake. You can miss control the ball and still make up for it by winning the next physical battle. Here, a poor first touch or a lapse in concentration regarding your positioning can be punished immediately. “The spaces are smaller, decisions have to be made more quickly and everything has to be more precise.” Gordon scored 39 goals in 152 appearances during just over three seasons at Newcastle after beginning his senior career at Everton. Gordon: Premier League sides would struggle in Spain The 25-year-old believes some Premier League sides would struggle to consistently adopt the style of football seen in Spain. “Some Premier League teams would struggle to play this style consistently because they might not have the patience or the quality in midfield that is required,” he added. “I won’t deny that the Premier League is incredibly intense. The pace is relentless, there are physical battles everywhere, long throw-ins, corner kicks and plenty of contact. “That’s why many English players believe it’s the best league in the world. They’re used to that sort of chaos. Football in Spain is different.” Gordon has yet to score for Barcelona but has provided three assists in three league games. He made his second consecutive league start in Monday’s 5-2 win over Rayo Vallecano, setting up Raphinha for Barcelona’s fourth goal. Sign up Odds by Schedule Scores Player News ATLANTIC Boston Celtics Brooklyn Nets New York Knicks Philadelphia 76ers Toronto Raptors CENTRAL Chicago Bulls Cleveland Cavaliers Detroit Pistons Indiana Pacers Milwaukee Bucks SOUTHEAST Atlanta Hawks Charlotte Hornets Miami Heat Orlando Magic Washington Wizards NORTHWEST Denver Nuggets Minnesota Timberwolves Oklahoma City Thunder Portland Trail Blazers Utah Jazz PACIFIC Golden State Warriors Los Angeles Clippers Los Angeles Lakers Phoenix Suns Sacramento Kings SOUTHWEST Dallas Mavericks Houston Rockets Memphis Grizzlies New Orleans Pelicans San Antonio Spurs ATLANTIC Boston Celtics Brooklyn Nets New York Knicks Philadelphia 76ers Toronto Raptors CENTRAL Chicago Bulls Cleveland Cavaliers Detroit Pistons Indiana Pacers Milwaukee Bucks SOUTHEAST Atlanta Hawks Charlotte Hornets Miami Heat Orlando Magic Washington Wizards NORTHWEST Denver Nuggets Minnesota Timberwolves Oklahoma City Thunder Portland Trail Blazers Utah Jazz PACIFIC Golden State Warriors Los Angeles Clippers Los Angeles Lakers Phoenix Suns Sacramento Kings SOUTHWEST Dallas Mavericks Houston Rockets Memphis Grizzlies New Orleans Pelicans San Antonio Spurs Fantasy Betting Standings Player Stats Team Stats Player Stats Team Stats Videos In open letter to NBA GMs, Victor Oladipo says his body is finally right, wants another chance Kurt Helin Kurt Helin Published September 1, 2026 12:22 PM Facebook Twitter Email Victor Oladipo is a man robbed of his peak seasons by injuries. In 2017-18, he averaged 23.1 points and 4.3 assists per game for the Pacers, won Most Improved Player and was an All-Star, an All-NBA and an All-Defensive Team player. Then the next season he ruptured his quadriceps tendon, and he was never physically right again. Oladipo, now 34, hasn’t played in the NBA in three seasons. In an open letter to general managers at The Players Tribune , Oladipo said it took a long time for him to stop chasing what was lost and just be patient and get his body right. He said he is finally in that place, can still contribute to a winning basketball team, and wants that chance. “Me, in this moment of my life, at 34 years old. The version of her dad that got kicked all the way down the mountain, then spent years trying to climb back up, only to get kicked back down, again and again … but never once quit trying to climb. The version of her dad that, let’s be real, is probably getting counted out by a lot of people, and is probably getting laughed at by a few of them … but has managed to keep his faith, and keep his purpose. The version of her dad that’s finally found the perspective, and the humility, to write a letter like this one. “To say to any GM who’s willing to listen: I believe my body is finally right. I believe I still have GREAT (and more importantly, WINNING) basketball in front of me. I believe I can be a valuable contributor to an NBA locker room. And what I’m asking for right now is an opportunity to prove it.... “So that’s where I’m at with everything. I don’t know how my journey here is going to end....... Maybe a team out there will give me a chance. Maybe no team will. That’s really up to you all. But if you’re in an NBA front office, and you took the time to read this: Thank you from the bottom of my heart.” Oladipo has been linked to Sacramento as a potential backup to rookie Darius Acuff Jr., but nothing official has come of that. Oladipo played in the G League for the Wisconsin Herd part of last season and averaged 13.5 points per game in the regular season, shooting 32.5% from 3-point range. He has also played some in China in recent years. Oladipo faces the reality many older players do: Most teams would rather give a bench point guard spot (or any position) to a young player they can develop and hold on to for years than to one on the back end of a career. Still, there is a real role for mature, quality veterans in the locker room who can still contribute something on the court. Whether Oladipo is that guy and gets a chance remains to be seen, but he’s made his pitch. Mentions Victor Oladipo Add favorite players, teams, and leagues with an NBCUniversal Profile Continue

Now they’re three key members of the Rams’ defense. McDuffie was traded to the Rams in March, Garrett was traded to the Rams a couple months later, and Donald just came out of retirement. McDuffie told Andrew Siciliano of NFL Media that he wouldn’t believed it was possible for Rams General Manager Les Snead and head coach Sean McVay to bring all three of them onto the same team. I probably would’ve said you’re lying , for real,” McDuffie said. “There’s no way you can get me. There’s no way you can get Myles. There’s no way you can get A.D. But, hey, hat off to Les. Hat off to Sean. Those guys are masterminds and they did it.” The 25-year-old McDuffie has already been a first-team All-Pro once and won Super Bowl rings twice in his first four NFL seasons -- and he’s the least accomplished of the trio: Garrett has been named the NFL’s Defensive Player of the Year two of the last three years, while Donald is one of only three players in NFL history to win Defensive Player of the Year three times. Most teams don’t add even one player with those kinds of credentials to their defense in an offseason. The Rams added three. McDuffie is still having a hard time believing it’s real. He can do without fame that comes with greatness Associated Press Associated Press Published September 1, 2026 12:19 PM Facebook Twitter Email Scheffler: FedExCup a 'nice way to finish' year August 30, 2026 08:29 PM Scottie Scheffler recalls his Round 4 comeback at the Tour Championship to win his second career FedExCup, calling his performance in the playoffs "a nice way to finish off the season." ATLANTA — Scottie Scheffler’s final act of the season was to sign his winning scorecard. After a few minutes to exhale, his wife and two sons having come into the room, he placed his cap over the fixed camera the PGA Tour now installs in previously private scoring areas. Content is king. It wasn’t quite the level of Brian Harman smirking and shooting the bird at the camera in Minnesota, which made Scheffler chuckle and pump his fist. Both were playful moments, and yet East Lake shed a little light on Scheffler’s incredible staying power. Scheffler loves what it takes to be the best player in golf, even the tedious work. He just doesn’t care for all the noise and notoriety that accompany greatness. “I have a tendency to keep my head down and kind of stay in my own lane when I’m out there playing,” he said during the trophy presentation at the Tour Championship. “It’s really fun when you’re able to win and celebrate with the fans in moments like these, and have my family here.” Still, his priority is to crush more than to engage. So he added somewhat apologetically, “I feel bad sometimes. I really do keep my head down and try to focus as much as I can. But I really do hear all the cheers, and I’m very thankful for all of them.” The RBC Heritage at Hilton Head is reputed to be among the most chill tournaments on the schedule, the perfect place to decompress right after the Masters. During the pro-am that week, Scheffler said he felt a calmer vibe at Augusta National despite the enormous pressure, mainly because of the space inside the ropes and spectators (patrons) who cheer, not scream. When he reached the ninth tee, fans at Hilton Head were screaming his name as he waited for the fairway to clear to tee off. Scheffler turned and smiled. It’s part of the deal, and he knows that by now. But this extraordinary run of dominance allows for speculation how long he can keep it up as the attention gets brighter. Winning is hard. The trappings that come with it can be exhausting. The way Scheffler showed up seemingly every week — he finished first, second or third in half of the 20 tournaments he played — and then capped off the season by winning two of the three postseason tournaments was satisfying. It also makes him a shoo-in to be voted PGA Tour player of the year for a fifth straight time. That would tie Tiger Woods for winning the most in a row. Best comparison with Tiger is separation Comparisons with Woods, just like athletes in any sport across generations, are for pool halls and podcasts. Scheffler brushed off the inevitable moment of passing Woods at No. 1 on the PGA Tour career earnings list, a spot Woods held for nearly 26 years. “I wouldn’t really consider that a Tiger record being broken,” Scheffler said. “I think it just shows one of the many effects he had on the game of a golf in a positive way.” Woods never played for a prize fund of $10 million in his peak years from 1997 through 2009. Scheffler played for an average purse of $19.25 million this year. When it comes to money records, it just isn’t a fair fight. The real benchmark — 82 tour wins — is still a long way off. Scheffler has gone three straight years with three wins or more. Woods went 10 out of 11 years winning at least four times. Scheffler, however, has separated himself in a similar manner as Woods. His points average in the world ranking is more than double that of Rory McIlroy at No. 2. This is his 171st week in a row at No. 1 in the world. Woods holds the record with 281 consecutive weeks at No. 1. A milestone that for years looks untouchable is now at least thinkable. Practice makes close to perfect for Scheffler There is not much drama with Scheffler, and he likes it that way. His obsession is such that he once said he had to force himself to find something other than golf to think about. Having two young boys have helped. “Part of what’s great about golf and part of what’s very frustrating about golf is it’s kind of an endless puzzle you’re always trying to solve,” Scheffler said. “I feel like in order to become good at this game, you have to really enjoy the harder parts of it, the stuff that’s a little bit more mundane.” For Scheffler, that would be the first 10 minutes on the stationary bike. Cardio work is not his favorite. Neither is a cold plunge at 5:30 a.m. “Do I want to go in there and freeze? No, but I do it,” he said in January. Practice, however, doesn’t get old. Neither does competing. His caddie, Ted Scott, once told of a round they played at Cypress Point early in 2025. Scheffler was returning from slicing open his right hand when he tried to use a wine glass to cut ravioli. He showed Scott no mercy that day, prompting the caddie to say, “Scottie don’t play games when he’s playing games.” It’s all about getting the most out of every day, from the cold plunge to the bike to the range to the first tee. Scheffler is relentless and it’s a matter of how long he can keep up this pace. “I don’t feel like I take days off. I’m highly competitive, and I’m very proud of being able to have the consistent results I’ve had over the years,” he said. “I feel like it’s a gift to play out here on the PGA Tour, and I don’t want to take it for granted. ... I don’t want to look back at the end of my career and feel like I could have done more in order to play well.” Add favorite players, teams, and leagues with an NBCUniversal Profile Continue

articles.title: Premier League Team Stats After Two Gameweeks - 2026/27
articles.excerpt: All 20 clubs have now played twice. The cumulative numbers say Arsenal's defence is the real thing, Manchester United are due more than five goals, and Hull City's six points rest on the thinnest underlying process in the league.
articles.source_type: Head-to-head player comparison, goalkeeper and position value analysis
articles.body: Premier League Team Stats After Two Gameweeks - 2026/27 Premier League Team Stats After Two Gameweeks - 2026/27 Every Premier League club has now played twice, which means the team-level numbers finally have enough in them to be worth reading. Everything below is cumulative - goals, expected goals (xG), shots and clean sheets across gameweeks 1 and 2 combined - pulled from the teams view of the Statz FPL Stats tool , where you can sort and slice all of it yourself. This is the companion piece to our GW2 player review : that one covers the individuals, this one covers the teams behind them. The two-week picture Attack first. Manchester United lead the league for expected goals with 6.61 xG from 54 shots - both league highs - yet have only five goals to show for it. Brentford sit second on 5.76 xG, Liverpool third on 5.51, and Chelsea have turned 5.28 xG into seven goals, joint-most in the division alongside Brighton , who have their seven from a more modest 4.45 xG. Manchester City have six from 4.80. At the other end, Arsenal are running the cleanest defensive numbers in the league: no goals conceded, 0.62 xG against, and one shot on target faced across two matches. They and Hull City are the only clubs with two clean sheets from two. City's 1.16 xG against is next best - though they are yet to keep a clean sheet - and Brentford, with 1.70 xG against and one goal conceded, complete the shortlist of defences whose underlying numbers genuinely hold up. The stragglers: Ipswich Town have conceded a league-worst 5.33 xG against (and six goals), Newcastle United have shipped 4.92 xG against from 44 shots conceded - joint-most with Ipswich - and Tottenham Hotspur have paired five goals conceded with none scored. Aston Villa 's attack is the starkest line in the whole table: two matches, 13 shots, not one on target. One more column worth knowing about now that defensive contributions score FPL points: Brentford lead the league with 197 defensive contributions across the two games, Leeds United have 190, Everton 185 and Crystal Palace 179 - with Palace's 59 tackles a league high by a wide margin. Overperformers and underperformers The caveat, stated plainly: two games is a tiny sample. Nothing here is a verdict. These are signals - gaps between results and underlying process that usually narrow over time. Hull City are the league's biggest overperformers, and it is not close. Six points from an expected-points figure of 1.5, three goals from 1.54 xG, and two clean sheets despite facing 3.37 xG and 32 shots. Newcastle are running a similar pattern: four points off 1.5 expected, four goals scored from 2.21 xG, and just two conceded from that 4.92 xG against. Everton have four points while conceding once from 4.37 xG against. All three have banked results their chance data did not earn - which is allowed, but rarely lasts. Chelsea are the interesting split case: seven goals from 5.28 xG at one end, five conceded from 2.77 xG against at the other. The attack is running slightly hot and the defence slightly unlucky at the same time - six points either way. The mirror image starts with Manchester United, the only club underperforming at both ends at once: three points against 4.8 expected, five goals from 6.61 xG, and four conceded from just 1.87 xG against. Nottingham Forest have one point from 3.0 expected, Liverpool two from 3.6 despite the league's third-best xG, and Coventry City have no points from 2.1 expected and no goals from 1.37 xG. Tottenham's blank is harder to excuse by luck alone - none scored from 1.87 xG on 26 shots - and Villa's zero points are the one bottom-of-table start the model actually endorses: their 0.8 expected points is the lowest in the league. What it means for FPL Clean sheets: the data trusts Arsenal above everyone. One shot on target faced in two games is as good as defending gets, and their defenders are the premium picks the numbers most support. Brentford's 1.70 xG against makes their budget defenders a quietly strong buy, and City's process (1.16 xG against) says their blank clean-sheet column is sequencing, not a warning. The traps run the other way: Hull's two clean sheets sit on 3.37 xG against and 32 shots conceded, Everton's single goal conceded sits on 4.37 xG against, and Newcastle's defensive numbers are the worst-kept secret in the league - buying any of those defences is paying for results the process did not produce. Attacks: Manchester United's volume - 54 shots, 16 on target, 6.61 xG - is exactly what you want to buy before the goals catch up, and Liverpool's 5.51 xG with two points tells a similar story. Brentford and City offer volume with results attached. The team-level trap is scoring without creating: Hull have three goals from 14 shots (only Villa, on 13, have taken fewer), and Ipswich have four goals from 2.31 xG while facing more expected goals than anyone at the other end - attackers from either side are riding variance. For the week-to-week application of all this, the FPL projections convert team strength into player-level expected points, the fixture ticker rates every club's upcoming run, and team news carries the predicted lineups before each deadline. Four GW3 fixtures through this lens Arsenal v Chelsea (Sunday) : the league's only unbreached defence against its joint-top scorers. The Statz model gives Arsenal a 41.5% clean-sheet probability and Chelsea just 16.4%. Everton v Manchester United (Sunday) : the biggest shot volume in the league meets a defence that has conceded once from 4.37 xG against. The model projects United at 1.74 goals and gives Everton a 17.5% clean-sheet chance - the overperformance gets a proper test. Manchester City v Coventry City (Saturday) : the highest clean-sheet probability of the gameweek, 49.6%, against a side projected at 0.70 goals and yet to score this season. If City's blank clean-sheet column really is sequencing, this is where it ends. Hull City v Aston Villa (Saturday) : the regression watch. Six points from 1.5 expected hosts no points and no shots on target - and the model favours the visitors, giving Villa 1.84 expected points to Hull's 0.92 and projecting them for 1.79 goals. articles.title: FPL Gameweek 2 Summary and Players to Watch
articles.excerpt: Bruno Fernandes plundered 23 points, Chelsea and Brighton traded seven goals, and the Gameweek 2 underlying numbers flagged six players your rivals have not noticed yet.
articles.source_type: Head-to-head player comparison, goalkeeper and position value analysis
articles.body: FPL Gameweek 2 Summary: Best Players and Who to Watch FPL Gameweek 2 Summary and Players to Watch Gameweek 2 of the 2026/27 season had a bit of everything: 32 goals across the ten fixtures, a seven-goal shootout at Stamford Bridge, a 23-point captaincy haul at Old Trafford and four clean sheets for the patient. Every number below comes from the Statz FPL Stats tool filtered to Gameweek 2 only - no season totals, no vibes, just what actually happened in this round. Two gameweeks is far too early to judge a season, but it is exactly the right time to separate players whose points are backed by chances from players riding early variance. That distinction - output versus underlying numbers - runs through everything below. If you want to poke at the data yourself, the Gameweek 2 summary page and the Statz FPL hub are the places to start. Gameweek 2 in numbers The round's headline act was Manchester United 5-2 Ipswich , where Bruno Fernandes scored three and assisted another. Chelsea 4-3 Brighton was the game of the weekend, Crystal Palace 1-4 Manchester City saw Erling Haaland and Rayan Cherki share City's four goals, and Liverpool 2-2 Nottingham Forest gave us returns on both sides. Fernandes owned the round on every metric that matters: 23 points, 2.50 expected goal involvement (xGI) and a bonus points system score of 87, with 60 the next-best BPS in the round. Four teams kept clean sheets: Arsenal (1-0 at Aston Villa), Newcastle (2-0 at Spurs), Sunderland (1-0 against Fulham) and Hull (1-0 at Coventry). Hull keeper Konstantinos Tzolakis turned his shutout into 10 points with three bonus, while Newcastle's Lukas Hornicek added four saves to his clean sheet for 7 points at under 1% ownership. The round was cruel to some, too. Brentford's Igor Thiago (£8.0m, 15.0% owned) generated 0.80 xG and walked away with two points, and Coventry's Taiwo Awoniyi put up 0.93 xG in a game his side lost 1-0 to Hull without scoring. Both blanks looked nothing like the performances underneath them. At the other end of the glamour scale, Sunderland's Nordi Mukiele and Leeds' Tarik Muharemovic led the round with 19 defensive contributions apiece - Mukiele turning his into 9 points thanks to the clean sheet. And Bournemouth's Alex Scott banked the round's oddest 12-point haul: a goal, three bonus and a clean sheet in a 1-1 draw - he was off the pitch by the time Everton scored, so the clean-sheet points stayed with him. The big performances Bruno Fernandes (MID, £12.0m, 48.0% owned) - 23 points. The numbers behind the haul are the real story. Fernandes racked up 2.02 xG on his own - an enormous single-game number for a midfielder - and added 0.48 xA for a round-high 2.50 xGI. Three goals and an assist was not a hot streak; it was roughly what his chances deserved. Just under half the game owns him at 48.0%, and Gameweek 2 showed why. Bryan Mbeumo (MID, £8.0m, 31.6% owned) - 11 points. Lost in the Fernandes noise at Old Trafford: Mbeumo posted 1.76 xG and 1.97 xGI in the same match, the second-best underlying line of the entire round. He converted just once. If Manchester United keep creating at this rate, his 11 points may be the floor rather than the ceiling. Rayan Cherki (MID, £7.7m, 21.3% owned) - 14 points. Two goals from 0.35 xG in 81 minutes at Selhurst Park - clinical finishing rather than a chance avalanche, though the 0.55 xA underneath shows he was creating too. That made him the round's second-highest scorer overall, ahead of his Manchester City teammate Erling Haaland's 13 points (two goals from 0.66 xG at 69.9% ownership). Morgan Gibbs-White (MID, £7.9m, 8.9% owned) - 13 points. A goal backed by 0.79 xG, plus an assist, in Nottingham Forest 's 2-2 draw at Anfield. Under 9% of managers own him, and this was output earned the honest way. Joao Pedro (FWD, £7.6m, 69.6% owned) - 9 points. A goal, an assist and 1.23 xG in Chelsea 's 4-3 win over Brighton . The template forward did exactly what 69.6% of the game bought him to do. Players to watch This is not a buy list - it is the six players whose Gameweek 2 underlying numbers were better than their output. One week of xG tells you more about the next month than one week of points does, so these are the names to track. Cross-check them against the Statz FPL projections before you act. Phil Foden (MID, £7.0m, 4.6% owned). The watch pick of the round. Foden produced 0.87 xG and 0.45 xA - a 1.32 xGI - and somehow left Selhurst Park with two assists but no goal. At £7.0m and 4.6% ownership, the Gameweek 2 data says he is the cheapest route into City's attack by some distance - and his two assists mean the returns have already started arriving even while the goal has not. Thierno Barry (FWD, £5.5m, 4.1% owned). The round's biggest xGI without a single return: 1.48 xG in 69 minutes for Everton , two points to show for it. Strikers who rack up 1.48 xG in a game do not usually stay goalless for long, and at £5.5m the entry cost is trivial. Morgan Rogers (MID, £7.5m, 25.6% owned). A round-high 1.01 xA for just one assist in Chelsea's seven-goal thriller, 1.15 xGI in total. The creativity is real; the returns undercounted it. Wilson Isidor (FWD, £5.5m, 0.9% owned). The strangest line in the whole dataset: 1.39 xG in 26 minutes off the bench, converted once for Sunderland's winner against Fulham. Per minute, nobody in Gameweek 2 came close. His profile page is worth a bookmark while his ownership sits below 1%. Dan Ndoye (MID, £5.5m, 0.6% owned). A goal plus 0.63 xA in 65 minutes against Liverpool, 0.98 xGI in total. A £5.5m midfielder producing that line at 0.6% ownership is exactly what this column exists to flag. James Hill (DEF, £5.5m, 0.9% owned). The defender curio: 0.74 xA plus 12 defensive contributions in Bournemouth's draw with Everton, for four points. A defender creating that much while topping up the defensive-contribution floor is a budget watch, not a punt. The numbers flatter him One caution flag from the round: Pascal Gross (MID, £5.5m, 13.6% owned) walked away from Stamford Bridge with 13 points - a goal, an assist and maximum bonus - from 0.05 xG and 0.11 xA. That is a 0.16 xGI turned into a double-digit haul. It happens, and nobody is giving the points back, but Gameweek 2 gave no evidence that Gross is getting into scoring positions regularly. Chasing last week's points is the classic early-season trap; the underlying numbers on his Gameweek 2 stats line say this was variance, not a pattern forming. An honourable mention in the same category: Everton's James Tarkowski scored 12 points from a goal carrying just 0.10 xG. The difference is that Tarkowski's ten defensive contributions give his score a floor that Gross's does not have - for him, a low-xG goal is a bonus on top of the DC points, not the whole case. What Gameweek 3 asks The fixture ticker frames the next round around one fixture: Arsenal against Chelsea at the Emirates, while Manchester United visit Everton and Manchester City host Coventry. Check the predicted lineups before Friday's deadline, and run your shortlist through the projections - Gameweek 2's underlying numbers are the lead, but minutes are the currency. Dig into the Gameweek 2 data Every stat in this piece is one filter away in the FPL Stats tool - set the gameweek range to 2-2 and sort by whatever you care about, from xGI to defensive contributions. For the by-player view, the player profiles split every haul by opponent strength. September 1 253 comments 1 September 2026 253 comments As Manchester City prepare to host Coventry City in Gameweek 3, many Fantasy Premier League (FPL) managers are set to deploy the Triple Captain chip on Erling Haaland (£15.5m). Indeed, the leading chip in our Gameweek 3 poll is the Triple Captain . Around 30% of responders say they’re playing that chip this week. Here, we take a look at some of the pros and cons of using the Triple Captain chip on Haaland in Gameweek 3. Cherki, Mbeumo, Newcastle players: Buy, keep or sell in Gameweek 3? Score More Points. Win More Mini Leagues. Join FFScout. PROS ALREADY OFF THE MARK Haaland is up and running. He scored twice in the 4-1 away victory at Crystal Palace in Gameweek 2. First, he found the net with a looping header, before a powerhouse finish late on. Prior to that, he blanked at home to Bournemouth, but on another day, he scores plenty. With no signs of rustiness after the World Cup, Haaland has recorded nine shots in the box in the first two Gameweeks, the most of any player in FPL. Above: Erling Haaland’s shot map in 2026/27 HOME COMFORTS Haaland is usually a reliable option on home turf. Under Pep Guardiola last season, he amassed 120 points, with 15 goals and four assists in 17 matches at the Etihad Stadium. In that period, he supplied six double-digit hauls and averaged 7.4 points per match. Paired with elite underlying numbers, the Norwegian penalty-taker probably has the best Triple Captain credentials of any player. NEWLY-PROMOTED OPPOSITION Moreover, it’s newly-promoted Coventry at home in Gameweek 3. Frank Lampard’s men have lost both of their first two matches, having conceded four times to Arsenal and Hull City. They’ve failed to find the net, too. In truth, Coventry’s start to the 2026/27 season hasn’t been terrible, but they have lacked physicality and goal threat, a concern ahead of Saturday’s trip to City. It also sounds like playmaker Rayan Cherki (£7.7m) will be going all-out to assist Haaland in this match. “When I saw Enzo [Maresca] was going to change me, I didn’t like that and I need to show them that I want to play and want to score and give assists for Erling. Today I didn’t give a lot of balls for him [Haaland]. The next time I want to give Erling a lot of balls.” – Rayan Cherki in Gameweek 2 The chance that Haaland may get a Double Gameweek in the first half of the season is extremely unlikely, so using the Triple Captain chip at home to newly-promoted opposition looks like a solid play. TAKE ON THE WILDCARDERS This is a simple one. Plenty of engaged Fantasy managers are on a Wildcard this week, mostly those who opted not to start with Haaland. They can’t Triple Captain him because they are already playing a chip, so this could be an opportunity to take them on. GOOD XMINS Haaland has completed the full 90 minutes in both matches so far this season. That might not be the case later in the season, especially when you factor in Europe. For example, City host Ipswich in Gameweek 7. But on either side of that encounter, they have Champions League fixtures against Paris Saint-Germain and AEK Athens, followed by an early Saturday kick-off away at Aston Villa. His minutes are probably going to be more uncertain, then. articles.body: Aston Villa complete signing of Mbaye and Harwood-Bellis Skip to content News Football Transfer News, Rumours & Gossip Aston Villa complete signing of Mbaye and Harwood-Bellis Aston Villa have completed the signing of Ibrahim Mbaye from PSG. Mitch Fretton Last Update: 3 hours ago 3 min read Add us as a preferred source on Google Aston Villa have completed the signing of Senegal winger Ibrahim Mbaye from Paris Saint-Germain for a reported fee of £47m. The 18-year-old has signed for Unai Emery’s side after making 31 appearances for PSG last season, scoring three goals and providing two assists as the French club retained both the Ligue 1 and Champions League titles. Mbaye also featured in all four of Senegal’s matches at the 2026 World Cup, scoring in their 3-1 defeat by France. Born in France, Mbaye represented Les Bleus at youth level before switching his international allegiance to Senegal in 2025 through his father. The winger joined PSG from FC Versailles 78 in 2018 and progressed through the club’s academy before making his senior debut in August 2024 at the age of 16. Mbaye becomes the latest attacking addition to Emery’s squad following the arrivals of Alejandro Garnacho, Johan Manzambi and Nicolas Jackson. From Paris to Birmingham. The next chapter starts now. pic.twitter.com/v3TPMwxmrA — Aston Villa (@AstonVilla) September 1, 2026 Taylor Harwood-Bellis has also arrived from Southampton, in a deal worth £29m. Villa have invested heavily in their squad this summer but have also seen several important players leave the club. Morgan Rogers completed a British-record £117m move to Chelsea before England defender Ezri Konsa joined Arsenal for £55m. Striker Ollie Watkins has also departed Villa Park, completing a £51m move to Saudi Arabian club Al-Hilal. Table of Contents When does the summer transfer window 2026 close? What time does the Premier League transfer window shut on transfer deadline day? When does the summer transfer window close around Europe? When does the 2026/27 winter transfer window open? Can Premier League clubs sign players outside of the window? When does the summer transfer window 2026 close? The window opened on Monday June 15 and will shut on Tuesday September 1. After that, every Premier League club can register a squad of up to 25 players, 17 of whom are allowed to be non-Home Grown Players. A Home Grown Player has been registered with any club affiliated to the English or Welsh Football Association for three entire seasons or 36 months across their career before his 21st birthday, or the end of the season during which they turn 21. Under-21 players do not count towards the 25-man limit. What time does the Premier League transfer window shut on transfer deadline day? The deadline is 23:00 BST in the Premier League, but clubs can have an extra two hours to file the remaining documentation if they submit a deal sheet confirming that an agreement has been reached. The deal sheet must arrive fully completed before the transfer window closes. For international transfers, clubs also have to comply with the FIFA Transfer Matching System deadline of midnight. When does the summer transfer window close around Europe? There are slight variations between the major European leagues. Here’s when they shut. League Date BST close Premier League Sept 1 23:00 18:00 15:00 LaLiga Sept 1 22:59 17:59 14:59 Serie A Sept 1 19:00 14:00 11:00 Bundesliga Aug 31 19:00 14:00 11:00 Ligue 1 Aug 31 19:00 14:00 11:00 When does the 2026/27 winter transfer window open? The Premier League winter transfer window opens on Friday January 1, 2027 and closes on Monday February 1, 2027 at 23:00 BST. Can Premier League clubs sign players outside of the window? Clubs can only add players outside of transfer windows who are free agents and if they have room in their 25-man squad. Premier League teams can still announce deals with other clubs, but those players will not be registered to play until the window re-opens. This means there is usually little to no movement when the window closes, with four months to wait until the window re-opens. Players can be released by Premier League clubs at any time, but the usual rule is that they cannot sign for another side outside of the market. Topics Aston Villa F.C. Paris Saint-Germain F.C. Players can be released by Premier League clubs at any time, but the usual rule is that they cannot sign for another side outside of the market. Summer transfer window latest news Among Premier League clubs, there were two lavish moves in July when Manchester City paid Nottingham Forest £116 million for Elliot Anderson and Chelsea spent £117m to sign fellow England midfielder Morgan Rogers from Aston Villa. Tottenham spent £75m on Savinho from City, £85m to sign Portugal midfielder Mateus Fernandes from West Ham and broke their club record to add Italy playmaker Sandro Tonali for £100m from Newcastle, who also sold Brazil midfielder Bruno Guimaraes to Arsenal for £75m and brought in Ivory Coast winger Bazoumana Toure for £42m from Hoffenheim. New Liverpool head coach Andoni Iraola recruited defender Jeremy Jacquet from Rennes for £60m and Brighton & Hove Albion and Spurs traded defenders, with Jan Paul van Hecke joining Roberto De Zerbi’s squad for £52m and Luka Vuskovic heading in the opposite direction for £50m. Aston Villa spent £59.5m on one of the stars of the World Cup, adding Switzerland midfielder Johan Manzambi from Freiburg, £59.5m, and Chelsea’s business did not stop with Rogers’ arrival, signing defender Maxence Lacroix from Crystal Palace for £51m and selling full-back Marc Cucurella to Real Madrid for £51.8m and midfielder Andrey Santos to Manchester United for £50m. Manchester City sold England goalkeeper James Trafford to Leeds United for £40m, but new Cityzens head coach Enzo Maresca has hinted that an expected move for Chelsea and Argentina midfielder Enzo Fernandez will not materialise. Arsenal’s interest in Vinicius Junior ended when the Brazil forward signed a new deal with Real Madrid, who signed Ivory Coast international Yan Diomande from Leipzig for a fee of up to £120m. Barcelona opted not to sign Marcus Rashford despite the England forward’s successful season-long loan at the club from Manchester United, instead signing Newcastle and Three Lions wideman Anthony Gordon for £69.3m. Barca have also signed City midfielder Rodri for £65m, pouncing with the World Cup winner with Spain in the final year of his contract at the Premier League giants. Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta is off to the perfect start in 2026/27 (Image credit: Getty Images) Facebook Pinterest Email Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Few pundits or supporters could see anything other than Arsenal retaining the Premier League trophy this season before opening day. Mikel Arteta has strengthened his squad in all areas of the pitch, whilst the managerial changes at their major rivals over the last eight months have left them not yet in a position to challenge. The Spaniard’s side weren’t the most attractive title winners last term, as tension crept into their approach as they chased their first championship in 22 years, but they have started this campaign with renewed confidence. Arteta at Villa Park on Monday night (Image credit: Getty Images) Last season, Bukayo Saka , Kai Havertz and Martin Odegaard all had their lowest goal contributions in the last three years, so ensuring those attackers stay injury-free will naturally make some improvement. However, there are also clear indications that they are evolving stylistically, with new signings Bruno Guimaraes and Christos Tzolis adding more creativity. Back-to-back titles? You wouldn't bet against them (Image credit: Getty Images) The sample size for this season is still relatively small, but the midfield seems to be progressing the ball forward more quickly, as they show signs of greater variation in their attacks. Arsenal have only added centre-back Ezri Konsa this summer, though their full-backs are another area where they can increase their output in the final third. The best features, fun and footballing quizzes, straight to your inbox every week. Arteta likes to purchase full-backs who are comfortable in central areas, with Riccardo Calafiori, Jurrien Timber and Piero Hincapie all having spent considerable time at centre-back throughout their careers. This enables them to not only offer cover in the centre of defence, but also make runs inside their wingers, invert into central positions in possession and provide physicality from set-pieces. Calafiori is perhaps the most interesting example, as he was one of the best centre-backs in Serie A during the 2023/24 campaign. Riccardo Calafiori (Image credit: Getty Images) Under the management of Thiago Motta at Bologna , he illustrated his ability to carry the ball forward and make line-breaking passes, whilst simultaneously intercepting opposition attacks and winning duels against robust strikers. After moving to the Emirates, he switched back to the role which he had predominantly played in his formative years at Roma At Villa Park on Bank Holiday Monday, Unai Emery had clearly devised a plan to nullify his influence, with John McGinn playing on the right-hand side directly against him. John McGinn (Image credit: Getty Images) The Scotsman was happy to track him more centrally, whilst Boubacar Kamara and Matty Cash also took on the responsibility of monitoring the Italian as he glided into their area of the pitch. However, just before the hour mark, substitute Eberechi Eze played a pass inside and Calafiori displayed his athleticism to wrap his foot around and scoop the ball into the path of Saka, who bundled it past Aston Villa goalkeeper Zion Suzuki. After a discussion with Arteta, Calafiori and Arsenal almost repeated the move when Eze played him in once more, only for the offside flag to be raised just after the left-back had cleverly dragged the ball past a trailing Alysson. In the 97 minute, he was the furthest Arsenal player up the pitch as his team went in search of scoring a second. The Italian has been directly involved in a goal in his last three games, including his early finish in the Community Shield against Manchester City. "It was very different," said Arteta after the match when reminded his team had lost on their last visit to the ground. "That shows our maturity, and it shows we have players who can change the momentum and understand what is needed in the game." Calafiori is one of those players, and it would be a huge surprise if he didn’t record a seasonal best for goal contributions in Arsenal’s pursuit of back-to-back titles. articles.body: Sunderland close in on Fofana after Arsenal talks Skip to content News Football Transfer News, Rumours & Gossip Sunderland close in on Fofana after Arsenal talks Sunderland are closing in on a deal to sign Malick Fofana. Mitch Fretton Last Update: 11 hours ago 3 min read Add us as a preferred source on Google Sunderland have reached an agreement to sign Lyon winger Malick Fofana, with the Belgium international set to undergo a medical before completing his move to the Stadium of Light. The 21-year-old has been given permission to travel to the north east ahead of signing a five-year contract, with Sunderland holding an option to extend the deal by a further 12 months. Some paperwork still needs to be completed, but the transfer is expected to go through before Tuesday night’s deadline. Fofana had emerged as a target for Arsenal, with The Athletic reporting on Monday that the Gunners were considering a move for the winger. He had previously been on their radar and had spoken with Mikel Arteta. Sunderland have been active in the transfer market this summer as they prepare for their return to the Premier League and Europa League football. Regis Le Bris’ side have brought in Thomas Meunier, Dayann Methalie and midfielder Jules Ahoka, while attacking additions have also been a priority. 🚨 BREAKING: Sunderland have agreed a deal to sign Malick Fofana from Lyon. 🛩️ The winger has been given permission to travel for a medical. ❓ Arsenal were also interested. ✍🏼 Permanent 5-year deal for the Belgian. 🇧🇪 #SAFC pic.twitter.com/1lU2UeU34j — Keith Downie (@SkySports_Keith) September 1, 2026 The Black Cats explored moves for Marseille winger Igor Paixao and Manchester City forward Jack Grealish, although Grealish is now set to return to Everton on loan. Fofana has made six appearances for Lyon this season, scoring twice. He found the net in the second leg of their Champions League play-off defeat by Fenerbahce before scoring in their opening Ligue 1 victory over Toulouse. The winger has scored 19 goals in 83 appearances for Lyon since joining from Gent for €17m in January 2024. Table of Contents When does the summer transfer window 2026 close? What time does the Premier League transfer window shut on transfer deadline day? When does the summer transfer window close around Europe? When does the 2026/27 winter transfer window open? Can Premier League clubs sign players outside of the window? When does the summer transfer window 2026 close? The window opened on Monday June 15 and will shut on Tuesday September 1. After that, every Premier League club can register a squad of up to 25 players, 17 of whom are allowed to be non-Home Grown Players. A Home Grown Player has been registered with any club affiliated to the English or Welsh Football Association for three entire seasons or 36 months across their career before his 21st birthday, or the end of the season during which they turn 21. Under-21 players do not count towards the 25-man limit. What time does the Premier League transfer window shut on transfer deadline day? The deadline is 23:00 BST in the Premier League, but clubs can have an extra two hours to file the remaining documentation if they submit a deal sheet confirming that an agreement has been reached. The deal sheet must arrive fully completed before the transfer window closes. For international transfers, clubs also have to comply with the FIFA Transfer Matching System deadline of midnight. When does the summer transfer window close around Europe? There are slight variations between the major European leagues. Here’s when they shut. The Premier League winter transfer window opens on Friday January 1, 2027 and closes on Monday February 1, 2027 at 23:00 BST. Can Premier League clubs sign players outside of the window? Clubs can only add players outside of transfer windows who are free agents and if they have room in their 25-man squad. Premier League teams can still announce deals with other clubs, but those players will not be registered to play until the window re-opens. This means there is usually little to no movement when the window closes, with four months to wait until the window re-opens. Players can be released by Premier League clubs at any time, but the usual rule is that they cannot sign for another side outside of the market. Topics Arsenal F.C. Premier League Sunderland A.F.C. ARS 6.9m 27/08 Hincapie ARS 5.4m 27/08 Madueke ARS 6.4m 27/08 P.M.Sarr TOT 4.9m 27/08 Sarr CRY 6.4m Scout Notes FPL notes: Mosquera injury latest + Tzolis off at half-time September 1 291 comments 1 September 2026 291 comments Arsenal have carried on where they left off last season, winning their first two Premier League games of 2026/27 to nil. A solitary goal from Bukayo Saka (£9.5m) saw the Gunners edge out Aston Villa, who at least made some small strides after their Gameweek 1 pasting at the Amex. Here are our Scout Notes, which feature data and screenshots from our new Match Centre. MOSQUERA INJURY LATEST + KONSA MAKES DEBUT The much-touted full debut for Ezri Konsa (£4.4m) didn’t materialise, as Cristhian Mosquera (£5.5m) kept his place in an unchanged backline. The entire Arsenal XI was the same as Gameweek 1, in fact. But Konsa did make it onto the pitch for his Gunners bow, replacing Mosquera after the 79th minute. The latter had needed medical treatment before coming off but Mikel Arteta said it was a precautionary withdrawal. “He’s fine, but he was feeling like he was about to have something, and that’s why we have the bench that we have, and that’s why we had to bring Ezri in.” – Mikel Arteta on Cristhian Mosquera Still, you wonder if Konsa will now be promoted to the line-up in Gameweek 3, having now had his first taste of action with his new club. “Really happy with Ezri, as well, because it was a really tricky debut to come here to your ex-club and just contain that emotion and play really focused. I think he was brilliant.” – Mikel Arteta on Ezri Konsa TZOLIS HOOKED – AND REPLACEMENT EZE PRAISED Coming off even earlier than Konsa was Christos Tzolis (£6.5m). The 24%-owned winger failed to emerge for the second half, having had a bit of a stinker before the interval. He’d been booked, too. The Greek wide-man, so impressive in the weeks preceding this game, didn’t complete a single cross, take-on or pass into the Villa box. Arteta didn’t mention the rationale behind that half-time withdrawal but did hail the impact of Eberechi Eze (£6.4m), who replaced Tzolis on the left wing. The England international ‘assisted the assister’ for Arsenal’s only goal of the game. “Ebs comes in, he makes a difference to win the game. “We knew that he could create an action. He created three actions that he put people almost looking at the goalkeeper one-against-one, but as well I have to trust him. When they make the rotation, especially on the right-hand side, and Cash’s goal, last year he lost him, we conceded the goal – and this year, I think he learned a lesson because every time something was happening he was at it, and I think he helped the team in a great way.” – Mikel Arteta on Eberechi Eze High praise for Tzolis’ replacement, then, which may be a bit of a concern ahead of Gameweek 3. Arteta has even ruled out the prospect of signing other attackers before tonight’s transfer deadline. “As I said, we’re trying to improve the squad until tomorrow night. We’re going to try to do that. I’ve been disconnected from the world for 24 hours because I think my energy and focus has to be on the match, but I will get back on it now.” – Mikel Arteta, when asked if he was planning to bolster his left-wing options ANOTHER GOAL FOR SAKA, ANOTHER ASSIST FOR CALAFIORI Saka notched a goal for the second successive Gameweek, while Riccardo Calafiori (£5.6m) now has back-to-back assists to his name. We didn’t see as much of the Italian international getting forward – Ben White (£5.5m) had over twice as many final-third touches – but he was there when it mattered for the winner, running inside of Eze and squaring for Saka to tap in. The in-form defender had gone close with a set-piece attempt of his own earlier. Encouragingly, he lasted 90 minutes (as did Saka and White), too. “He’s been great. He’s been much more consistent. I think he’s been training every single day and you can see that his emotional state is high. I think physically is in a really good place.” – Mikel Arteta on Riccardo Calafiori THE ARCHETYPAL ARSENAL DISPLAY Arsenal were a bit raggedy with their passing at times, gifting Villa the ball in some dangerous areas, while their final ball at the other end was often lacking. But we’re only two Gameweeks in, and we can expect some cobwebs at this early stage of 2026/27. Otherwise, this was the archetypal Arsenal display. Defence is their strong suit, and they restricted Villa to precious little. Even the hosts’ closest effort, an Emi Buendia (£6.0m) strike from distance that clipped the top of the bar, very likely would have been disallowed, had it gone in, for a foul in the build-up. A Nicholas Jackson (£6.5m) cross that evaded everyone, an off-target Ian Maatsen (£4.5m) effort and a blocked Matty Cash (£4.5m) shot were about the best of the rest, but Villa didn’t really threaten the clean sheet. David Raya (£6.0m) didn’t have a save to make. Another strength is set plays. We’ve already mentioned Calafiori’s chance, while Gabriel Magalhaes (£8.0m) perhaps should have scored from a Declan Rice (£7.5m) corner, with Zion Suzuki (£5.0m) flapping. The one stick used to beat Arsenal with is their lack of open-play threat. In fact, at Villa Park, they had only four such shots (‘SP’ below is set-play attempts): Still, you never get the feeling they’re really panicking, probing patiently while they’re waiting for that one opening, knowing that one chance may be enough, given their superiority at the back. Not great to watch, but often effective. RICE BANKS DEFCON AT THE LAST! There’s a boost for Rice owners this morning! After the data refresh, the midfielder has joined Gabriel in banking DefCon points. Saka remains just one contribution away. BETTER FROM VILLA Anything after Gameweek 1 was going to be an improvement for Villa, and it always looked like the opening weekend was a ‘bottoming out’ period, with the squad decimated and looking morale-sapped following some high-profile exits. The ranks have been bolstered since, with Jackson and Suzuki making their full debuts here. Aaron Wan-Bissaka (£4.5m) and Alejandro Garnacho (£5.9m) appeared from the bench, too. It was a workmanlike display, with chances at a premium, but Arsenal are going to stifle most teams. Hull City in Gameweek 3 will be more of an acid test as to where they are with their rebuild. “Today, I think we compete fantastic collectively, tactically as well. The team responded fantastic. This is the way.” – Unai Emery £4.5m midfielder George Hemmings made another start for the Villans, although you wonder how long his run in the team will last, with Buendia and Garnacho able to take up his left-wing role, and Joao Gomes (£5.5m), Johan Manzambi (£5.9m) and Leon Goretzka (£6.0m) still to return in central positions. To smooth discussions and meet the Italian club's evaluation, the Blues are prepared to send 22-year-old winger Jamie Gittens to the Stadio Olimpico. World Cup winner Fernandez remains subject to transfer interest from Manchester City , with a big-money move to the Etihad Stadium looking increasingly likely before the deadline passes. articles.body: Grealish set for Everton return from Manchester City Skip to content News Football Transfer News, Rumours & Gossip Grealish set for Everton return from Manchester City Jack Grealish will be returning to Everton from Manchester City on loan. Mitch Fretton Last Update: 11 hours ago 3 min read Add us as a preferred source on Google Everton have agreed a deal to re-sign Jack Grealish on a season-long loan from Manchester City. The 30-year-old is set to undergo a medical with the Toffees, with the move expected to be completed before Tuesday’s 23:00 BST transfer deadline. Grealish spent much of last season at Everton on loan, scoring twice and providing six assists in 20 appearances before a foot injury ended his campaign in January. The England winger had attracted interest from several clubs, including boyhood side Aston Villa, but his preference was to return to Everton. Everton chief executive Angus Kinnear said the club had “remained in contact” with Grealish throughout the summer. The Toffees are looking to add to their attacking options after winger Iliman Ndiaye is expected to complete a £65m move to Manchester City. Everton also appear close to signing Monaco and USA forward Folarin Balogun in a £40m deal, while their attempt to bring Richarlison back from Tottenham has stalled over personal terms. 🚨💣 BREAKING: Jack Grealish will undergo medical as new Everton player on Tuesday morning, here we go! Deal agreed with Manchester City on loan with green light from Jack tonight. 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁥󠁮󠁧󠁿 #EFC been pushing for several days and now got Grealish back – follows @David_Ornstein pic.twitter.com/6cDP00erVw — Fabrizio Romano (@FabrizioRomano) August 31, 2026 Grealish joined City from Aston Villa for £100m in August 2021 but has made only two appearances for Enzo Maresca’s side this season. He came off the bench in the Community Shield defeat by Arsenal before also featuring as a substitute in City’s Premier League win over Bournemouth. Table of Contents When does the summer transfer window 2026 close? What time does the Premier League transfer window shut on transfer deadline day? When does the summer transfer window close around Europe? When does the 2026/27 winter transfer window open? Can Premier League clubs sign players outside of the window? When does the summer transfer window 2026 close? The window opened on Monday June 15 and will shut on Tuesday September 1. After that, every Premier League club can register a squad of up to 25 players, 17 of whom are allowed to be non-Home Grown Players. A Home Grown Player has been registered with any club affiliated to the English or Welsh Football Association for three entire seasons or 36 months across their career before his 21st birthday, or the end of the season during which they turn 21. Under-21 players do not count towards the 25-man limit. What time does the Premier League transfer window shut on transfer deadline day? The deadline is 23:00 BST in the Premier League, but clubs can have an extra two hours to file the remaining documentation if they submit a deal sheet confirming that an agreement has been reached. The deal sheet must arrive fully completed before the transfer window closes. For international transfers, clubs also have to comply with the FIFA Transfer Matching System deadline of midnight. When does the summer transfer window close around Europe? There are slight variations between the major European leagues. Here’s when they shut. League Date BST close Premier League Sept 1 23:00 18:00 15:00 LaLiga Sept 1 22:59 17:59 14:59 Serie A Sept 1 19:00 14:00 11:00 Bundesliga Aug 31 19:00 14:00 11:00 Ligue 1 Aug 31 19:00 14:00 11:00 When does the 2026/27 winter transfer window open? The Premier League winter transfer window opens on Friday January 1, 2027 and closes on Monday February 1, 2027 at 23:00 BST. Can Premier League clubs sign players outside of the window? Clubs can only add players outside of transfer windows who are free agents and if they have room in their 25-man squad. Premier League teams can still announce deals with other clubs, but those players will not be registered to play until the window re-opens. This means there is usually little to no movement when the window closes, with four months to wait until the window re-opens. Players can be released by Premier League clubs at any time, but the usual rule is that they cannot sign for another side outside of the market. Topics Everton F.C. Manchester City F.C. Andoni Iraola (Image credit: Getty Images) Facebook Pinterest Email Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google At the start of the summer, most Liverpool supporters and observers would have identified three key areas of the team that needed addressing in the transfer market. The obvious was a winger to effectively replace Mohamed Salah. In signing Bradley Barcola, Liverpool have done that but on the opposite wing. Barcola , though, you could argue, is actually the replacement for Luis Diaz, who departed the year before. Liverpool's glaring right-back issue Trent Alexander-Arnold holds the Premier League trophy amid Liverpool's title celebrations at Anfield in May 2025 (Image credit: Getty Images) The next two positions that most supporters would have wanted to see addressed also revolved around the lack of replacing other previously departed legends. Fabinho left Liverpool three years ago now, but still his role in midfield as a defence-first player hasn’t been replaced. Have Liverpool replaced Fabinho yet? Many fans don't think so (Image credit: Getty Images) While Trent Alexander-Arnold left a year ago and no matter how hard he tries, Jeremie Frimpong simply isn’t a replacement, or even an actual right back. Liverpool, though, have gone through the summer seemingly without any desire to add either a midfielder or a right-back, despite the clear need in each instance. The best features, fun and footballing quizzes, straight to your inbox every week. Arguably it’s at right-back which is the biggest issue, although both full-back positions are areas of major concern and this was highlighted in the 2-2 draw with Nottingham Forest - Andoni Iraola's first home game in charge. Frimpong and Milos Kerkez were hooked in the 72nd minute, with Liverpool 2-1 down at the time. Now, there are potentially several other reasons (not least youngster Trey Nyoni's impressive cameo in midfield) why Iraola’s team enjoyed their best 20 minutes of the game from that point on, but certainly a contributing factor was the full-backs being replaced. Szoboszlai can learn like Milner - and become a better midfielder Dominik Szobsozlai, as he was regularly last season, moved to right-back, immediately giving Liverpool a player who can actually put in a cross and also be defensively stronger than the player he was replacing. The Hungarian might not necessarily like playing there, but Iraola could do far worse than have the same conversation Jurgen Klopp had with James Milner in 2016 in explaining how he wanted the midfielder to be his left-back for the season ahead. A year later, Milner explained what he learned in the new position: “But at times you have to curb that and adapt to the match situation and maybe sometimes hold back a bit if the time of the game suits that. I think sensing danger early is the biggest thing to learn. When you play in midfield you’re obviously always switched on to defending.” Dominik Szoboszlai was occasionally used at right-back by Arne Slot last season (Image credit: Getty Images) Those words about “sensing danger early” are incredibly timely, with Iraola’s pre-Nottingham Forest press conference featuring a very similar message when discussing his midfield’s need to find a balance after being caught out twice by Newcastle in the opening fixture. “There are players that are very good, they’re smelling, ‘OK, there is real danger, I can’t take the risk of going (forward),” explained Iraola. “Now I think I have to stay’. “Recognising those situations is the job we have to do now.” A season at right-back, then, would actually help Szoboszlai learn that side of his game and make him a better midfielder in future. That should be the message Iraola gives him in order to get the Reds’ No. 8 to buy into the role. Would Szoboszlai particularly enjoy it? Probably not, but it’s about what’s best for the team, as Milner succinctly explained: “It’s about whatever’s best for the team and ultimately I just want to be out there playing games, contributing and helping this football club.” And if Szoboszlai has designs on becoming Liverpool captain after Virgil van Dijk departs, then a selfless season at right back would show he puts the team first and give him a new understanding of the team and overall patterns of play. Liverpool solve two issues with Szoboszlai role change Dominik Szoboszlai (Image credit: Getty Images) For Liverpool, they’d be getting a far more reliable outlet on the right, who can produce crosses like the one Szoboszlai did for Alexander Isak against Forest, which the £125 million man couldn’t get on the end of. No Liverpool player had more touches, created more chances or made more accurate crosses than Szoboszlai against Forest. He made three stat-recorded accurate crosses, while Frimpong and Kerkez made none between them. The duo attempted six, with none of them finding their target. It was a similar story against Newcastle the week before. Of course, stats on crossing is pretty flawed, a player can produce a wonderful cross but if the forward doesn’t get on the end of it, it’s recorded as a failed cross. The eye test tells us that Szoboszlai’s crossing was significantly better than Frimpong’s versus Forest. Of that there is no doubt. He can also move inside more to create numbers-up situations in midfield, again more akin to Alexander-Arnold did. Liverpool’s focus on signing attacking wingers for Iraola this summer has neglected the right-back and midfield positions, but moving Szobsozlai fixes both, at least temporarily. If Iraola is serious about getting the best out of his squad, and Szoboszlai is serious about being a team player, it’s a change that would significantly benefit Liverpool this season. As well as writing about Liverpool for FourFourTwo he also contributes to other titles including Yahoo and Bleacher Report. He is a lifelong fan of the Reds. She joined City in summer 2024 and after an injury-affected first season, last season scored 10 goals and made five assists to help City win their first league title in a decade. “Every single league title is special for different reasons,” Miedema said. It was really special to be part of it and to be able to celebrate the league and FA Cup win as well.” After six years of dominance, it was going to take a lot to knock Chelsea off their pedestal. But new manager Jeglertz, aided by a lack of Champions League football due to a fourth-placed finish in the 2024/25 season, helped City do just that. “Coming in last summer, there were a lot of changes, new people coming in and a new coach coming in. This year, the league has expanded by two teams to a field of 14 teams. A number of high profile players have also joined the WSL this season, something Miedema says speaks volumes of where the league is at. “It’s amazing to see that so many big players want to come play in England and that the league has increased by two teams as well,” she added. “It’s only going to get more exciting and more difficult to actually win it. To be in the league now and try to be successful again is going to be extremely difficult. But isnt’t that why we love football? “That’s the reason every good player wants to come to England, because you want to measure yourself against the best.” After a season away from Champions League football, City will be back competing against Europe’s best. “I’m really excited to be back but it's going to be tough because you're going to be travelling a lot, you're going to be playing a lot of games. “I think some of the girls will have to get used to it. But it's a competition you want to be playing and you want to measure yourself with the best in Europe. “I can't wait to see how we do in the Champions League because it’s a completely different challenge to playing in the WSL.” TOPICS Ayisha Gulati Women's Football Writer Ayisha Gulati is the women's football writer at FourFourTwo . Fresh from a summer covering the Lionesses’ triumphant Euro 2025 campaign in Switzerland, she brings a passion for all things WSL, UWCL, and international women’s football. She has interviewed names including Alessia Russo and Aitana Bonmati and enjoys telling stories that capture the excitement on and off the pitch. articles.title: Saka salutes Arsenal’s defensive resolve after hard-fought Villa win: ‘Without the ball we were incredible’
articles.excerpt: Bukayo Saka has hailed his Arsenal team-mates for their performance against Aston Villa.
articles.source_type: Weekly five-players-to-buy and players-to-avoid pieces, injury-doubt round-ups
articles.body: Saka salutes Arsenal's defensive resolve after hard-fought Villa win: 'Without the ball we were incredible' Skip to content Football News Premier League News Saka salutes Arsenal’s defensive resolve after hard-fought Villa win: ‘Without the ball we were incredible’ Bukayo Saka has hailed his Arsenal team-mates for their performance against Aston Villa. Mitch Fretton Last Update: 21 hours ago 3 min read Add us as a preferred source on Google Bukayo Saka has praised Arsenal’s defensive work as the foundation of their 1-0 win at Aston Villa on Bank Holiday Monday, insisting the champions showed exactly the kind of resilience required to mount a serious title defence. Saka’s close-range finish just before the hour mark was the difference between the sides at Villa Park, the winger converting Riccardo Calafiori’s low cross after a slick move that released the pair of them in behind a high Villa line. It was Arsenal’s second consecutive win and second consecutive clean sheet to open the new campaign, with Mikel Arteta marking his 250th Premier League game in charge of the club with maximum points. “Very, very tough game. It’s not easy coming here, they made it hard for us. It feels even better to come out with the win,” Saka said. “The way they defend, really compact and with a high line, they caught us offside. We had to adapt to that. Different from what we faced last week, we weren’t able to implement our attacking pattern. “One goal is normally enough for us because we are so solid at the back. When we got the first one, it actually opened the game up. We wanted to push for the second one.” The winger singled out Arsenal’s full-back play as a key contributor to their attacking threat, before returning to the theme of their defensive performance as the match’s defining feature. “All the full-backs, the way they play gives us a lot. For us wingers, it opens up the game for us, we’ve always got composure in the box,” he said. “We weren’t at our highest level with the ball. Without it, we were incredible. As soon as we lost it, we were running back. We knew that they liked to play in transition. All the boys put in a shift tonight. It helps with a clean sheet.” Arteta on squad depth Villa offered precious little in terms of attacking threat throughout, they have not registered a shot on target in either of their two opening Premier League fixtures, the first time any team has achieved that since Swansea City in 2017-18. Arsenal, however, could not afford complacency against a side stung by the 4-0 defeat to Brighton on the opening weekend, and Arteta acknowledged as much. “This is a really difficult place to come and win the game. Last season we lost in the last kick of the game. They were hurt after what happened last week. It was a great squad performance tonight,” he said. Arteta was asked whether this represents his strongest-ever squad in terms of depth. “That is what we need. The players that come in make the difference. All of them contributed to create more dominance and more momentum,” he said. “The level of focus and the way they want to contribute to the team, that is going to be decisive in the season.” Topics Arsenal F.C.
