articles.title: How AI Football Predictions Work: The Models, the Data and the Limits
articles.excerpt: AI football predictions are everywhere, but few sites explain what is actually happening under the hood. This is the full picture: the data that goes in, how projections become probabilities, why simulation beats picking winners, and the things no model can know.
articles.source_type: Head-to-head player comparison, goalkeeper and position value analysis
articles.body: How AI Football Predictions Work - Models, Data and Limits How AI Football Predictions Work: The Models, the Data and the Limits Type "AI football predictions" into a search engine and you will find everything from serious statistical models to anonymous accounts posting five-fold accumulators with a robot emoji. The phrase has become marketing shorthand, which makes it hard to know what you are actually being sold. This guide explains what a genuine AI football prediction is: the data that goes in, the modelling steps that turn that data into probabilities, why good systems simulate matches rather than pick winners, and - just as important - what no model can know. By the end you should be able to look at any prediction site, including our own AI football predictions , and judge it on substance. The data that goes in Every credible model starts with structured event data, collected match by match. For Statz that means, for every team and every player: Results and match events - goals, shots, shots on target, corners, fouls, tackles, cards, passes, recorded consistently across competitions. Expected goals (xG) - a quality-weighted measure of chances created and conceded, which stabilises much faster than raw goal counts. You can see this data on our Premier League xG table Minutes and lineups - who actually plays, for how long, and in what role. A striker's per-90 numbers mean nothing if he starts on the bench, so expected lineups and minutes projections feed directly into every player-level prediction. Context - venue, competition, schedule congestion and opponent strength, so a midfielder's four tackles against a possession-dominant side are weighted differently from four tackles against a team that never keeps the ball. Quantity matters less than consistency. A model trained on clean, consistently defined data across seasons will beat a bigger model fed inconsistent numbers, which is why serious providers obsess over data definitions before they obsess over algorithms. From raw stats to projections Raw averages are a bad predictor. A team averaging 6 corners a game may have faced a run of weak opponents; a defender averaging 2.5 tackles may have played three matches as an emergency full-back. The modelling step that fixes this is the projection : an opponent-adjusted, venue-adjusted, lineup-aware estimate of what a team or player should produce in one specific fixture. Conceptually the model asks: given how this attack performs against defences of this quality, at this venue, with these expected personnel, how many shots, corners, cards and goals should we expect? The output is a set of fixture-specific numbers - not "Arsenal average 15 shots" but "Arsenal project to 13.2 shots against this specific opponent's block". Player projections stack a second layer on top: the player's share of his team's projected output, adjusted for role and minutes. That is how a system prices a line like "2+ shots on target" for a winger - his share of a fixture-specific team projection, not his season average, with a hit rate showing how often he has cleared that line before. This is exactly what powers the Statz Bet Builder Tool Why simulation beats picking winners Once you have projections, there are two roads. The naive one is classification: train a model to output "home win", "draw" or "away win". The better one - the one Statz uses - is simulation . Goals in football arrive roughly according to a Poisson process, which means that from a projected number of goals for each side you can simulate the match thousands of times and count outcomes. Simulation wins for three reasons: One model, every market. From the same simulated matches you can read off win probabilities, correct scores, both teams to score, and over/under lines for goals, corners and cards - all internally consistent with each other. No false confidence. A simulation never says "Arsenal will win". It says Arsenal win 54% of simulations, draw 24%, lose 22% - which is the only honest way to describe a football match in advance. Value detection. Probabilities can be compared directly to bookmaker odds. If the model says 54% and the odds imply 48%, that gap is the entire basis of data-driven betting - see our expected value guide You can watch this exact process run on any fixture with the free Statz Match Simulator , which simulates from projection-anchored Poisson models and shows the full probability spread rather than a single pick. Where Elo ratings fit Elo ratings - the chess-derived system where teams trade rating points based on results and opponent strength - are often mentioned alongside AI football predictions. Elo is a useful team strength signal: it is simple, self-correcting and hard to fool over a season. But on its own it is a blunt instrument, because it sees only results, not performances. A team winning repeatedly while being outshot keeps gaining Elo right up until the regression arrives. Modern systems therefore use Elo-style ratings as one input among many, blended with xG-based performance measures that see through scorelines. If a site describes itself as an "Elo rating football prediction" service, that is a reasonable foundation - but performance-adjusted models have more information to work with. Player props: the most model-friendly markets It may seem backwards, but the markets AI handles best are not match winners - they are the unglamorous player stat lines. Shots, fouls, tackles and passes are high-frequency events driven by stable factors: role, minutes, team style and opponent. A ball-winning midfielder attempts tackles every match because of how he plays, and much of that persists from week to week; match results, by contrast, swing on a deflection or a red card. That stability is why hit rates on player props are the most actionable output a model produces, and why our players-in-form picks work the way they do: The general principle for using any prediction system: trust it most where the underlying event is frequent and role-driven, and least where a single moment decides everything. What the models cannot know Anyone selling AI predictions without this section is selling something else. Things no model sees coming: Red cards and injuries in-play. A sending-off after ten minutes invalidates every pre-match projection. Models price the average frequency of these events, not their timing. Team news inside the final hour. Projections assume expected lineups. A surprise rotation - especially in cup competitions or congested weeks - moves player props sharply, which is why checking confirmed lineups before acting on any projection is non-negotiable. Motivation and dead rubbers. Data reflects what teams have done, not what they privately intend to do with a second-string XI in a match that means nothing to them. Small-sample chaos. Early season, new signings, new managers - projections lean on priors until real data accumulates, and priors are sometimes wrong. Variance, always. A perfectly calibrated 60% prediction loses four times out of ten. Over a weekend, anything can happen; models only separate from luck over hundreds of matches. How to judge any prediction model Three tests separate real systems from noise: Does it show its working? A probability, a projection, a hit rate - something checkable. A pick with no number behind it is an opinion. Does it publish a settled record? Every pick, including the losers. Statz keeps its ledger on the football tips page for exactly this reason - judge the models there, not on our copy. Is it calibrated? Over a big sample, do its 60% predictions land about 60% of the time? This is a stronger test than raw win rate, because it measures whether the probabilities mean what they claim. If you want to put the theory to work, start with the Statz AI predictions hub - every tool there exposes the projection behind the prediction, so you can apply these tests to us first. The Bees netted in the first-half via Kevin Schade (£6.0m), before Dominic Calvert-Lewin (£6.0m) equalised for Leeds late on. Here are our Scout Notes from Elland Road. FPL Gameweek 2: Sunday’s goals, assists, bonus + DefCon points MATCH STATS: Leeds United v Brentford stats in our Match Centre CALVERT-LEWIN OFF THE MARK Calvert-Lewin’s late strike earned a point for Leeds, who somewhat uncharacteristically found it difficult to keep pace with Brentford for much of this encounter. You won’t get an easier finish from Calvert-Lewin, who tapped into an empty net from a few yards out, stabbing home substitute Lukas Nmecha ’s (£5.5m) low cross. But the point felt like a decent one for Leeds, after Brentford had controlled most of the match. Daniel Farke made one alteration to his line-up from their opener, with Noah Okafor (£5.9m) in for Harry Wilson (£6.5m), who was on the bench. However, after a slow start, Farke switched his system at half-time, moving to a back four. Wilson and Ao Tanaka (£5.0m) came on for Jaka Bijol (£5.0m) and Brenden Aaronson (£5.5m), with the substitutions eventually paying off. RODON INJURY LATEST In a blow for Leeds, Joe Rodon (£4.5m) had to be subbed off in the first half with a suspected hamstring injury. The severity of the issue will now be assessed ahead of Saturday’s trip to Brighton and Hove Albion. “It looks like hamstring injury, so it was not possible for him to sprint and to run, it was painful. We have to assess him right now. “I hope he’s not out too long because he’s a key player, and especially also in the centre position, we don’t have too many senior options. It was a difficult game for Nico Elvedi to come in, and I’m happy how he adapted to this game. “Thank God, we have him meanwhile with us. But yeah, of course, it would be a big blow if Joe’s out for a while.” – Daniel Farke on Joe Rodon New arrival Nico Elvedi (£4.5m) came on in his place, but a spell out for Rodon would leave Leeds short in this position, something they might potentially look to address before tomorrow’s transfer deadline. Gabriel Gudmundsson (£4.5m), meanwhile, returned to the bench against Brentford. DANGO BENCHED, ANDREWS ON LEWIS-POTTER There were two alterations for Brentford from their opener. Jaidon Anthony (£6.0m) came in on the right wing for Dango Ouattara (£6.5m), while Mikkel Damsgaard (£5.5m) replaced Mathias Jensen (£5.5m), who missed out due to a slight strain suffered in training. In his pre-match press conference, Andrews had discussed rotation. “I think the most challenging part at times is when you leave really good players, really good people out of the starting line-up, but I’m always quick to remind people we won’t achieve anything with 11 players. It has to be a team effort, it has to be a squad effort on any given day. And the impact that we can have from the bench is going to be key throughout the season.” – Keith Andrews Rewarded for his fine midweek performance, Anthony failed to really take his chance. However, Brentford’s winger on the opposite flank, Schade, did impress. A constant threat down the left, he netted his first goal of the season with a clever finish, guiding the ball into the far corner with the outside of his boot. Left-back Keane Lewis-Potter (£5.5m) supplied the assist, his second attacking return of the season. New positional rival El Hadji Malick Diouf (£4.5m) was on the bench on Sunday. When asked if Lewis-Potter could move further forward due to Diouf’s presence, Keith Andrews said… “What I like about Keane Lewis is he’s versatile. I think it’s a super strength. And then sometimes when you are that versatile, you struggle to nail down one position. I think that’s pretty fair, when you scrutinise that, but he’s so invaluable to have in the squad. I mentioned it a few weeks ago, before we signed Malick, that I can envisage Keane playing in different positions throughout the season and I don’t think that will change.” – Keith Andrews on Keane Lewis-Potter As for Igor Thiago (£8.0m), he had a couple of decent opportunities to put Brentford back in front. His header was first parried by James Trafford (£5.0m), before the Brazilian put the rebound into the side netting. Above: Igor Thiago’s xG shot map v Leeds Two of Thiago’s misses on Sunday were Opta ‘big chances’. That’s three he’s now missed in the first two Gameweeks, the joint-most of any player. All in all, however, this was another positive display from Brentford. “We laid some really solid foundations last season that we want to build upon and it has been a good start to the season. We looked very calm and confident in the first half.” – Keith Andrews USUAL SUSPECTS BANK DEFCON The usual suspects banked defensive contribution (DefCon) points at Elland Road: the impressive Tarik Muharemovic (£5.0m), Anton Stach (£6.0m), Kristoffer Ajer (£4.5m), Nathan Collins (£5.5m) and Mamadou Sangare (£5.6m). Ethan Ampadu (£5.5m) wasn’t far off, either. As for Sangare, he had another positive run-out against Brentford. Not only did he bank DefCon for the second successive Gameweek, but he also recorded three shots from in/around the box. “He’s an all-round midfielder. He’s not a holding midfielder, he’s not an attacking midfielder – he does a bit of everything. He’s got really good game understanding and he plays with a nice edge that I really like.” – Keith Andrews on Mamadou Sangare 85 Comments Login to Post a Comment Previous First Last » Next AC/DC AFC 1 day, 8 hours ago OFFICIAL: Allan Elias has signed a five-year #ManCity contract until 2031, subject to international clearance https://x.com/City_Xtra/status/2094395630471057762 Open Controls Permalink Login To Reply el polako 1 day, 8 hours ago Who dat? But shortly after signing a new contract in 2019 and just weeks after he started in Chelsea’s 4-1 Europa League final win over Arsenal , the Brazilian defender signed for the Gunners in an £8million deal. The reason for making this bold move across the capital with the ink on his new deal still wet was a simple one - the hiring of his former teammate Frank Lampard as Chelsea boss. Pick the ultimate 4-4-2 line-up from players in FourFourTwo's definitive Top 100 List Luiz on why Lampard’s Chelsea wasn’t for him Luiz has recently turned 30 when Lampard, fresh from a stint on charge of Derby County, was handed the Stamford Bridge top job, but age was not a factor for Luiz, who is still playing as a 39-year-old for Cypriot side Pafos. “I was already over 30 and had renewed my contract with Chelsea,” Luiz tells FourFourTwo . “No-one had ever broken the club policy of renewing for two years after the age of 30, and I renewed for two years. Luiz swapped Chelsea for Arsenal after Frank Lampard's arrival (Image credit: PA) “Then after two months, I went to Arsenal. It was down to the decision to bring Frank Lampard in as manager. In pre-season, I already could see the way he was going to play wasn’t going to leave me happy. “At that age, I thought “I want to enjoy the game in the way I play it”, so it was better to leave.” The best features, fun and footballing quizzes, straight to your inbox every week. For Luiz, this was a decision made as a matter of principle. “There are two kinds of workers in life,” he continues. “Those who work to protect themselves and the job, and those who want to do something different. In any company, 90 per cent protect the job, but I want to be part of the 10 per cent. “It would have been easy to have stayed quietly at Chelsea, but I’m not like that. So I sat down with Frank Lampard and said ‘I want to leave – the way you’re going to play won’t be good for me, and the way I’d play in your system won’t be good for you either’.” Luiz did not see himself fitting into Lampard's system A year after playing his final match for Chelsea against Arsenal in the Europa League final, there was another twist of fate for Luiz. “Life is so funny – later that season, the FA Cup final was between Arsenal and Chelsea. I leave, telling the manager I don’t think his philosophy would suit me, that maybe it wouldn’t work to win anything, then at the end of the season the final is against him. “So if I won, in theory I was right. If I lost, I wasn’t. Thank God, we managed to win, and I was very respectful in the way I behaved, not celebrating, and respecting the history I built at Chelsea.” TOPICS Joe Mewis For more than a decade, Joe Mewis has worked in football journalism as a reporter and editor. articles.title: Under-18s looking to "bounce back" after defeat to Ipswich
articles.excerpt: AFC Bournemouth under-18s Lead Coach, James Lowy, says his side will "bounce back" after a 6-2 defeat away at Ipswich Town. Goals from a trialist and Harley Simpson saw the Cherries go into half-time level at 2-2, before Ipswich secured the three points in the second-half. James Lowy spoke to afcb.co.uk: "It was a game of two halves. I thought we competed really well in the first-half and put ourselves in a good position. "We created a number of opportunities through pressing and regaining the ball high, but we didn't capitalise on those opportunities. "For us to compete at this level, they are chances that we would need to take. "In the second-half, we struggled to compete in our duels. In and around the final third we lacked some quality and could have done better with some chances too. "Ipswich defended well, and the difference was in both boxes today. "It's been a really tough period for us physically, with games coming thick and fast. "We have a young squad and some injures, so it is important for us now to rest and recover and put ourselves in the best position going into West Ham on Saturday." Lowy's players are back in action this Saturday (5th September).

articles.title: Post-Sunderland Press Conference
articles.excerpt: Álvaro Arbeloa knows improvements are needed if his Fulham side are to have a successful season in the Premier League. It was a relatively even contest on the whole in Sunderland on Sunday afternoon, but a greater cutting edge from the hosts saw them eke out a 1-0 win. “It wasn't our game, for sure,” our Head Coach admitted. “We were far from our level. We were talking during the half-time, that obviously you can have some bad days or even come here in a difficult stadium against a European team, and maybe you have a bad day with the ball, like it was in the first half, but you need to put more energy, better attitudes, better mentality. “So, we improved during the first 20-25 minutes of the second half, but then we concede a [shot off the] post, and four minutes later the goal. So yes, we need to improve in many things of our game, soon. “And the first thing is that we need to know what you have to do to win games – put more energy and, like I said, better mentality and attitude as a team. articles.title: Markham bags brace as Cherries beat Hashtag
articles.excerpt: AFC Bournemouth maintained their perfect start to their FA Women's National League campaign, with a 4-1 victory over Hashtag United. A Jenna Markham brace plus one apiece from Tamara Wilcock and Charlotte Harris secured the three points, in a game Helen Bleazard's team were on top for large periods and deserved the three points they walked away with. Wilcock was the first to test the Hashtag United goalkeeper. Cutting in from the left, her right-footed effort forced a strong save to tip it round the post. Elena Cole was close to a headline making long-range effort, but her shot was pushed over the bar. Nevertheless, it was a strong opening 15 minutes from Bleazard’s players. In the 17 th minute, Markham did what she does best and put the Cherries infront. Bella Hall broke free down the right and put a dangerous cross into the box. Former Cherry Kelci Bowers just about got her head to it, but only clearing the danger as far as Issy Bryant, the winger crossed onto the head of Markham, who beat Laura Hartley in the Hashtag goal. Georgi Kinkladze joined Manchester City in 1995 (Image credit: Getty Images) Facebook Pinterest Email Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google When Georgi Kinkladze arrived at Manchester City in the summer of 1995, the Georgian playmaker was one of Europe’s most promising young attacking talents. It didn’t take long for the former Dinamo Tbilisi midfielder to become a cult hero at Maine Road, with the signing coming just as the still-young Premier League was beginning to establish itself as a viable destination for some of the continent’s best players. This was proved evident in the fact that City were able to see off AC Milan , one of that era’s greatest sides, to Kinkladze’s signature. Kinkladze on snubbing AC Milan for City City saw of AC Milan to land Kinkladze (Image credit: Getty Images) “There was interest from Italy, but [City chairman] Francis Lee was very determined,” Kinzladze tells FourFourTwo as he looks back at his 1995 move to England. “He flew to see me and convinced me that City was a place where I could be the main man. I didn't know much about Manchester, but I liked the idea of a challenge in England.” Kinkladze quickly became a City fans' favourite (Image credit: Getty Images) It quickly became clear to the young Kinkladze that English football was very different to anything he had previously experienced. “When I arrived, the football was very different. It was much faster and more direct. The weather and the food were hard to get used to, but the fans made it easy. From the first day at Maine Road, they treated me like one of their own. That connection was instant.” The best features, fun and footballing quizzes, straight to your inbox every week. Alan Ball was the City manager at the time, having spent the previous season in charge at Southampton, famously building his team around Matt Le Tissier , instructing his side to ‘Just the ball to Le Tissier.’ So was that similar with Kinkladze at City? “Alan Ball was very important in my development as a player,” he continues. “He loved technical players and wanted the team to play with flair, even if we were struggling in the table. “The 90s were a different time and sometimes I was targeted by foul play. If you tried to dribble, someone would try to kick you. Vinnie Jones and the Wimbledon Crazy Gang were famous for it. Former England international Alan Ball was in charge of City at the time (Image credit: Alamy) “But I had played in the streets of Tbilisi so I knew how to jump over a tackle. I always thought that if they couldn't catch me, they couldn't hit me.” Those early Premier League days saw a number of big-name foreign players join the league, with Kinkaldze admitting that it was an exciting time to be involved. “It was the start of something new,” he adds. “Seeing Gianfranco Zola , Dennis Bergkamp and Juninho arrive in the Premier League was exciting and it felt like the league was opening up to creative players. “The long ball reputation of English football was changing.” TOPICS Joe Mewis For more than a decade, Joe Mewis has worked in football journalism as a reporter and editor. Mewis has had stints at Mirror Football and LeedsLive among others and worked at FourFourTwo throughout Euro 2024, reporting on the tournament. In addition to his journalist work, Mewis is also the author of four football history books that include times on Leeds United and the England national team. Now working as a digital marketing coordinator at Harrogate Town, too, Mewis counts some of his best career moments as being in the iconic Spygate press conference under Marcelo Bielsa and seeing his beloved Leeds lift the Championship trophy during lockdown. articles.excerpt: Matchday Live returns this afternoon, Sunday 30 August, as Town take on Manchester United at Old Trafford. The show will begin one hour ahead of kick-off, from 3.30pm, and is available to watch live and for free across the club’s X, YouTube and Facebook channels, as well as on TownTV . Host James Kirtland will be joined in the Portman Road studio by former Town forwards Macauley Bonne and Freddie Sears to bring supporters all the build-up ahead of the Premier League fixture. I arrived at White Hart Lane and someone stopped me in my car, opened my door and offered to park my car. I thought it was a wind up. It would have been at Wimbledon!” Towards the end of Sullivan’s time at Wimbledon, the club began the talks that would lead to their relocation to Milton Keynes , which caused huge amounts of fan unrest. The Premier League was changing, so things had to change and modernise. “But to move out of Wimbledon just didn't seem right. It just didn't seem right to take Wimbledon away from Wimbledon. George Graham had got us to the final but then Glenn Hoddle took over. Daniel Levy had just taken over the club, so there were a lot of changes going on at the time. “We’d go on to finish in the bottom half of the table so, while we had a talented side, it wasn’t a strong period. Read on for 20 barely believable stories from all four corners of the globe... Easter Island (A) When watching the cup draw, any team is keen to avoid a potential banana skin, so Santiago Wanderers probably weren't too thrilled when they pulled out a trip to the remote Juan Fernandez Islands in the 2024 Copa Chile. The fixture meant a journey to Robinson Crusoe Island, 400 miles off the Chilean coast and named after the famed Daniel Defoe novel, which tells the story of a shipwrecked English merchant stranded on a remote island for 28 years. There weren't enough commercial routes available for Santiago Wanderers to reach the island, so they had to call upon a Chilean navy supply ship, the Aquiles, to face unknown opposition. Juan Fernandez's team had been hastily assembled from recreational teams on the island, but were hampered by players missing training for lobster harvesting. They still made their professional opponents sweat though, only narrowly losing 2-1. Easter Island's Estadio de Hanga Roa before its 2014 redevelopment (Image credit: Joe Mewis) It was the second time a team from the country's remote islands had entered the Copa Chile. In 2009, a team from Rapa Nui, more commonly known as Easter Island, hosted Colo-Colo , who are widely regarded as the nation's most successful club. Colo-Colo returned home 4-0 winners, but the most memorable moment was Rapa Nui's pre-match Polynesian war dance, on a field flanked by two of the island's famous Moai statues. Too bad to take part When a club is kicked out of their league, you generally presume they've cheated to win, but for Sueca United it was the reverse – thrown out of the lower levels of Valencia's league system for being so bad they were accused of not trying. The best features, fun and footballing quizzes, straight to your inbox every week. The club were the brainchild of eccentric actor Pau Codina and offered a chance to those who may not have got a game elsewhere. As admirable as that was, it left Sueca outmatched week after week. Over 11 seasons, they lost more than 300 games in a row, letting in more than 4,000 goals. The average scoreline throughout the club's history was 24-0. Come September 2023, the Valencian Football Federation had lost patience and expelled Sueca United after just two games, including a 40-0molly-whopping. Enough! A derby on a ferry?! Football players stand at a football pitch on the lower deck of a ferry on its way from Hiiumaa to mainland, Estonia, on March 30, 2013 (Image credit: AFP via Getty Images) The Estonian islands of Saaremaa and Hiiumaa have always had a fierce but good-natured rivalry. When they decided to play a football match in 2013, neither side was willing to surrender their home advantage, so they came up with a novel approach to a neutral venue – the game was played aboard the M/S Muhumaa passenger ferry connecting the islands. A grass lawn was laid down on the boat's deck, but there was only room for five-a-side, which probably reduced the risk of any challenges going, erm, overboard if things heated up. Hiiumaa won 4-1 – a surprise, as Saaremaa is home to FC Kuressaare, who play in the Estonian top flight. Unusually, they train in Tallinn but host home games on their island, meaning home matches often require longer journeys than away trips. Have boots, will travel Sudanese side Al Hilal recently achieved an unprecedented feat – winning the league in three different countries, in the space of just two seasons. Displaced from their homeland by a brutal civil war, they and Sudanese rivals Al Merrikh joined Mauritania's Super D1 League for 2024-25. The two countries aren't exactly neighbours, situated around 3,000 miles apart, but Al Hilal duly finished top of the table, albeit only recognised as “honorary champions”, with locals FC Nouadhibou technically the title winners. The two Sudanese clubs then briefly returned to their own country, with Al Hilal winning the Elite League – a short-form event to determine which clubs would represent the nation in continental competitions. Both then joined the Rwanda Premier League for 2025-26, where Al Hilal comfortably completed an unlikely treble. Pick the ultimate 4-4-2 line-up from players in FourFourTwo's definitive Top 100 List Oxygen required There was endless talk about the effects of playing at altitude before England's World Cup win in Mexico City this year, but that was trivial compared to a visit to Peruvian side Union Minas. From the 1980s to the early 2000s, the Cerro de Pasco side reached the summit of Peruvian football with their squad of jobbing veterans and nearly men, aided by substantial home advantage. The Estadio Daniel Alcides Carrion is the highest stadium in the world at around 14,000 feet above sea level – that's about 2,126 Dan Burns, and less than 4,000 feet lower than the base camps on Mount Everest. Opposition teams were so overwhelmed by the altitude that they would frequently be incapacitated, with oxygen masks a common sight in the visiting dressing room at half-time. Union briefly led the top tier standings in the 1998 season, but the decline of the mining industry hit the area hard and they slid down the leagues before halting operations in 2011, only returning last year. Six titles and a funeral Some clubs evoke strong feelings of animosity from their rivals without it being entirely obvious why. For others, it's more apparent. Take Maltese club Valletta FC, for example. The Lilywhites are one of Malta’s most successful clubs – they’ve won 25 league titles and in 2000-01, they laughed in the face of Gerard Houllier’s Liverpool cup treble by winning an almost unheard of domestic sextuple, at once securing the Premier League, Rothmans Trophy, Super Five Cup, Lowenbrau Cup, Super Cup and the Centenary Cup. But it's the way Valletta celebrate their success that antagonises opponents – whenever they win the league, fans hold a mock funeral street parade for their beaten rivals, carrying coffins with the insignia of their rivals through the streets. It was no great surprise then that when Valletta suffered the first relegation of their history in 2023-24, a healthy dose of schadenfreude was expressed by other clubs. Free trip to Tahiti Beautiful Bora Bora (Image credit: Getty Images) Since 1961, the Coupe de France has allowed entrants from French territories around the world, creating some of the most epic away days in world football. The French Football Federation covers the costs, but amateur teams still have to brave getting time off from their day jobs for what could be a lengthy jaunt. In 2024-25, fourth-tier Normandy side US Avranches landed an away match with AS Dragon from Papeete in Tahiti – flying nearly 10,000 miles from rainy northern France to a tropical paradise island in the Pacific Ocean, only to lose on penalties after a 2-2 draw. The wrong club While players will always try to pretend that a transfer is motivated by a previous love for their new club, in reality there are often unspoken reasons behind switching teams. One of the strangest was the case of Congolese winger Thievy Bifouma's move to Iranian side Esteghlal Khuzestan in 2024. The former West Bromwich Albion loanee explained he put pen to paper because he wanted to face Cristiano Ronaldo in the Asian Champions League. “I reviewed the calendar and realised they had a game against Al Nassr – I said to myself this was where I wanted to go,” he told Iranian media. The slight issue was that Al Nassr had a date with Esteghlal FC, based in Tehran, not Esteghlal Khuzestan, a completely different team situated hundreds of miles to the south. “I had no idea there were two teams named Esteghlal,” Bifouma admitted. “When I arrived, my countryman Gael Kakuta called me and asked where I was.” Kakuta played for Esteghlal FC – the pair quickly realised that they wouldn't be team-mates after all. "We got out of jail today, lads" A Young male detention centre for under-20-year-olds known as "Fundaçao Casa" or Febem, established by the Sao Paulo city government to help young offenders back to society (Image credit: Getty Images) There are a fair few prison-based football teams around the world, but Welsh side HMP Prescoed are a rarity – their players aren't made up of guards or support staff, they're inmates at the Category D, or open, prison. The team competes in the Gwent Central League, where a cursory glance at the league table suggests they appear to have an excellent home record, but abysmal away form. The reality is that HMP Prescoed aren't allowed to travel to away matches, for obvious reasons – they play them on their own field but must forfeit every game 5-0 and take a three-point deduction. As a result, the best-case scenario for the season is to finish on zero points. Last season they ended on minus five, having bagged five wins and a draw from their 14 fixtures. Amercian nightmare When the small Caribbean island of Antigua was given a chance to enter a club in the United Soccer League, the third tier of US football, it seemed like a great opportunity. By the time of their ill-fated third campaign in 2013 though, Antigua Barracuda's dream had turned into a nightmare. The league was supposed to be ‘international', but three teams from Puerto Rico were removed during the 2011 season, and by 2013 Barracuda were forced into relocation to the US mainland just to participate at all. The cash-strapped team lived in a cramped hotel in Tampa, Florida, making journeys of up to 10 hours in a tiny minibus to fulfil fixtures. At one point they even had to train in their hotel's car park, as they didn't have access to a pitch. They lost 26 games out of 26. Okinawa's number two team Third-tier Japanese side FC Ryukyu come from the island of Okinawa, famed for its beaches, coral reefs and a well-known Second World War battle. articles.title: Sunderland’s Europa League schedule confirmed
articles.excerpt: Sunderland AFC will begin the 2026-27 UEFA Europa League league phase on home soil, with AZ Alkmaar the visitors to the Stadium of Light on Wednesday 16 September. The Black Cats will then make their first trip of the league phase on Thursday 15 October, travelling to Portugal to face SCU Torreense, before heading to Poland a week later to take on Lech Poznań. Régis Le Bris’ side will return to Wearside on Thursday 5 November, when GNK Dinamo will visit the Stadium of Light. The Lads will then welcome Jagiellonia Białystok to Sunderland on Thursday 26 November, before rounding off their European fixtures of 2026 with a trip to Italy to face AC Milan on Thursday 10 December. Sunderland will begin 2027 with an away trip to Belgium to face RSC Anderlecht, before completing the league phase at the Stadium of Light against PFC Levski Sofia on Thursday 28 January. articles.title: Scott: We had chances to go and win the game
articles.excerpt: Midfielder Alex Scott felt AFC Bournemouth “deserved to win the game” after they were pegged back late on in a 1-1 draw against Everton. Speaking post-match, Scott said: “I think we deserved to win the game. A mistake at the end and it’s cost us three points, which in this league, between three points and one, that’s the margin. “We had chances to go and win the game and we didn’t take them. articles.title: POTM MCATEE DISCUSSES POINT AGAINST LIVERPOOL
articles.excerpt: McAtee discusses Forest’s point against Liverpool Reds took the lead twice at Anfield Midfielder scooped POTM award from the game James McAtee says the Nottingham Forest players didn’t know how to feel after picking up a point against Liverpool. The Reds led twice at Anfield, but two equalisers meant it was a point for the Reds on an afternoon when it could easily have been all three. McAtee was named Player of the Match after an outstanding individual display, but the playmaker was full of praise for his teammates for sticking together and taking a point from the game. “We don’t really know how to feel. To come here and get a point is amazing, but the game was in our hands twice. “There’s a bit of disappointment because we could have got the points, but we’re also happy with the performance. We came here, we stuck together and we put a good point on the board. “It was a credit to the players for taking the lead again after they equalised. But when you come here anything can happen, so we can’t be too disappointed. “We stuck to the game plan, we tried to get in scoring positions, which we did. Alisson made an unbelievable save from Igor which would have seen us 2-0 up at the break.

articles.title: Coventry City 0-1 Hull City
articles.excerpt: Fixtures Coventry City Vs. Hull City - Sat, Aug 29 2026, 15:00 Hull City’s wonderful start to the new Premier League season continued as they beat Coventry City 1-0 at the CBS Arena to make it two wins from two on their top flight return. Backing up their opening day win against Manchester United with another solid display, the Tigers this time left it late to strike the decisive blow as substitute Liam Millar raced through on goal with eight minutes remaining to confidently slot the ball into the net and send a sold-out away end wild with delight. articles.excerpt: Good afternoon everyone, and welcome back to the Stadium of Light for our first home game of the season against Fulham. Last season, we created memories that will stay with us forever, and you stood with us every step of the way. We achieved something special, and now we have the opportunity to build on that with Premier League and European football ahead of us. We know what you expect from us. Ultimately, I want to win, but we know that doesn’t just start at the weekend – it starts on the training ground earlier that week. It’s a process and a project, and we can’t turn it off and on. articles.title: “Beating Fulham was one of the best nights of my career. I took my shirt off and threw myself onto the turf as if it were a swimming pool” Diego Forlan on his 2010 Europa League success

This journey has thrown up plenty of career highlights, but for the former Manchester United man, the 2010 Europa League final remains a particular standout. The forward was a key part of Atletico Madrid’s 2-1 extra-time success over Fulham in Hamburg that night, scoring both goals for his side, including a 116th-minute winner to end the Cottagers' fairytale run to their first European final. Forlan on firing Atletico to Europa League glory Forlan joined Atletico Madrid in 2007 (Image credit: Alamy) “That night in Hamburg was one of the best of my career,” Forlan tells FourFourTwo . “A dream final. Not so much because it was a brilliant match, but because of the script.” Fulham’s remarkable run to the final in just their second-ever European campaign had seen them first navigate a group containing Roma , CSKA Moscow and Basel, before Shakhtar Donetsk, Juventus , Wolfsburg and Hamburg were accounted for in the knockouts. Roy Hodgson had led Fulham to the Europa League final (Image credit: PA) “Fulham arrived as the underdog, but they made life very difficult for us,” Forlan continues. I scored after half an hour, Simon Davies equalised, and the final went to extra time.” With the clock continuing to run down, penalties loomed, only for Forlan to deliver when it mattered most, as he took full advantage of a chance that fell his way deep in the second half of extra time. The best features, fun and footballing quizzes, straight to your inbox every week. “When everything seemed to be heading for a penalty shootout, Sergio Aguero battled for a ball out wide and spotted me in the heart of the box,” he continues. “I managed to get the tip of my boot to it to give Atletico the title.” Forlan’s reaction to the goal was as instinctive as his finish. “I took my shirt off and threw myself onto the turf as if it were a swimming pool,” he recalls. Forlan scored 96 goals in five seasons with Atletico (Image credit: Getty Images) For Forlan, the significance of the goal stretched further than just adding another title to Atletico’s roll of honour. “That goal tasted like glory, because it also marked a turning point for a club that started to feel important again,” he believes. “Spain’s capital, a city used to seeing Real Madrid celebrating titles, was painted red and white, and thousands of fans gathered at Plaza de Neptuno in a huge display of pride.” TOPICS Joe Mewis For more than a decade, Joe Mewis has worked in football journalism as a reporter and editor. articles.title: Under-18s Defeated By Manchester United
articles.excerpt: Everton Under-18s were beaten 3-0 by Manchester United at Finch Farm on Saturday morning. James McEvoy had the ball in the net early on for the visitors but it was ruled out for offside, before United got one that did count midway through the first half, as the dangerous Edson DeJonge-Seiros crossed from the left and Jariyah Shah slammed into the back of the net. Everton grew into the contest and Harry Brookes saw an effort blocked, while Dafi Pemberton spun cleverly on the edge of the penalty area before pulling his shot wide of the target. The Blues' Rodney Aduda then saw his header well saved after being picked out by Harvey Billington. United had chances, too. Juame Camacho wasn’t far away with a snapshot and Nathaniel Junior-Brown failed to hit the target after catching the hosts' in possession. Early in the second period, Blues' goalkeeper Ted Wilcox safely gathered an attempt from DeJonge-Seiros and, at the other end, a John Dodds close-range volley was athletically turned away by United shot-stopper Charlie Hardy. The second United goal came on 56 minutes – James McEvoy heading home from a dangerous corner. Genuine opportunities were at a premium after that. Freddie Murdock

Matthias Jaissle was confirmed as Eddie Howe's replacement at Newcastle United this summer (Image credit: Newcastle United v Getty Images) Facebook Pinterest Email Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Less than two years ago, FourFourTwo sat inside the bowels of Al Ahli's inner city training ground in Jeddah, and whispers abounded. “If he loses this game, the manager might well be sacked,” one Saudi Pro League expert told us that evening, as we waited for Matthias Jaissle to arrive for his latest pre-match press conference. Al Ahli had won only three of their first eight games of the new league season, and sat eighth in the table before the Jeddah derby with title-challenging Al Ittihad – a fixture that would attract a raucous crowd of 52,546. Given that Jaissle's club were one of the Saudi Pro League's big four – all owned by the country's Public Investment Fund (PIF) – their results were below expectation. Back then, the main focus of our visit to Al Ahli had been the recent signing of Ivan Toney , rather than Jaissle, who was largely unknown to British audiences in October 2024. Our question was whether he could help his new frontman make England's next World Cup squad – Jaissle knew Thomas Tuchel, having played for him in the youth teams at VfB Stuttgart. “Let's see if Thomas calls me and asks how Ivan is doing,” the smartly dressed Jaissle told FFT . “Ivan has the potential, definitely – he must deliver here to be seen in the UK, and we're doing our best to bring him into the best shape.” Prior to this summer's World Cup, Tuchel did indeed call Jaissle to discuss Toney, revealing the “fantastic feedback” he received was enough to persuade him to pick the 30-year-old in his squad. By then, though, Jaissle could easily have been long gone as Al Ahli boss. He did lose that Jeddah derby against Al Ittihad, a tetchy game interrupted by a sandstorm that blew dust from the nearby desert into the stadium. He avoided the sack, but was reportedly on his way out two months later after a loss at Al Kholood, with Max Allegri said to be his long-term replacement. Pick the ultimate 4-4-2 line-up from players in FourFourTwo's definitive Top 100 List That was until ultras protested at the training ground, putting up a banner declaring “Enough failure, leave!” The message was aimed at the club's hierarchy, rather than the manager. Jaissle stayed, and became an Al Ahli legend within months. The best features, fun and footballing quizzes, straight to your inbox every week. Jaissle was a central defender during a playing career that saw him help Hoffenheim to the Bundesliga for the first time in 2008, when he'd just turned 20. He'd been expected to be alongside Mesut Ozil, Mats Hummels and Manuel Neuer as part of the Germany under-21 squad that thrashed England in the final of the Euros in 2009, but damaged his ACL shortly before the tournament and would never be the same player again. Further injuries forced him to retire in 2014, aged 25, before he got a job as a youth coach at RB Leipzig – his former Hoffenheim manager Ralf Rangnick had since become a key man in Red Bull's football project. Jaissle adopted a similarly high-pressing style, and has taken it with him ever since. After a stint as assistant at Danish club Brondby, he joined Red Bull Salzburg, led their feeder side FC Liefering to a joint-highest finish, then was handed the reins at the main club, replacing Jesse Marsch in 2021. Matthias Jaissle poses after leading FC Red Bull Salzburg to the Austrian championship in 2023 (Image credit: FC Red Bull Salzburg via Getty I) Working with young players such as Benjamin Sesko , Karim Adeyemi, Noah Okafor and Brenden Aaronson, he took Salzburg to a double in his first season, plus the Champions League's knockout stage for the only time in their history. They lost 7-1 at Bayern Munich in the last 16, while Jaissle was still only 33. A season later, they went 30 matches unbeaten on the way to yet another domestic triumph. It was Salzburg's 10th straight title, but they haven't won the league since Jaissle left that summer. The German joined Al Ahli just a month after they'd been one of four clubs to be taken over by the Saudi PIF – together with Al Ittihad, Al Hilal and Cristiano Ronaldo' s Al Nassr. Jaissle's new club had been Saudi Pro League champions in 2016 but relegated since, only returning to the top flight in the same summer as his arrival. They quickly signed Riyad Mahrez, Roberto Firmino, Edouard Mendy, Franck Kessie and ex-Newcastle winger Allan Saint-Maximin, finishing an encouraging third in Jaissle's first season – enough to qualify for the Asian Champions League. Ivan Tony scored 72 goals in two seasons under Jaissle (Image credit: Getty Images) Then came Toney's arrival, and that tricky start to 2024-25 when Jaissle so nearly lost his job. He knew the pressure he was under when we visited, but didn't let it show – remaining professional throughout, even taking time to greet visiting European media afterwards. It was hard not to warm to him. “Things take time – the club has a long-term vision,” Jaissle told us, subtly calling for patience as he attempted to turn around results, while nodding to his ability to improve young players. “I hope we can do better by implementing the philosophy from the top down to the academy, because at some point we'll need the young talents. In my eyes, that is the right approach. “A lot of signings were made before I arrived, so it's important as a coach that you're flexible enough to adapt to a new country, culture and player profiles. In the long run, it's important everyone is aligned, that you improve your squad and players in the way you want to play.” Jaissle replaced Eddie Howe at Newcastle United this summer (Image credit: Getty Images) Jaissle was afforded time to do that. Their progress to the knockout stage of the Asian Champions League had been a factor in him avoiding the sack – Al Ahli had a stronger second half of the league campaign, improving to fifth, then surprisingly became kings of Asia for the first time ever. The Champions League's final three rounds all take place in Jeddah, giving Al Ahli a home advantage that helped, but they still had to defeat reigning Saudi champions Al Hilal in the semis, before a final victory over Japanese side Kawasaki Frontale – conquerors of Ronaldo's Al Nassr. Last term, while finishing third in a three-way domestic race, they went all Brian Clough's Nottingham Forest and became continental champions again. Toney was key, scoring 72 goals in two seasons under Jaissle. When PIF-owned Newcastle were looking for a manager to replace Eddie Howe this summer, it shouldn't have been a surprise that they opted for the German. Howe will be a tough act to follow, having delivered the Magpies a first major honour in 56 years. Why have a manager who's won one historic trophy, though, when you can have a gaffer who's won two? He previously spent 10 years as a newspaper journalist, and completed the 92 in 2017. articles.body: How​‍​‌‍​‍‌ Football Data Is Revolutionizing the Way Online Football Games Are Played - Premier Fantasy Tools Last updated on August 29th, 2026 A football match has always revolved around numbers like goals, passes, possession, etc., which have long helped fans understand the game. In today’s age of information, the amount of available data has increased manyfold. Supporters can now easily get updates on players’ performance, tactical trends, and match developments via their mobile phones in no time. This unprecedented access to detailed and deep-dive information has also affected football fans’ online gaming interactions. Data has been integrated into the football game experience, which ranges from prediction contests and fantasy football matches to football-themed casino games and gambling games. Fans are now doing more than just watching matches; they are reading, interpreting, and using the information as part of their gameplay. Football Fans Are Getting More Analytical Football supporters now come into contact with the numbers used by scouts, coaches, and professional analysts. Concepts like expected goals, passing accuracy, shot locations, player heat maps, and possession maps are now common features of football reports and analysis. One can reasonably expect that, at least, a fan spending her time comparing Premier League players on a weekday lunch break would later switch from fantasy games to match predictions and perhaps even head over to a platform like mBit crypto casino while staying glued to the football highlights. Modern football entertainment is fundamentally a product of choice, information, and interaction. Instead of thinking of football as an event that takes place in ninety minutes on the pitch, fans today choose to craft a digital journey around match day. Fantasy Football Has Made Statistics More Interesting This change is most evident in fantasy football . These days, people are making decisions not only based on famous names but also on various pieces of information. Some of the typical statistics are: Goals and assists are a primary measure of goal-scoring and goal-setting abilities Minutes played are an important factor in finding trustworthy main contributors Shots and chance creation are a good measure of a forward’s or an attacker’s involvement in play Upcoming fixtures give an idea of which players will have the most favorable matches ahead of time Form over time shows how the player has progressed in the game Using data can make weekly team selection another interesting aspect of the game. Some fans spend even more time looking through player stats than watching the matches themselves. This has also created another field of football-related conversation. It is not uncommon for friends to get together and talk over stats, swap transfer ideas, and even share screenshots of their fantasy teams. In this way, data analysis becomes a social football activity. With Live Updates, Football Matches Are Getting More Exciting The biggest strength of today’s advanced football data is its almost real-time updates. During the match, football fans gain real-time or near-real-time access to possession stats, player ratings, the number of corners, etc. Such a situation gives the match-watching experience the ‘second screen effect’, one watching the match on the TV while simultaneously checking data on the phone or the tablet. Football is more than a sport for fans who see every match as a chance to play fantasy football or other football-related online games. They can also watch their favorite games while playing the football games they love, or even bet on sports online with great odds for real and virtual competitions. Data can often explain situations that would otherwise be hard to figure out just by watching the action. The team with very few possessions is the one that has created the most chances. For fans who love prediction games and other football-related online games , this extra information can keep them engaged at every step. Each replacement, shot, and tactical shift can add a new data point. Algorithms Are Giving a More Tailored Touch to Football Games Running behind numerous digital platforms is the power of algorithms that digest vast quantities of information. These programs are intelligent enough to learn which aspects (leagues, teams, players, games) each user demands most. As a result, the experience users have on such platforms becomes much more personalized. For example, a supporter of a certain club may receive the following kind of information: Games of their team or opponent team. Player stats about their favorite players. Match suggestions in fantasy football based on a player’s recent form. Access to football-themed games, only or primarily. To see the content related to competitions which they regularly watch. By reducing the time spent searching for information, a fan gains more free time and is more likely to find content that appeals to them firsthand. It’s no secret that Spurs need firepower up top, after Richarlison showed precisely why he’s not up to the task with a poor performance against Brentford in the opening game of the season, and Dominic Solanke’s injury record making him an unreliable option. Osimhen has long been regarded as one of the most talented strikers in the world, but has he ever truly lived up to that hype? Now is the time for him to prove it, and Tottenham is the perfect place to do that. How much would Victor Osimhen cost Spurs? articles.title: A statement from our Owner and Executive Chairman Doug King
articles.excerpt: Today we mark a special moment in the history of Coventry City FC, as we return to the Premier League. The agreement represents the first official cider partnership in the club's history and will see Thatchers products served throughout Vitality Stadium, further enhancing the matchday experience for supporters. Thatchers Gold will headline the cider offering across the stadium, complemented by Thatchers Zero to provide supporters with both alcoholic and alcohol-free options. Established at Myrtle Farm in Somerset in 1904, Thatchers remains an independent family business, with four generations having dedicated themselves to producing premium cider and a fifth generation preparing to continue that legacy. Its strong presence across the South West makes the partnership a natural fit, bringing together two organisations with deep regional roots. The agreement marks the club's first official beer partnership in 18 years and comes at a landmark moment, with supporters set to enjoy an enhanced matchday experience as the redevelopment of Vitality Stadium continues. As part of the partnership, Molson Coors will bring both Carling Original and Carling Premier – its premium nitro-smooth variant – to Vitality Stadium, alongside a range of the brewer’s leading beer brands including Coors, Madrí Excepcional, Alpacalypse and Madrí Excepcional 0.0%. The collaboration reflects Carling's long-standing commitment to British football, with the brand continuing its mission to bring supporters together through the game. Built around its "Beer of Mates" positioning, Carling has become synonymous with football occasions and shared matchday experiences, making it a natural fit for the Cherries as the club enters an exciting new chapter. articles.title: Young Blue Surprised By Goalscoring Hero Barry
articles.excerpt: A young Evertonian whose passion for the Blues was broadcast to the world has been to Finch Farm to meet his goalscoring hero. Lucas, 5, showed raw emotion when cameras caught him wildly celebrating Thierno Barry’s decisive second-half strike in the opening day 2-0 win over Crystal Palace at Hill Dickinson Stadium. The heartwarming footage was shared widely on social media, prompting Barry to issue a special invite to Lucas and his family to visit the Club's training ground. Dan, Lucas' father, said: “We can’t believe how it’s all escalated. At the match, I was inundated with texts from friends and family, and I thought it was just the lads commenting on the goal, but no; it was mum, dad, uncles, friends, friends of friends – and it carried on for the full week, with constant text messages and comments from as far away as Australia and America. “It was only when we got home from the game that we saw the pictures and it was amazing. “Everyone says that’s how it should be as a football fan, and the fact it was so raw. “The passion was just unbelievable. articles.title: Matchday shuttle bus back for Saturday’s home fixture against Hull City
articles.excerpt: Coventry City’s Matchday Shuttle Bus will be back from this Saturday’s opening home game of the Premier League season. The Shuttle Bus will run for each Coventry City home league match, and the cost to fans will continue to be subsidised by the Football Club as it helps its supporters travel to the Coventry Building Society Arena on matchdays. The return service will be priced just £5 each matchday, with fans able to buy their ticket as they board the Shuttle Bus pre-match. A member of staff will take contactless card payments (no cash payment) and issue a return shuttle bus ticket. Post-match, fans will just need to show driver their shuttle ticket for the return journey back into the city centre. Please note that a ‘one-way’ ticket is not available and buses will not be taking payments post-match. The service will collect fans ahead of matches from the Bus Interchange at Coventry Train Station (near Central Six, opposite Burger King) and then pick up fans at White Street Coach Park, before dropping them off at the Bus Station at Arena Park Shopping Centre, near to Foleshill Road/Nandos. FPL GW2 Differential Picks Yoanne Wissa – Newcastle United – 6.0 Forward – 3.0 % TSB Wissa looks sharp this season. After spending most of last season injured, he had a good World Cup and proper pre-season. He provided an Assist in Gameweek 1 and could have had more points as he got 2 Big Chances . Hop on early and enjoy Wissa’s points. He scored and grabbed 3 Bonus in Gameweek 1 to continue his brilliant form for Everton after scoring 8 Goals and 7 Assists last season . He will now face a Bournemouth team who looked shaky against an average Manchester City team in Gameweek 1. Bournemouth conceded the most xG (2.25) and the joint 2 most Big Chances (4). Under Marco Rose, Bournemouth look more open at the back. KDH is brilliant at picking up half spaces and loves playing against teams that allow him spaces in the final 3 . He usually gets attacking returns whenever he plays. Havertz and Arsenal now face Aston Villa, who conceded the 2nd most xG (3.77), 2nd most Shots (21), and joint most Big Chances (6) in Gameweek 1. They conceded most of their chances from the center of the park, and that is why Hinshelwood hauled. Havertz can exploit the same positional weakness against a struggling Villa side this Gameweek. articles.title: Hosts on the money in cup opener
articles.excerpt: AFC Bournemouth’s defence of the FA Women’s National League Cup started with defeat in their opening group game against Moneyfields at the John Jenkins Stadium on Thursday. The Cherries memorably lifted the cup after beating Southern Premier Division counterparts Plymouth Argyle in the final at QPR’s Matrade Loftus Road headquarters in March 2026. But the holders were beaten 3-1 by Division One South West leaders Moneyfields thanks to strikes from Tierney Scott and Sophie Phelps, coupled with an unfortunate own goal from Clarabella Hall. Tilly Westcott, Isla Betts and Mia Hammick were all named in the Cherries starting line-up, the trio all products of the club’s successful development programme. They had mixed fortunes with Westcott and Hammick both impressing, while Betts succumbed to an injury midway through the first half. Westcott capped an excellent individual display by netting the Cherries’ goal, the young midfielder finishing superbly from distance to make it 2-1 early in the second half. The tail end of last season was bumpier - a 2-1 defeat at Sunderland, a 2-1 win over Tottenham, a 1-0 FA Cup loss to Manchester City and a 1-1 draw at Liverpool. Across their last 10 matches in all competitions Chelsea have won 3, drawn 1 and lost 6. Brighton's start has been close to flawless: a 4-0 win over Aston Villa on 23 August, three days after a 0-0 draw at Tromsø in the Europa Conference League. They closed last season unevenly - a 3-0 win over Wolves, then defeats to Leeds (1-0) and Manchester United (3-0) - but their last 10 reads 5 wins, 2 draws and 3 defeats. The fouls column is just as consistent. Spending four years with the Parisian giants, the forward returned to England at the age of 11, joining Everton’s academy. Spending five years with the Toffees, Cho’s next move saw him sign a professional contract with French side Angers on 2 May 2020, becoming the youngest ever player to sign a professional deal in French football. articles.body: FPL GW2 Scout Picks Based on Stats, Analysis and Matchups Skip To Content Trending Now FPL GW3 Midfielders FPL GW3 Free Hit cons of gw3 wildcard pros of gw3 wildcard fpl gameweek 3 wildcard FPL GW2 Scout Picks Based on Stats, Analysis and Matchups FPL GW2 FPL GW2 Ultimate Guide and Tips FPL Scout Picks Game week Preview August 27, 2026 August 28, 2026 Dylan FPL GW2 Scout Picks Based on Stats, Analysis and Matchups Welcome to our FPL GW2 Scout Picks blog! Wow – what a start to the new season that was! Manchester United mauled, Spurs stung, City and Chelsea scraping wins, Liverpool and Newcastle playing out a thrilling draw and Brighton’s dismantling of Aston Villa – FPL Gameweek 1 had it all! Most of our teams should be well optimised for FPL GW2, but if you need any extra information or want some tips/punts going into this second round of fixtures, then our FPL GW2 Scout Picks will certainly be of use! Long-time readers will know that we like to keep a running total of how our AAFPL Scout Picks fare against the Official PL Scout’s team each week. Unfortunately, in FPL GW1 our squad got off to a not-so-great start, picking up just 53 points to the Official Scout Picks’ 55. So close! We go again in GW2… GW 1 AAFPL Team Official FPL Team As always, our Scout Picks will be based on the eye test, stats, analysis, and in this case also Pre-Season. Let’s first take a look at the fixtures for FPL GW2 Link to all our FPL GW2 blogs including scout picks, players to target, buy, hold, sell analysis, differentials, captaincy metrics, best forwards, and more. Completely free to access as well! FPL GW2 Fixtures FPL GW2 Scout Picks FPL GW2 Scout Picks – Goalkeeper Raya (6.0m) is our goalkeeper pick for this week as Arsenal travel to face Villa in FPL GW2. Arsenal reminded the league why they are reigning Premier League champions in FPL GW1with a confident display against Coventry. The Gunners came away 3-0 victors on the day, limiting the opposition to just 4 shots, 1 shot on target, and 0.2xG across the 90 . Coventry had just 3 touches in Arsenal’s box during that game and put up the lowest xG across the opening weekend of Premier League matches. Arteta’s side were comfortably the best defense in the league last season and showed us again why we should be targeting their defensive assets in FPL. Villa, Arsenal’s opponents in FPL GW2, were dismantled by Brighton in FPL GW1, conceding 4 and scoring 0. Most of Villa’s woes came from their defensive disaster class, but they were also light on first-team attackers due to injury and transfers. Emery’s team put up just 0.3xG in that game and took only 6 shots, 0 of which were on target …. Despite coming 4th, Villa put up only the 12th best xG, finishing 14 points better off than their xPTS suggests. Their average underlying numbers, lack of first team players and squad overhaul, plus their awful GW1 performance, make them a team to target in FPL GW2. Shaw offers high CS potential in a fixture against newly promoted Ipswich as well as some attacking and DC potential. Shaw’s season DC numbers were relatively low, but the number of clearances, blocks, interceptions and tackles that he was making did indeed jump post-Carrick appointment. This increase in Shaw’s CBIT/90 makes him a far more attractive option from an FPL perspective, especially at just 4.5m. Manchester United, of course, disappointed in FPL GW1 in their 2-0 loss to Hull. The underlying numbers suggest that United were not as bad as initially seems, however, and offer some hope to managers who have backed their assets in these first two fixtures (Hull and Ipswich). Hull scored two goals from set-piece situations in GW1 (something that United certainly need to work on), but if you take these two chances out of the equation then United actually defended quite well across the game… Hull created 1.01xG in that match but outside of their two goals they took only 6 shots (2 on target) and created just 0.28xG. I think this shows that United did generally defend quite well, but were too slow and disorganised at corners. Ipswich looked average against a very mediocre Sunderland team in GW1 and created little of note outside of their goal on the counter-attack and their last minute winner. Don’t sell your United assets yet, hold onto them for FPL GW2! Calafiori keeps his spot in the AAFPL Scout Picks team to complete the Arsenal defensive double up for FPL GW2. Coupled with Raya, Calafiori offers ample cover for Arsenal’s defence in FPL GW2 and more than makes up for our lack of a certain 8.0m defender… Gabriel’s yellow card in FPL GW1 showed why so many managers chose to avoid the expensive brazilian in FPL this season while Calafiori’s assist and CS proved a lot of those who have been preaching that a Mosquera/Raya + Calafiori double up was the better option. Unfortunately, due to Konsa’s transfer to Arsenal , Mosquera looks set to lose his spot in the team in the immediate future, leaving Calafiori as the only viable Arsenal defensive asset (though Ben white is an interesting differential!)… Gvardiol completes the defence in our FPL GW2 scout picks team. Thanks to Maresca’s pre-season comments, it was common knowledge that Gvardiol would be a ‘central pillar ‘ of this new-look Manchester City side, and the croatian rewarded his FPL backers with a huge 9 point haul against Bournemouth in GW1. With Palace and Coventry in the next two – two sides which failed to score in their respective GW1 fixtures – Gvardiol’s ownership will surely jump above the 15% mark in the coming days. Starting the game as a LB, Gvardiol needed just 1 shot to make his mark on the game, scoring with his first attempt in the 90th minute! His attacking potential is clear, and given the opportunity Gvardiol’s finishing is genuinely impressive for a so-called defender, but it is his security of minutes in the Manchester City defence which makes him such an attractive FPL option. At just 5.5m, Gvardiol offers an affordable way into a Manchester City defence with many moving pieces. Until we have more information on which other defenders are ‘nailed’ Gvardiol looks by far the best option in our opinion. O’Reilly could be a great differential punt for the next couple of fixtures but his minutes are no where near secure in the long term… Further Read: FPL Gameweek 2 Transfer Tips: Players to Buy, Monitor, Sell & Hold FPL GW2 Scout Picks – Midfielders We’ve selected a midfield four of Mbeumo (8.0m), Bruno Fernandes (12.0m), Ndiaye (6.0m) and Rice (7.5m) for our FPL GW2 Scout Picks team… Mbeumo and Bruno both looked far from their best in their FPL GW1 fixture against Hull. I think a lot of United’s problems stem from the overhaul in midfield . When the balls did get through Mbeumo, Rashford, Cunha and the other attacking players were able to get shots off and create half-chances for themselves but the issue appeared to me to be that the ball wasn’t getting to those players enough. Bruno was forced deeper to progress the ball as the two new midfielders failed to gel for large parts of the game. The signing of Baleba from Brighton will surely help the likes of Tielemens and Bruno, but a period of time to allow this new midfield to gel is also surely necessary. The forward largely had to create half chances and space for himself, but did produce fleeting moments of quality. The match against Ipswich in GW2 offers another opportunity for Mbeumo to impress. Similarly, Bruno (who struggled against Hull’s back 5 system) will find more space higher up the pitch against Ipswich’s 4-2-3-1. It would be wrong to doubt Bruno’s quality or his value as an FPL asset after just 1 mediocre performance – most managers would have wanted Bruno in their teams for both GW1 and GW2 to attack both games against promoted sides – it would be unwise to dump him after one match. Le Fee is the 3rd midfielder in this week’s scout team, although he blanked in GW1 we are backing him for GW2 as the Black Cats are at home to Fulham. Rice completes the Arsenal triple up for our FPL GW2 scout picks team. Like Szoboszlai, Rice offers a fairly cheap way into an elite side whilst also providing semi-regular goal involvements plus regular DC and bonus points . Rice averaged higher DC/90 (35% hit rate to Szobo’s 26%) than Szobo last season as well as bagging 23 bonus points to Szobo’s 21. Evidently, through an FPL lens they are very similar, and should be targeted based on fixtures and team/individual form. Arsenal’s fixture is far better for this week with the Gunners facing an out-of-form (and out of players!) Villa side which was battered 4-0 in GW1… The english midfielder blanked in FPL GW1 and will be low on the list of Arsenal assets to target for this fixture, considering the hype around Tzolis and the form of Havertz and Odegaard. However, due to Rice’s versatility of points scoring we think that he’s a better asset in FPL GW2. Furthermore, Hinshelwood scored twice in GW1 by crashing into the box from midfield and finishing chances won through pressing – one of Rice’s key roles/attributes is his box-crashing and I could see him playing a similar role in this game. Rice picked up just 3 points in FPL GW1, below last season’s average of 5.11 PPG, but he played well and we’re confident he’ll better that score in GW2. A couple of players caught the eye, including Giles who looks like a great, creative defender at just 4.0m , especially if Hull stick with a 5-back system, but it was ex-Sheffield United striker McBurnie who really impressed. McBurnie is the linchpin of the team – linking play, arriving late into the box and generally harassing opposition defenders. He looks like a very good FPL option at just 5.5m – especially with Coventry and Villa in the next two games… The striker did not score, but did pick up an assist in FPL in his first premier league game for Hull. articles.excerpt: In this FPL Gameweek 2 Transfer Tips blog, we take a look at players to Buy, Hold & Sell based on their Performance, stats, and fixtures. The post FPL Gameweek 2 Transfer Tips: Players to Buy, Monitor, Sell & Hold appeared first on ALLABOUTFPL: Your one stop place for all FPL tips, FPL captain picks, FPL news, FPL players, previews, reviews,differential picks, analysis and weekly updates. .

articles.body: FPL Gameweek 2 Transfer Tips: Players to Buy, Monitor, Sell & Hold Skip To Content Trending Now FPL GW3 Midfielders FPL GW3 Free Hit cons of gw3 wildcard pros of gw3 wildcard fpl gameweek 3 wildcard FPL Gameweek 2 Transfer Tips: Players to Buy, Monitor, Sell & Hold Buy, Hold, Sell FPL GW2 FPL GW2 Ultimate Guide and Tips FPL Tips Game week Preview August 26, 2026 August 27, 2026 aww.soum FPL Gameweek 2 Transfer Tips: Players to Buy, Monitor, Sell & Hold Except for Palmer, none of the Top 10 scorers from GW1 had an ownership above 10%. Even more importantly, of the 12 most premium FPL assets, only three — Saka, Palmer and Gabriel – returned in GW1, meaning nine of them blanked. That is not going to happen every week. So, don’t panic. Don’t pivot. Don’t rage-transfer. Trust the process. There were reasons you settled on your GW1 team after weeks of research, analysis and deliberation. One bad Gameweek doesn’t suddenly make all that work irrelevant. Trust your own judgement and, most importantly, don’t make transfers simply because you’re frustrated with your GW1 score. With that out of the way, let’s get into our BASH — BUY, AVOID, HOLD & SELL picks for GW2, sponsored by …. Well, nobody. We are poor, but you can help here if you want 😊 Link to all our FPL GW2 blogs including scout picks, players to target, buy, hold, sell analysis, differentials, captaincy metrics, best forwards, and more. Completely free to access as well! FPL GW2 Transfer Tips: Players to BUY Arsenal Avengers Ben White (£5.5m) – DEF, Arsenal – 6.1% TSB Christos Tzolis (£6.5m) – MID, Arsenal – 25.8% TSB Arsenal’s defence looked every bit as formidable as we expected in GW1, and White offers something particularly interesting on top of that defensive potential. He not only provides access to Arsenal’s clean-sheet potential but also posted the second-highest xGI among Arsenal players in GW1, behind only Saka. At just 6.1% ownership, you’re also getting a genuine differential with significant upside. If you’re looking for an Arsenal defender who can deliver at both ends of the pitch, White should be very high on your list. Tzolis is another Arsenal attacker who caught my eye in GW1, recording the third-highest xGI in the Arsenal squad, just behind White. And the timing is particularly appealing. Arsenal face an Aston Villa side that could be without several of their key players, with Rogers, Konsa and Tielemans leaving the club, Onana and Manzambi injured, and Watkins and Emi Martínez also doubts. That could create perfect conditions for Arsenal’s attackers to thrive, and Tzolis has already shown enough underlying threat to make him an intriguing GW2 option. PS: If you have the money, you can always upgrade Tzolis to Saka. We certainly wouldn’t complain about that move. Further Read: 2026/27 FPL Chip Strategy Guide – First Half of the Season Yoane Wissa (£6.0m) – FWD, Newcastle – 2.8% TSB Looking for a low-owned forward with genuinely strong underlying numbers? Wissa could be your guy. Among forwards, he ranks inside the Top 5 for shots, big chances, xG, xGI, NPxGI and assists — pretty much every attacking metric you could ask for. And then comes the fixture. Newcastle face Spurs, who currently rank in the Bottom 5 for xGC, expected clean sheets and goals conceded. At just 2.8% ownership, Wissa gives you the perfect combination of form, underlying numbers, fixture and differential potential. Don’t overthink this one. If you’re looking for a way to gain rank without joining the template, Wissa could be a very tasty GW2 punt. Yes, Chelsea looked excellent against Fulham. But we need to put that performance into context. Brighton are a completely different proposition. They were among the three best defences in the Premier League last season for both goals conceded and xGC, and they’ve picked up where they left off. In GW1, Brighton allowed their opponents zero shots on target. They also face Arsenal in GW3 at the Emirates which is another tricky fixture. So while Chelsea’s attackers remain excellent FPL assets, GW2 is not the week to chase their points simply because they delivered in GW1. GW4 offers a better entry point for Chelsea attackers when they face Hull City at Stamford Bridge. If you already own them, that’s a different story. But if you’re considering buying them, I would suggest you wait. Further Read: Fixtures and Players to Target for FPL GW2 (Position wise) FPL GW2 Transfer Tips: Players to SELL Morgan Gibbs-White (£8.0m) – MID, Nott’m Forest – 9.5% TSB This one is a little more straightforward. Gibbs-White has picked up a knee injury and will miss Forest’s League Cup game against Leeds. There is still hope that he recovers in time for the weekend, but at this stage, there is no guarantee he’ll be available. And even if he does make a quick recovery, the fixture run isn’t exactly screaming “hold”. Forest face Liverpool, Spurs and Aston Villa in their next three Premier League games. So you’re potentially looking at a player with an injury doubt, followed by a difficult run of fixtures. Fitness uncertainty + tough fixtures = sell. If you have a straightforward route to another good midfielder, this is one transfer we’d be comfortable making. Further Read: FPL GW2 Team Selection- Transfer Plans, Watchlist and Team Reveal FPL GW2 Transfer Tips: Players to HOLD Manchester Magicians Bruno Fernandes (£12.0m) – MID, Man Utd – 49.1% TSB Bryan Mbeumo (£8.0m) – MID, Man Utd – 36.5 TSB We know GW1 was disappointing. But if you bought Bruno and/or Mbeumo, there was a very clear reason behind it: Manchester United had two promoted sides in their opening two fixtures. One bad Gameweek shouldn’t suddenly make us forget that logic. More importantly, United now return home, and we expect them to respond after a below-par opening performance. There is a strong chance the lessons from GW1 have been learned, and a reaction could be coming. The underlying numbers are encouraging too. Despite United’s poor performance, Mbeumo still ranks inside the Top 5 midfielders for both xGI and NPxGI. And Bruno showed exactly why he won the POTY of last season. He was the only player in GW1 to complete at least 35 final-third passes — nobody else even reached 30. That’s not the profile of a player we want to sell after one blank. Hold. The fixtures, underlying numbers and expected role are still there. Give them another week before reaching for the transfer button.
