FPL Gameweek 1 Review After deliberating all week and being set on going with a Haaland draft until Thursday, I shifted to a non-Haaland draft and decided to be aggressive on the chips. Bench Boost chip was always active for GW1, and I distributed funds all across the 15 players to get the most out of it. It’s always subjective to extract the points derived out of just Bench Boosting when you have purposefully spread the funds, I would still look at it as a 12-pointer, as these are the players I would have benched if not for the BB chip. 67 points on a Bench Boost is not worth writing home about, but as it was a low-scoring Gameweek. As a result, I am 787k in the overall rankings right now. The aim is to stay inside the 1 million mark by Gameweek 10 and to finish the season inside the top 10k. Manchester United triple up and Bruno captaincy disappointed as they lost 2-0 away to Hull, when it was one of the top 3 fixtures to target. Nico O’Reilly could have had returns but ended up with a blank, Gross should have had a penalty, but the referee showed mercy to Aston Villa, resulting in a blank for Gross as well. I would call these instances unlucky, and the picks are definitely more than fine for the short or medium-term. The double up on Liverpool with Isak and Szoboszlai almost disappointed me, until a last-minute penalty was taken and converted by Szoboszlai. It looks like he is set to be on penalties for now. articles.excerpt: Fantasy Premier League is all about making good decisions before the next Gameweek. EPL results can help with that. They can show which teams are in good form, which players are getting chances and which fixtures could bring more FPL points. Of course, football fans also enjoy the matchday experience itself. For those who like […] The post How EPL Match Results Can Influence Your Fantasy Premier League Strategy appeared first on Premier Fantasy Tools .

articles.body: How EPL Match Results Can Influence Your Fantasy Premier League Strategy - Premier Fantasy Tools Last updated on August 26th, 2026 Fantasy Premier League is all about making good decisions before the next Gameweek. EPL results can help with that. They can show which teams are in good form, which players are getting chances and which fixtures could bring more FPL points. Of course, football fans also enjoy the matchday experience itself. For those who like to add some extra entertainment around the games, Spino can be another option alongside watching EPL matches and following your FPL team. Don’t Look Only at the Score A 3–0 win looks great, but the score doesn’t tell you everything. A team might win easily and create many chances. That can be a good sign for its attackers. But sometimes a team wins without creating much and simply takes its chances. The same works for defeats. A team can lose 1–0 but still create many good chances. Its attackers may still be worth keeping. So don’t make an FPL decision just because you saw the final score. Look at the Players Results can help you find players who are becoming more important for their teams. Look at how often a player shoots, creates chances and plays. Also check if he takes penalties, corners or free kicks. At the same time, a player who scored twice from two chances may not score again next week. Goals and assists are important, but they are not the only things to watch. Check the Next Fixtures Recent results can also help you think about upcoming games. A team may have won four matches in a row. That sounds great. But if those wins came against weaker teams, you should be careful before buying several of its players. The opposite is also true. A team may have lost a few games against strong opponents. If easier fixtures are coming next, its best players could become good FPL options. Fixtures can change the value of a player very quickly. Watch for Changes Team tactics can also affect your FPL decisions. Maybe a defender has started going forward more often. Maybe a midfielder now plays closer to the striker. Maybe a new player has changed how the team attacks. These small changes can lead to more goals, assists and clean sheets. This is why watching matches can be useful. Statistics tell you what happened. Watching the game can help you understand why it happened. Don’t Chase Every Goal One of the biggest FPL mistakes is reacting too quickly. A player scores two goals and everyone wants to buy him. Another player gets zero points and everyone wants to sell him. Don’t rush. Before making a transfer, look at the player’s next fixtures, playing time and role in the team. One good or bad match usually isn’t enough information. Sometimes keeping your current player is the better choice. Think About the Next Few Gameweeks The best FPL decisions usually come from looking at several things together. Check the latest EPL results. Look at player performances. Check upcoming fixtures. Then think about whether there is a real trend. Don’t just follow the last score you saw. A player who keeps getting chances is often more interesting than a player who simply scored last weekend. A team that creates chances every week can be more useful than one that had one big win. In the end, EPL results are useful tools for FPL managers. Just don’t let one match make all your decisions for you. Watch the games. Check the numbers. Look ahead. articles.title: Coventry City sign Ethan Pinnock from Brentford
articles.excerpt: Coventry City FC are delighted to announce the signing of Ethan Pinnock from Brentford on a permanent contract for an undisclosed fee. The defender arrives with a wealth of experience and has spent the last seven seasons with the Bees, five of those in the Premier League. He began his career in non-league with Dulwich Hamlet. He enjoyed a six-year spell with the south-east London outfit and won promotion to the Isthmian League Premier Division in 2013. His performances caught the eye of National League side Forest Green Rovers who signed him in 2016. Pinnock enjoyed a successful season in Gloucestershire as he helped Forest Green reach the EFL via the National League play-offs. His standout performances convinced then Championship side Barnsley to offer him a three-year contract. He played 67 times during a two-year stint at Oakwell before making the move to Brentford in 2019 and he went on to make 216 appearances for the Bees. Pinnock has also represented Jamaica 28 times and has played in the Copa America and Gold Cup for his country. The 33-year-old is now looking forward to his new challenge with the Sky Blues. The contract also includes an option for a further 12 months. The exciting 21-year-old winger followed up an impressive 2025/26 season with Town U21s in Premier League 2 by being part of Gary O’Neil’s pre-season plans. Tudor’s 18 goal contributions in 20 games for John McGreal’s U21s side saw him named the club’s Academy Player of the Year. He started Town’s pre-season fixtures against Wycombe Wanderers and Le Havre and accompanied the first team to the training camp in Germany, before making his senior debut against the Foxes. articles.excerpt: The opening weekend of the 2026/27 Premier League season has already given fantasy managers plenty to think about. For FPL managers, attention now turns quickly towards transfers and the … Continue reading FPL & FanTeam Gameweek 1 Review: Early Stars, Value Picks and Price-Rise Watch The post FPL & FanTeam Gameweek 1 Review: Early Stars, Value Picks and Price-Rise Watch appeared first on .
articles.source_type: Season reviews, highest scorers per club, long-running community analysis
articles.body: FPL & FanTeam Gameweek 1 Review: Early Stars, Value Picks and Price-Rise Watch - FPL & FanTeam Gameweek 1 Review: Early Stars, Value Picks and Price-Rise Watch - Skip to content The opening weekend of the 2026/27 Premier League season has already given fantasy managers plenty to think about. There were surprises, strong performances from several cheaper players and, perhaps most importantly at this early stage of the season, some potential bargains beginning to emerge. For FPL managers, attention now turns quickly towards transfers and the first price changes of the campaign. For FanTeam managers, where there is less reason to chase short-term price movements, Gameweek 1 instead gives us our first opportunity to assess which players are providing the best points per million. It is worth remembering that one Gameweek is a very small sample. Nevertheless, early-season information can be particularly valuable because player roles, new signings and unexpected starters are only just becoming apparent. The Premier League’s opening weekend also produced some major surprises, including newly promoted Hull beating Manchester United 2-0, Leeds winning 1-0 at Nottingham Forest and Brentford defeating Spurs 3-0. Manchester City needed late goals to overcome Bournemouth 2-1, while Liverpool drew 2-2 at Newcastle. FPL GW1: don’t ignore the price market The first few weeks of an FPL season are unusual because transfers aren’t only about points. Team value can matter too. Once millions of managers start moving towards the same emerging players, prices can begin changing quickly. Losing £0.1m on one player while a planned replacement gains £0.1m can effectively turn a straightforward transfer into one that is no longer affordable. The latest FPL price-change indicator on Tuesday 25 August has two players standing out as particularly likely risers: Player Club FPL Price Price-change progress Maxim De Cuyper Brighton £4.5m +120.0% Mamadou Sangaré Brentford £5.5m +103.7% Both are currently shown as “Very likely to rise”. FPL price changes take place overnight, so managers already intending to buy either player should pay particular attention before the next update. De Cuyper – the early defensive bandwagon Maxim De Cuyper is the clearest name on the current price-rise list. Brighton’s opening weekend has propelled the £4.5m defender into the spotlight and his transfer activity has already pushed him to +120% on the price-change indicator. That is exactly the profile that can create an early FPL bandwagon: inexpensive enough to fit easily into squads, a big opening score and potentially capable of producing returns at both ends of the pitch. There is also an interesting crossover with FanTeam. De Cuyper scored 15.3 FanTeam points in GW1. At a FanTeam price of £5.0m, that equates to an exceptional 3.1 points per million – joint highest in the entire game after GW1. The key question is whether he is simply GW1’s big scorer or a player who can offer sustainable value. FPL managers should avoid buying purely because a price is rising, but anyone who already wanted De Cuyper has an additional reason not to wait too long. A word of caution on Brighton Brighton’s emphatic 4-0 opening-day victory over Aston Villa is likely to attract plenty of FPL investment, with De Cuyper at the front of the queue after his huge GW1 return. However, managers should be wary of simply chasing last week’s points. Brighton travel to Chelsea in GW2, which is a considerably tougher test and reduces the immediate appeal of bringing in their defensive players purely for the next Gameweek. De Cuyper’s potential price rise adds some urgency for managers who already want him longer term, but the Chelsea fixture means there is also a perfectly reasonable case for waiting rather than jumping aboard the Brighton bandwagon after just one match. Sangaré – another possible overnight riser Brentford midfielder Mamadou Sangaré is the other player currently beyond the 100% threshold, sitting at +103.7%. Brentford’s 3-0 victory over Spurs was one of the outstanding results of GW1, and Sangaré was among their standout performers. Again, the FanTeam numbers back up the attraction. Sangaré produced 9.7 points and costs only £4.5m there, giving him a GW1 PPM of 2.2. There is an important distinction between the two games, however. His FPL price is £5.5m according to the current price-change table, whereas FanTeam managers can obtain him for £4.5m. That potentially makes Sangaré even more interesting as a FanTeam budget enabler. Other FPL players attracting transfers Several Arsenal players appear prominently on the price-change screen, although none is currently classified as very likely to change. Ødegaard is at +77.0%, while Calafiori is +87.0%. João Pedro is another player attracting buyers at +70.8%. At the opposite end are players being transferred out heavily. Martinelli (-94.9%), Gyökeres (-87.6%), Sarr (-78.8%), Dowman (-78.2%), Hincapié (-76.6%) and Amad (-68.8%) are among those showing substantial downward ownership movement. Those figures should not automatically trigger transfers. The danger after GW1 is chasing last week’s points while selling good players simply because they blanked or failed to start. This is especially relevant with premiums. Haaland, for example, blanked against Bournemouth, but Manchester City still won 2-1 and his long-term fantasy potential has obviously not disappeared because of one match. FanTeam GW1: points per million reveals some unlikely leaders FanTeam’s GW1 data gives us another way of analysing the opening weekend. Rather than simply sorting players by total points, FISO’s FanTeam player table can be sorted by Points Per Million (PPM). This measures the return a player has generated relative to his price. After GW1 the leading value players are: Rank Player Club Pos Price GW1 pts PPM Ajayi Hull DEF £4.0m 12.3 3.1 De Cuyper Brighton DEF £5.0m 15.3 3.1 Kayode Brentford DEF £4.5m 12.3 2.7 Mendy Hull DEF £4.5m 12.3 2.7 Lewis-Potter Brentford DEF £5.0m 12.3 2.5 Hinshelwood Brighton MID £6.0m 13.3 2.2 Sangaré Brentford MID £4.5m 9.7 2.2 Tzolakis Hull GKP £4.5m 8.8 2.0 Kelleher Brentford GKP £4.5m 8.3 1.8 Janelt Brentford MID £5.0m 8.3 1.7 The striking feature is the dominance of defenders. Five of the first six players are classified as defenders, with Hull, Brighton and Brentford accounting for all of them. That doesn’t necessarily mean we should rush to build a defence consisting entirely of GW1’s PPM leaders. Clean sheets are inherently volatile, and a defender’s PPM can change dramatically following one shutout or one goal. But it does reinforce an important fantasy principle: relatively inexpensive defenders from teams capable of keeping clean sheets can provide the budget savings needed to afford premium attacking players. Brentford emerge as an early FanTeam value source Brentford deserve particular attention. Kayode (£4.5m) returned 12.3 points, Lewis-Potter (£5.0m) also scored 12.3 and Kelleher (£4.5m) collected 8.3. Sangaré and Janelt then appear among the leading midfield values. That gives FanTeam managers several different routes into Brentford rather than simply chasing one standout player. For managers prepared to use a block-defence strategy, Kelleher combined with one or two Brentford defenders is particularly interesting. Their 3-0 victory over Spurs immediately rewarded anyone prepared to concentrate defensive investment rather than spreading it across several clubs. Hull provide the surprise bargains Very few fantasy managers would have expected Hull players to dominate an early-season value table. But their 2-0 victory over Manchester United has done exactly that. Ajayi sits joint top of the FanTeam PPM rankings after scoring 12.3 points from a £4.0m price. Mendy produced the same score for £4.5m, while £4.5m goalkeeper Tzolakis returned 8.8. The temptation is obvious. The caution is equally obvious. One excellent defensive result against Manchester United does not suddenly make Hull one of the Premier League’s strongest defensive sides. The promoted club’s players may nevertheless prove extremely useful if they continue to offer starting players at £4.0m–£4.5m. Brighton’s GW1 stars Brighton provide arguably the most interesting combination of high scores and potential longer-term assets. De Cuyper’s 15.3 was the highest FanTeam score among the leading PPM players, while midfielder Hinshelwood produced 13.3 points for £6.0m. Brighton’s strong start also produced several more players further down the FanTeam value rankings, including Verbruggen, Dunk, Boscagli and Vuskovic. De Cuyper is therefore one of the most intriguing players across both games after GW1 although the much tougher fixture at Chelsea in GW2 should be borne in mind. In FPL he is threatening an immediate rise from £4.5m. In FanTeam he has started with 15.3 points from a £5.0m price. Some established names still delivered The FanTeam PPM rankings aren’t entirely populated by cheap players. Cole Palmer looked in scintillating form and returned 10.7 points from his reasonable £8.5m FanTeam price. Chelsea won a lively 3-2 match at Fulham, with Palmer among the scorers alongside João Pedro and Morgan Rogers. Manchester City’s defenders also appear relatively high in the value rankings. Guéhi and Gvardiol both returned 8.3 FanTeam points at £6.0m thanks to their goals. Arsenal defenders White and Calafiori also feature prominently thanks to their assists, with White producing 9.3 points at £5.5m and Calafiori the same score at £6.0m. These players may not match the spectacular PPM of a £4.0m defender who scores 12 points, but established defenders from stronger clubs could prove more reliable over a much longer period. Don’t build a GW2 team entirely from GW1 points The first Gameweek always creates temptation. Someone scores 12 or 15 points and suddenly looks essential. Someone else blanks and managers immediately want rid of him. That is rarely the best way to play either FPL or FanTeam. What GW1 has given us is new information. We now know more about the EPL starting line-ups , formations, set-piece responsibilities, attacking roles and the competitiveness of newly promoted sides. The challenge is separating information that might be sustainable from what was simply a one-match event. In FPL there is the additional complication of team value. De Cuyper and Sangaré are the two players who require particular attention today because the current indicators suggest both could rise imminently. FanTeam managers can afford to concentrate more heavily on footballing considerations. The first PPM table suggests Brighton and Brentford could contain some genuinely useful value options, while Hull’s budget players are worth monitoring rather than automatically assuming their opening-week returns will continue. Above all, GW1 has reinforced the basic construction principle for fantasy squads: identify genuine value at the cheaper price points and use the savings to accommodate the premium players capable of producing the biggest scores and becoming strong captaincy options. One Gameweek isn’t enough to tell us who those season-long bargains will be – but it has given us the first set of clues. We use cookies to ensure that we give you the best experience on our website. articles.title: How to Bet the Carabao Cup Second Round: Rotation, Goals and Team News
articles.excerpt: Tonight's strongest Carabao Cup selection projects higher than anything in the English leagues next Saturday. The card is not the problem - the team sheets are. How to use the projections, which markets are rotation-proof, and the lineup check that decides it.
articles.source_type: Head-to-head player comparison, goalkeeper and position value analysis
articles.body: How to Bet the Carabao Cup Second Round How to Bet the Carabao Cup Second Round: Rotation, Goals and Team News The Carabao Cup second round gets written off as a lottery. On our projections it is not, or at least not for the reason people think. The strongest selection on tonight's seventeen-tie card is Watford at home to Peterborough, projected at 63.4% . The strongest selection anywhere in the four English leagues next Saturday is Wolves at home to Stoke, at 60.2% . The cup card is, if anything, marginally less even than a normal league weekend, because the round pairs teams from different divisions. So the fixtures are not the problem. The team sheets are. Everything below is about that gap. The rotation problem, and why the model cannot solve it Nobody knows who is rotating until the lineups drop. Some managers will field youngsters and a pure second string; others will want to protect league momentum and make one or two changes at most. Two clubs in identical league positions will treat this round completely differently, and neither will tell you in advance. Our projections are honest about their own blind spot here. They are built on league form , and tonight's set was generated on Friday. They do not know who is being rested. When the model says Ipswich are 61.7% to beat Leicester, it means Ipswich's league-standard side against Leicester's league-standard side. That is not a flaw to route around, it is the thing to plan for. It means every number on this page is a starting position , and the last hour before kick-off is where you finish the job. The team news routine Check about an hour before kick-off , when lineups are confirmed. Ours land on the fixture pages as they are announced. Look at the shape of the change, not the count. Six changes with the spine intact is a different proposition to four changes that remove the entire midfield. If you see a teenage midfield, leave it alone. A projection built on league form has nothing useful to say about a side with three academy players in it. Check both teams. A rotated favourite against a rotated underdog is closer to the original number than a rotated favourite against a full-strength one. Where the numbers still help Goals markets sidestep the question This is the most useful thing on the page. A goals market does not care which eleven turns up, and if both managers change things the defending usually suffers before the attacking does. The model's highest both-teams-to-score ties tonight: Tie BTTS 2+ goals Southampton v West Ham 62.4% 81.8% Cardiff v Norwich 61.8% 81.4% Plymouth v Coventry 58.9% 81.3% Watford v Peterborough 57.5% 83.5% Ipswich v Leicester 56.8% 82.3% Blackpool v Lincoln 56.3% 77.2% Walsall v Leyton Orient 55.7% 76.0% Birmingham v Brentford 54.5% 79.5% The ten highest-projected ties on the card all reach 76% or better for two or more goals. That is the shape of a round where nobody is quite settled. Clean sheets are the market to avoid The highest clean-sheet probability on the entire seventeen-tie card is 39.5% , for Wolves away at Sheffield Wednesday. After that it is Fleetwood at 38.9% and Middlesbrough at 38.5%. Not one team on the card is even a 40% chance to keep it out. Backing a clean sheet, a correct score or a to-nil in this round is asking for precision the evening will not give you. If you are backing a winner, back a mismatch Selection Win % Projected goals Watford v Peterborough 63.4% 2.21 Ipswich v Leicester 61.7% 2.12 Middlesbrough at Doncaster 61.1% 2.00 Brentford at Birmingham 58.8% 1.95 Barnsley v Crewe 55.9% 1.80 Wolves at Sheffield Wednesday 54.9% 1.70 Coventry at Plymouth 54.1% 1.91 Note how quickly it flattens. By the seventh name you are at 54%, and below that the card is a coin toss - Fleetwood 45.6%, Lincoln 45.1%, Millwall 44.5%. There is no value in reaching down that list for a favourite; if the model will not commit past the halfway mark, neither should you. How we are playing it Two trebles on today's Daily Acca , deliberately built as opposites. The first takes the three strongest projected winners - Middlesbrough, Watford and Ipswich - and accepts the rotation risk in exchange for a price. The second takes the three highest both-teams-to-score ties and avoids the question entirely: it does not matter who is rested if both ends of the pitch are leaky. Both are staked at a point, both are priced around 4.0, and both are published before team news, which is precisely why the routine above matters. Leave clean sheets and correct scores alone. Nothing on the card reaches 40%. Do not chase a favourite below about 55%. The list flattens into coin tosses fast. Check the lineups an hour before. articles.title: FPL Gameweek 2 Preview – Don’t Knee Jerk
articles.excerpt: FPL Gameweek 2 Preview – Don’t Knee Jerk As we head into Gameweek 2 of the Fantasy Premier League (FPL) season, there will be an incredible temptation to think your team is shit and just grab a player that did well last weekend – this is what FPL managers call a knee jerk. I – […] The post FPL Gameweek 2 Preview – Don’t Knee Jerk appeared first on Full90 FPL .
articles.source_type: Gameweek previews, transfer tips, captaincy corner, fixture focus
articles.body: FPL Gameweek 2 Preview - Don’t Knee Jerk - Full90 FPL Skip to content FPL Gameweek 2 Preview - Don’t Knee Jerk As we head into Gameweek 2 of the Fantasy Premier League (FPL) season, there will be an incredible temptation to think your team is shit and just grab a player that did well last weekend – this is what FPL managers call a knee jerk. I – James – feel that temptation too. My team was a sea of 1s and 2s last week and I finished with 46 points on a bench boost. Triple united blank, captain Haaland blank, no Arsenal and my boy Dango off after 66 mins. And of course, the one highly-owned guy I backed against in Joao Pedro delivered just to add insult to injury last night. But, I came into this season with a plan for the first few weeks and, as much as I feel a fool for having Virgil over Calafiori (which was something I was genuinely debating), I am sticking to my plan. As I said in my gameweek 1 review , it’s important not to overreact. Just remember, Reijnders looked like the next De Bruyne after gw1 last season… Of course, like most rules, there are exceptions. And the exception here is if you have injured players – but wait for news from the press conferences – or players that didn’t play. I don’t mind making a move for those guys. If you are bench boosting you basically HAVE to fix that. But, if you aren’t bench boosting, do consider that you have a bench which you can use. Friday Deadline Warning Gameweek 2 kicks off on Friday night with Palace at home to Man City at 8pm UK time. So, the game closes at 18:30 that night. DefCon Corner In case you missed it, my thesis is that defcon points were super easy to come by last year and I don’t think they will be the same this year. For what it’s worth, Joe disagrees and nobody else seems to be talking about this… Gameweek 1 last year, 14 defenders and 9 midfielders got defcon points. This gameweek 1 (with one game left to play) it was Fulham 2-3 Chelsea xG: 1.34-1.70 You wanted it and Joao Pedro delivered an attacking return in the first minute. It was outrageously bad defending but he took the chance well. Rogers and Palmer also got on the score sheet with the new front three looking very impressive, even if the Fulham defending was somewhat questionable. Really, Chelsea need to look at Sanchez who was shockingly poor. He was at fault for at both goals. The first he just let through and the second he parried to Garcia. So, I still think their defence is probably best avoided. Palestra wasn’t even in the squad by the way. Josh King (not that one) was the one bright light for Fulham. He looked very dangerous in the first half. However, their defending was pretty piss poor – I’d be worried about that. Brighton Europe & Carabao Cup Midweek Brighton play against Tromsoe again on Thursday. Just be aware of this in case you own some of their assets. In the Carabao Cup we have: Tues 25th August Ipswich v.s. Leicester Plymouth v.s. Coventry Stoke v.s. Hull Birmingham v.s. Brentford Forest v.s Leeds (again) Weds 26th August Newcastle v.s. West Brom Spurs v.s. Charlton Preston v.s. Everton Thurs 27th August Chelsea v,s. Luton Fulham v.s Wimbledon Transfer News Man City signed Bouaddi for £85mn. He’s very young but could be a starting midfielder in a few weeks time. Let’s just wait and see. It seems like Spurs have wrapped up a £150mn double move for Marmoush and Savinho. Best FPL Fixtures From Gameweek 2 In case you haven’t seen it yet, check out our awesome new fixture ticker that Joe has created. This year we have made it interactive – you can change how far in the future you want to look and look at absolute best fixtures or relative overall or for attack or defence. For these previews, I am more inclined to use the absolute ticker because it shows the weaker teams better and that’s generally where we tend to use transfers – our premium players tend to stay a bit longer. Best Attacking Fixtures From FPL Gameweek 2 Newcastle top the ticker then. I’d be making moves for Wissa and Barnes in draft FPL because we have long-term evidence that they score goals and they played good minutes. I am less inclined to do that for Elanga because he is more of an assist merchant and Osula didn’t get near to 90 mins which worries me. In regular FPL, I want to see another week of football ideally but Spurs were so bad I can see why you would be inclined to go there. Everton are next but I think you should only really be thinking about Ndiaye . His main benefit is pens because his underlying open play numbers tend to be poor. I know Dewsbury-Hall scored at the weekend but I just don’t think he is that good – he HUGELY overperformed last season. Sadly, I don’t like Barry because I don’t trust him to play 90 regularly. At Hull, I am only looking at McBurnie and Slater . McBurnie is nailed to play 90 and cheap – that’s really rare for forwards. Slater is a super cheap midfielder that is on set pieces which makes him a great enabler but I don’t want to play him every week. At Liverpool, I am still concerned that Gakpo will leave the club so I wouldn’t go there until the window closes. I need to see Wirtz play 90 this week to keep him in mind going forward. However, I still like Isak if you have the money up top. Despite the shocking performance, I would keep any Man United attackers you have. Mbeumo and Bruno Fernandes are still my favourite two there and I still think they are good for returns against Ipswich. Best Defensive Fixtures From FPL Gameweek 2 Newcastle top the ticker again here. I think the best picks are Thiaw and Botman because they are good for defcons. Hall has more upside but also is always an injury risk. I wouldn’t go anywhere near Palace this week because of the City fixture. And, I wouldn’t go anywhere near Villa because they were all over the place last weekend. And, I don’t think I would pay for the Liverpool defence. I have Virgil because of these fixtures but I am not feeling confident because of how weak they looked defending the counter. He’s the only real pick here because he has defcon and attacking potential. Jacquet and Araujo are not nailed. Kerkez and Frimpong are just too expensive for what you get. I would avoid Coventry. I am happy to play them in bench boost 2 still but they were so poor against Arsenal that I do not trust them. Now open for 2026/27 Every premium tool, £25 for the season. £25 season pass or £5 a month Join Full 90 FPL 14 day refund, no questions asked. The season pass does not auto-renew. Rotation Planner The cheap pairs whose fixtures cover each other Transfer Planner Whose fixtures are about to turn, and who replaces them Captaincy Picker and Matrix The armband this week, and the one coming in three Top 150 Draft Rankings £5 on its own. Included here, plus the mid-season refresh The Midweek Fixture No ads Across the whole site and every tool, while you are a member Still free for everyone: the fixture ticker FPL Gameweek 2 Transfer Tips In this section, I pretend that you are asking me ‘should I buy/sell this player?’ and offer my advice, normally on players I haven’t covered above in fixtures. Of course, I already told you in the intro to try not to make moves, so I am assuming you are forced into these. And, you should always wait as late as possible for injury news etc. Should I Buy? Calafiori – Yes. He is attacking and plays for the best defence in the league. Yes, I am concerned about Hincapie taking some of his minutes but until that happens I am happy to go there. De Cuyper – No. I don’t think he will hold down this attacking spot and he plays away to Chelsea this week. Sangare – Yes. Both Joe and I are usually very down on new players to the league because they often struggle more than people expect but this guy did exactly what people were anticipating – def cons and a bit of attacking threat for 5.5 is great. Odegaard – Yes. I love Odegaard so that biases my opinion on him. But if he stays as this focal part of the Arsenal attack he will clean up on bonus points whenever he gets a return. Kayode – No. It’s just too short-term a move. He has two great fixtures followed by three bad ones (assuming Villa have sorted themselves out by gameweek 6). Tzolis – Yes. I am a little nervous that he starts to be rotated relatively soon because that’s how Arteta manages his team. And, I am a little nervous that Arsenal won’t be as attacking as you expect a top team to be. But, for 6.5, this guy looked electric in his first PL performance. Havertz – No. I don’t trust that he is nailed yet. Szoboszlai – Yes. Confirmed he is on pens (or at the least has pen share) and has all the routes to points. Gvardiol – Maybe. If he plays as attacking as he did last game every week then he is great. But I am still worried that he will be rotated. Cherki – No. He SHOULD start for City. But that doesn’t mean he will. Joao Pedro – No. If you swerved him week 1 like me, then you did it for a reason. Wait until after he plays Arsenal. Guehi – No. I don’t know if he is nailed and they just spent £85mn on a DM so we don’t know if he keeps his spot there or goes back into the backline. White – Yes, until Timber is back he is nailed. Prefer Calafiori though. Hinshelwood – No. Wait until after they play Chelsea. Saka – No. Not until he plays 90 do I trust his fitness. Should I Sell? Konsa – No. Unless you’re forced to do this to make moves elsewhere because you have 4 Arsenal or you need to play your bench boost, try and hold him on your bench. In two weeks he might be a nailed on starting centre-back for the best team in the league at 4.5. Gyokeres – Yes. He is not nailed. Van de Ven – Yes. As much as I think they probably need him back instead of one of Senesi or van Hecke, he is injured. Sarr – Yes. It looks like he is on his way out of the club. Mbeumo/Fernandes/Shaw – No. Not when he is about to play a promoted team at home. Watkins – Yes. Looks like he is going to be sold. Rice – No. I don’t trust that he is fit so I wouldn’t buy him, but you already have him so probably worth keeping him. Anderson – Yes if he is injured but wait for news. Calvert-Lewin – No. If you are selling the only nailed on 6.0 forward after one blank then you really need to re-assess how you are playing this game. Gabriel – No. He has a good fixture and you will need to take a hit at this point if you are making a move to try to release money. Munoz – Maybe. I wouldn’t have started the season with him because of the transfer speculation but now you have him you may as well keep him for another couple of weeks. Gibbs-White – No. Playing away to Liverpool this week is not ideal but we have already seen they can be got on the counter. Semenyo – No. I am concerned about how wide he played and his lack of attacking output but he is fine to hold for another week. Le Fee – No. Run him out against Fulham for one more week and then re-assess. Best Captains for FPL Gameweek 2 Here, we assess who the best captain options are for FPL Gameweek 2. My opinion hasn’t really changed and I still think Fernandes is the best captain option at home to Ipswich. Haaland is always an option too. If you want something more spicy (which generally we advise against) then I like Mbeumo at home to Ipswich or Isak at home to Forest or one of the Arsenal lads, purely based on how bad Villa looked last week. That’s It. We’ve covered the best fixtures, transfer tips and captains for FPL gameweek 2. If you are looking for a full readout of gameweek 1 then check out the review piece here If you are mad and have just scrolled down here for the conclusion then it is this: don’t make transfers unless you have to. articles.title: xG Report: The Weekend's Biggest Chance Creators in All Four English Divisions
articles.excerpt: Brentford created the most in England. West Ham created 3.23 expected goals at home and lost to a Charlton side who managed 0.70. The top five chance creators in every English division, plus the early Championship, League One and League Two xG tables.
articles.source_type: Head-to-head player comparison, goalkeeper and position value analysis
articles.body: Weekend xG Report: Championship, League One, League Two xG Report: The Weekend's Biggest Chance Creators in All Four English Divisions Brentford created the most in England this weekend: 3.87 expected goals against Tottenham, from a home side that scored three and could have had more. That is the headline number. The more interesting one is 3.23, which is what West Ham generated at home to Charlton in the Championship. They lost 2-1. Charlton had 0.70 xG and took all three points. That is the weekend in one fixture, and the reason this column exists. Below are the top five chance creators in each of the four English divisions, the biggest gaps between what teams deserved and what they got, and the early xG tables for the Championship, League One and League Two. The top five xG teams in every English division All figures are total expected goals from the weekend's fixtures, with the opponent's xG alongside for context. Premier League Team Scored Match Brentford 3.87 Brentford 3-0 Tottenham (0.59) Liverpool 3.64 Newcastle 2-2 Liverpool (1.27) Brighton 3.19 Brighton 4-0 Aston Villa (0.33) Manchester United 2.19 Hull City 2-0 Man Utd (0.99) Manchester City 2.13 Man City 2-1 Bournemouth (0.57) Liverpool drawing 2-2 at Newcastle having created 3.64 to their hosts' 1.27 is the sort of result that looks like a title-race wobble and reads, in the numbers, like an away performance that deserved more. United's 2.19 without a goal at Hull is the opposite problem, and one we flagged in our Gameweek 1 review Championship Team Scored Match West Ham United 3.23 West Ham 1-2 Charlton (0.70) Millwall 2.93 Millwall 3-0 Norwich (0.96) Cardiff City 2.81 Derby 2-2 Cardiff (1.88) Lincoln City 2.44 Lincoln 1-3 Portsmouth (1.39) Southampton 2.43 Southampton 3-1 Stoke (1.13) Three of those five failed to win. Lincoln lost 3-1 at home having created a full expected goal more than Portsmouth, and just outside the five, QPR drew 0-0 with Bolton having generated 2.09 xG to Bolton's 0.16 - the most lopsided chance count of the weekend anywhere in England. League One Team Scored Match Stockport County 3.01 Stockport 1-2 Blackpool (1.85) Wycombe Wanderers 2.26 Wycombe 1-1 Plymouth (0.93) Luton Town 2.19 Luton 2-2 Notts County (0.55) Huddersfield Town 2.06 MK Dons 1-1 Huddersfield (1.38) Blackpool 1.85 Stockport 1-2 Blackpool (3.01) Stockport against Blackpool was the weekend's clearest case of a game not going the way the chances did. Stockport created more than 3.0 xG at home, Blackpool created 1.85, and Blackpool won. Luton, meanwhile, drew a game in which they had four times their opponents' expected goals. League Two Team Scored Match Bristol Rovers 3.42 Bristol Rovers 5-3 Newport (0.64) Colchester United 2.48 Colchester 2-1 Oldham (0.42) York City 2.19 Rotherham 1-1 York (0.83) Exeter City 2.15 Exeter 2-0 Accrington (0.85) Crawley Town 2.10 Rochdale 1-2 Crawley (0.88) Bristol Rovers had the highest xG in the EFL and the highest score in the country, and the match still produced one of the strangest lines of the weekend: Newport scored three goals from 0.64 expected . Eight goals from a combined 4.06 xG is not a normal afternoon. The biggest gaps between chances and goals Two lists, both from this weekend, across all four divisions. Scored far more than they created Team Goals Match Newport County 0.64 Bristol Rovers 5-3 Newport Barnet 1.38 Shrewsbury 1-3 Barnet Portsmouth 1.39 Lincoln 1-3 Portsmouth Notts County 0.55 Luton 2-2 Notts County Charlton Athletic 0.70 West Ham 1-2 Charlton Created far more than they scored Team Goals Match West Ham United 3.23 West Ham 1-2 Charlton Manchester United 2.19 Hull City 2-0 Man Utd Queens Park Rangers 2.09 QPR 0-0 Bolton Walsall 2.03 Walsall 0-0 Grimsby Stockport County 3.01 Stockport 1-2 Blackpool None of this means the results were wrong. Finishing is a skill, goalkeepers have good days, and a 0.64 xG afternoon that yields three goals is a real three goals. What the gap tells you is how repeatable the performance was - and over a season, teams in the second list usually start scoring more. The early EFL xG tables Two games in. Nothing above is a prediction. xG measures chance quality, not merit. A side that scores three from 0.64 has not got lucky in any moral sense. They have finished well, or been finished against badly. articles.title: Super Sub Report: What Every Premier League Substitution Produced in Gameweek 1
articles.excerpt: Under Super Sub a player prop continues on the replacement, so the number that counts is the pair's combined total. Here is what all 90 Gameweek 1 substitutions produced - fouls, shots, on target and tackles, player by player.
articles.source_type: Head-to-head player comparison, goalkeeper and position value analysis
articles.body: Super Sub Report: Gameweek 1 Substitution Stats Super Sub Report: What Every Premier League Substitution Produced in Gameweek 1 Martin Ødegaard came off on 76 minutes against Coventry having had three shots, one of them on target, and made three tackles. Mikel Merino replaced him and had two more shots, one on target, in fourteen minutes. Between them: five shots, two on target, three tackles That pairing matters because of how Super Sub works. bet365 call it Sub On Play On, Sky Bet and Paddy Power call it Super Sub, Betfair call it Safe Sub, and on the markets it covers the principle is the same - when the player is substituted, his replacement's tally continues the line. So the figure that counts is the pair's combined total, not the starter's own. We have a full explainer on the rule and which books offer it This is the first edition of a weekly column. Every Premier League round, we take every substitution and publish what the two players produced between them. Gameweek 1 is now complete: ten matches, 90 substitutions Gameweek 1: the pairs Each cell shows what the player who came off produced, plus what his replacement produced, and the player total for the pair. These are twelve of the round's most productive pairings. Match Came off Came on Fouls Shots On target Tackles Arsenal 3-0 Coventry Martin Ødegaard (76') Mikel Merino (14m) 0 + 1 = 3 + 2 = 1 + 1 = 3 + 0 = Brentford 3-0 Tottenham Mathias Jensen (67') Yegor Yarmolyuk (23m) 3 + 1 = 2 + 1 = 1 + 0 = 2 + 2 = Brighton 4-0 Aston Villa Jack Hinshelwood (64') C. Kostoulas (26m) 0 + 0 = 3 + 2 = 2 + 0 = 2 + 1 = Everton 2-0 Crystal Palace JP. Mateta (63') J. Strand Larsen (27m) 2 + 2 = 2 + 1 = 0 + 1 = 2 + 0 = Ipswich 2-1 Sunderland Julio Enciso (71') Jack Clarke (19m) 1 + 0 = 3 + 2 = 0 + 1 = 1 + 1 = Ipswich 2-1 Sunderland Issahaku Fatawu (66') Kasey McAteer (24m) 1 + 1 = 0 + 0 = 0 + 0 = 4 + 1 = Newcastle 2-2 Liverpool Florian Wirtz (63') A. Mac Allister (27m) 0 + 0 = 3 + 0 = 1 + 0 = 1 + 2 = Brentford 3-0 Tottenham Dango Ouattara (67') Jaidon Anthony (23m) 3 + 1 = 2 + 1 = 0 + 0 = 0 + 2 = Brighton 4-0 Aston Villa Yasin Ayari (64') Costinha (26m) 2 + 0 = 2 + 2 = 0 + 1 = 0 + 1 = Nott'm Forest 0-1 Leeds Harry Wilson (66') Noah Okafor (24m) 1 + 1 = 0 + 0 = 0 + 0 = 2 + 2 = Fulham 2-3 Chelsea Oscar Bobb (67') Shea Charles (23m) 1 + 0 = 0 + 0 = 0 + 0 = 3 + 2 = Fulham 2-3 Chelsea Cole Palmer (83') Estêvão (7m) 0 + 0 = 5 + 0 = 2 + 0 = 2 + 0 = The Fatawu and Wilson rows are the ones to sit with. Neither pair troubled the goalkeeper at all, and both produced a healthy tackle count - a reminder that the volume in these markets is defensive far more often than it is attacking. The last row is the counter-example, and it is just as important. Cole Palmer had five shots and two on target before being taken off on 83 minutes at Craven Cottage. Estêvão came on for the closing seven minutes and added nothing to any of the four columns. A replacement is only worth what his minutes allow, and seven of them are worth very little. How often the pair got somewhere the starter did not A second way of reading the same 90 substitutions. For each standard line, how many times did the player who came off finish below it, and how many times did the pair's combined total reach it anyway? Line Starter finished below it Pair total reached it 2+ tackles 3+ tackles 2+ fouls 1+ foul 3+ shots 1+ shot 1+ shot on target 1+ tackle 2+ shots 2+ shots on target That is 100 times across the round, at the time of writing, that a pair's combined figure landed on the right side of a standard line when the starter's own did not. Read the narrow version and it sharpens. Take only the players who came off exactly one short: on 2+ tackles that happened 37 times and the replacement supplied the missing tackle in 14 of them, and on 3+ shots it happened 18 times and the replacement supplied the shot in 8. The market that behaves differently is shots on target. Fifty-nine players came off without one; nine had a replacement who managed one. And on the harder 2+ line, 83 starters finished below it and the replacement got the pair there just twice. It is simply a rarer event to ask of somebody with 25 minutes, which is worth knowing before you decide the rule is worth more than it is. The busiest cameos Substitutes who put up numbers without any help from the man they replaced: Joe Willock (34 mins, Newcastle) - a shot, one on target, two tackles and two fouls. The most complete cameo of the round. Yéremy Pino (35 mins, Crystal Palace) - two shots, two tackles, a foul. Evann Guessand (27 mins, Crystal Palace) - a shot on target, a tackle, two fouls. Anan Khalaili (35 mins, Crystal Palace) - four tackles , more than most starters managed. Mikel Merino (14 mins, Arsenal) - two shots, one on target, in a quarter of an hour. Crystal Palace appear three times. Two down at Goodison, they changed things early and their substitutes chased the game - which is the game-state effect in miniature, and a reminder that what a replacement does is shaped by the scoreline he walks into. What to watch in Gameweek 2 Volume markets carry the effect. Tackles and fouls account for 64 of the 100 threshold crossings above. Shots on target account for eleven. Time on the pitch is the lever. The replacements who put up numbers here mostly had 20 minutes or more. A change on 85 minutes rarely moves anything. The bench decides it. A holding midfielder replaced by another holding midfielder keeps a tackle count ticking. Replaced by a striker because the team is chasing, it stops - and the shot count starts instead. It can go the other way. If the player is his side's best tackler, nobody replacing him matches that rate, and the pair's total grows more slowly than his own would have. The explainer works through that case. Our player projections and the Bet Builder tool model a player's own expected output, which is the right thing to model for an ordinary market and an incomplete picture on one where a replacement's numbers are added to his. What this column does and does not tell you These are match statistics, not bet settlements. Everything above is what players did on a pitch. We do not know which lines a bookmaker offered, whether anybody backed them, whether Super Sub applied to that market, or how any individual bet was settled. Nothing here should be read as a bet won or lost. Market coverage belongs to the bookmaker. Which markets and competitions carry the rule varies by operator and can change. Check the operator's own terms. The numbers move after the match. Provider stat corrections land for days, and they move in both directions. Between two runs of the same query a tackle was added to the Brighton game, and a shot on target came off another, taking the 2+ shots on target count down from three to two. Treat every total here as a snapshot. Updated for the full round. This edition first published with nine matches, before Fulham v Chelsea had been played, and now covers all ten. From Gameweek 2 the column runs on the Tuesday, once the round is complete. Lines overlap. A pair reaching 1+ tackles may also reach 2+. The 100 counts thresholds, not bets. 18+. articles.title: Three Players Who Just Became Very FPL Relevant
articles.excerpt: All three are owned by fewer than three percent of managers. All three cost £6.0m or less. All three scored on the opening weekend, and one of them we flagged before a ball was kicked.
articles.source_type: Head-to-head player comparison, goalkeeper and position value analysis
articles.body: Three Players Who Just Became Very FPL Relevant Three Players Who Just Became Very FPL Relevant The opening weekend of an FPL season is where template squads meet reality. Erling Haaland, in seven out of ten teams, did not score. Three players owned by barely anyone did. Here are the three whose weekend actually changes something, with what they cost and how many managers already have them. Ownership and prices are from the Statz FPL data at the time of writing. Anton Stach, Leeds, £6.0m, 1.2% owned Stach scored the only goal at the City Ground, winning Leeds the round's sole away victory against a Forest side the model made 44.8% favourites. We flagged him before the season started: in our FPL coverage he was the deep cut, a top-12 projected player in the entire game at £6.0m with ownership that rounded to nobody. That case has not weakened. A midfielder at that price who takes set pieces and arrives in the box is the definition of an FPL differential, and 1.2% ownership means his goals move your rank rather than keeping you level. Jack Hinshelwood, Brighton, £6.0m, 0.9% owned Two goals in a 4-0 win, in a Brighton side missing Baleba, Mitoma and Ferguson. That last part is the important part: Hinshelwood's route into the team came from an injury list, and the question every FPL manager now has to answer is what happens when those three are fit. At £6.0m and under 1% ownership he is the sort of pick that wins you a gameweek. Whether he holds the shirt into September is a different question, and the predicted line-ups will answer it before the deadline rather than after. Maxim De Cuyper, Brighton, £4.5m, 2.7% owned The one that matters most, because of the price. A £4.5m defender who scored and kept a clean sheet in the same afternoon is exactly the profile our budget enablers guide was written about: the cheap slot that quietly funds a premium elsewhere while contributing points of its own. The honest caveat One gameweek is one gameweek. Two of these three owe their minutes at least partly to somebody else's injury, and a single haul is not a projection. The way to judge them is the same as it was in July: look at the expected minutes first and the points second. The Statz Season Rankings model both across all 38 gameweeks, and the Team Planner will tell you what any of them is projected to add to your specific squad rather than to a hypothetical one. articles.body: FPL Gameweek 1 Review and Takeaways - Don’t Overreact - Full90 FPL Skip to content FPL Gameweek 1 Review and Takeaways - Don’t Overreact The FPL General picked the wrong season to go without the two-mium. If he had started without Haaland and Bruno Fernandes this season he would be laughing. And that kind of summarises gameweek 1. Outside of the Arsenal picks, and Szoboszlai nobody owned by more than 25% of managers returned. If Pedro doesn’t return tomorrow this will have been one of those good weeks to have a bad week. So, I can’t be too upset to be on 46 points all out. Though obviously I am frustrated, I am trying not to overreact to anything. Just look how crazy some of the opening day results are based on our pre-season expectations. We know almost nothing. If you had a plan coming into this season, stick to it. As most of the PL teams now know, stability matters… Don’t Overreact The clear caveat is that this is still only one week’s worth of information I am going to do some conjecture with it. We will likely see in a couple of weeks what is the “truth.” I’m writing this at the top so that I don’t have to say “we will see” after every statement. Just remember, Reijnders looked like the next De Bruyne after gw1 last season… Did Bench Boost 1 Work? Well, it wasn’t great for me but it was fine and I am happy it’s done. I got 9 points which is about the minimum you expect. Joe smashed it with 18 points though – good for him, the little bastard. Match-By-Match Reviews I watched 4 games this weekend and the highlights for the rest. I’ve also reviewed all the stats so we can see who was lucky and who wasn’t. Arsenal 3-0 Coventry xG 1.88-0.20 Arsenal Smash Coventry The first game of the season was a bloodbath. It was hard to tell whether Arsenal were just elite or Coventry were just dreadful. I suspect a bit of both. On xG, it was only 1.88-0.20 so maybe we shouldn’t read too much into this. But it’s hard not to when you add this performance to the Community Shield performance – Arsenal’s attack was just way better than I remember it being last season. Partly that is down to newboy Tzolis who had 4 shots for 0.19 xG and 3 key passes for 0.14 xA – if you watched the game you’ll be shocked about how low that is because he looked electric. He was even stepping into a sort of second striker role when Arsenal worked the ball down the right, which they frequently do when Saka is playing. He didn’t make a full 90, getting hooked at 76 mins for Eze which is a bit of a concern. My conclusion on him is this then, if you picked him then it was a good one but I am not desperate to get him in right now. That’s pretty much how I feel about Odegaard too who also put up 3 key passes for 0.1 xA and 3 shots for 0.21 xG. The thing about Ode is that he is so involved in everything that he takes the bonus points too. But he also went off at 76 mins for Merino As expected, neither Saka nor Rice made it much past 65 mins. Until they play a 90, I just don’t think we can go there. In defence, they looked solid of course. None of them got DefCons but Coventry were really bad so I’m not surprised. Of course Cala got the goal and was a good pick but it didn’t help my nerves about rotation when he went off before 90. Are Coventry Fucked? As for Coventry, I think they were really, really shit. I know that Arsenal were the winners of the Premier league last year but that was some weak, pathetic shit we saw from Coventry. It’s probably not an original thought to say I don’t think that Lampard is a great coach but this terrible performance reminded me. Thomas got defcons at least. Hull City 2-0 Man United xG 1.01-1.83 Disastrous Start for Man United In complete contrast to Coventry, Hull looked properly up for this game. If you watched the highlights you’d be forgiven for thinking that Hull dominated but United were better on xG and put up 21 shots to Hulls 8 shots. But still. Cunha started up top and had 3 shots for 0.24 xG and 2 key passes for 0.21 xA. He was hooked after 80 mins. Mbeumo put up 4 shots for 0.5xG and 0.23 xA and lasted the full 90 mins. Dorgu started left wing and put up 0.47 xG from three shots in a single half before being replaced with Rashford who didn’t get a single shot off. Sesko played 23 mins and only got 1 shot off for 0.04 xG. Bruno Fernandes put up 3 shots for 0.08 xG – all from miles outside the box – and 3 key passes for 0.26 xA. A lot of these guys then outperformed the Arsenal boys on underlyings but just failed to actually put the ball in the net. They lacked a lot of energy and just seemed to be so slow – letting Hull grab the ball far too often. I don’t think we should worry too much about Mbeumo and Bruno – they both played 90 and put up reasonable numbers. But, I am a little worried about how much depth Man United have because that means that any of these guys, besides maybe Bruno, could get hooked before 90 and we really want 90 mins. None of the back line got close to defensive contribution points and they were obviously not that great either. Perfect Premier League Start for Hull Realistically, I can’t see us going for any Hull assets regularly but I want to call out two interesting players. Firstly, Slater took corners and set pieces for only 4.5 – he could be a great pick for that 8th attacker slot that just sits on your bench. Obviously he also got an assist. Secondly, McBurnie had two shots in the first 20 mins, and was pretty unfortunate not to get a goal in my opinion. Again, he’s a rotation option (or Draft option). The season pass does not auto-renew. Included here, plus the mid-season refresh The Midweek Fixture No ads Across the whole site and every tool, while you are a member Still free for everyone: the fixture ticker Ipswich 2-1 Sunderland xG 1.80-0.66 Ipswich Catch the Black Cats Napping Literally. The first goal was a fantastic counter-attack that saw Enciso drive forward and assist Emersonn who put up 0.82 xG from 3 shots in just 66 mins. Enciso went off injured and Jack Clarke came on and scored the second. O’Shea got 18 defensive contributions from right back and Nunez got 12 defcons in 80 mins. Sunderland confirm fears? I said multiple times coming into the season that I was worried about these guys – they’re underlying numbers suggest they were pretty poor last season, potentially this result confirms those fears. However, they did most of their good work at home so maybe not. Angulo took the free-kick for the goal and it was brilliant. But that was about all he did and he only lasted 59 mins. Brobbey had 2 shots for 0.3 xG but was taken off after 67 mins. Le Fee did basically nothing and got subbed at 80 mins. My hero Granit Xhaka got defcon points and an assist after being fouled for the free kick. Ballard narrowly missed out on defcon points and O’Nien was replaced on 67 mins. Brentford 3-0 Spurs xG 3.87-0.57 Spurs Still Suck We’ve just reviewed all the promoted teams and NONE of them conceded this much in terms of xG. They conceded 26 shots. 26! It was an almost completely new backline of Robertson, Senesi, van Hecke and Gray – Robbo and Senesi got defcon points and van Hecke was only 1 away from getting the points. But obviously, they conceded 3 times… And, as you can tell from the expected numbers, they were woeful going forward. Their attack is a hard avoid at the moment. Brentford’s Stability Prevails 10 of Brentford’s players were regulars from last season. Schade smashed Dango out of the water in terms of underlying numbers – 0.52 xG from 5 shots v.s. 0.05 xG from 2 shots. The latter was subbed off after 67 mins for Anthony top cap off basically every Dango owner’s fear come true. In a rare turn of events, Thiago hit the post with a pen to finish with no returns from an xG of 1.0. There was only one newbie to Brentford’s team and he absolutely smashed his debut. Sangare got defcons, one real assist and one FPL one. He was great but it is worth noting his xA was only 0.33. At the back, Ajer got DefCons but might not keep his spot when van den Berg is back. Kayode had 4 shots for 0.5 xG and walked away with a goal. Lewis-Potter played left-back and scored from his 2 shots and 0.77xG. Everton 2-0 Palace xG: 1.12-1.96 Everton Ride Their Luck A bit like last season then. They somehow give up a tonne of xG but walk away with a clean sheet. Nobody got defensive contribution points but Tarkowski was only one off and Branthwaite was only two off. Ndiaye was the best 6.0 going into this week because he got a full 90 and an assist. Dewsbury-Hall scored off 0.12 xG and Barry scored off two shots and 0.45 xG. Palace Falter The big news is that Ismalia Sarr didn’t even make the starting lineup after Galatassaray made a bid for him. Munoz was still in the team (despite the transfer rumours around him). He had a couple of shots in the first half but was subbed at 55 mins. Richards, Wharton, and Kamada all walked away with DefCon Points. As expected, Mateta didn’t play 90 and was subbed at 63 mins for Strand Larsen after two shots for 0.70 xG. Man City 2 – 1 Bournemouth xG: 2.36-0.63 Maresca’s Fifa Career Enzo Maresca is playing Fifa. Either that, or he’s taking tips from Thomas Tuchel. By my count, he started six defenders – with Guehi playing DM and O’Reilly playing in the 10. Foden was playing on the right-wing which I think was also weird. The goal they conceded didn’t do anything to convince me that the defensive frailties witnessed in the Community Shield were a one-off. As if they wanted to make City feel better for being bad in defence, Bournemouth left Guehi open whilst two of them wrestled Ruben Semenyo was the only midfielder to make 90 mins and he switched from the left to the right when Grealish came on for Foden on the 82nd minute. Cherki got the assist after coming on got O’Reilly in the 63rd minute. He found Gvardiol in the box basically playing second striker which is REALLY interesting if he can lock down a starting spot. Of course, Haaland blanked which basically meant that nobody got a return from their captain in gameweek 1 Bournemouth Brilliant? Well. No. Not really. They looked competent and good, like they normally do. But they didn’t create that much and relied on counter-attacking. Evanilson got the assist to the goal but didn’t get a shot off. Tavernier was the one who scored and the only one of the front four to make it to 90 mins. Silva got defensive contributions. Brighton 4 – 0 Villa xG: 3.67-0.31 Villa Are In Trouble The xG numbers show that the final scoreline doesn’t lie. Villa were shit. It’s probably not escaped your attention that they have been gutted by transfers out but I expected that Emery would just pull something out of the bag and put on a decent performance, even if they lost. Well that was wrong. Watkins must be on his way out because I don’t see any good reason not to start him. That hopefully will make Jackson a good pick if he goes over there. Brighton Actually Brilliant 21 shots, 6 big chances, 3.67 xG and a 4-0 win against an Emery team. Hats off to them. None of them got close to defcon points but that’s probably not a shock given how bad Villa were. Rutter started at striker but I’d still be nervous about going there until the transfer window closes. Hinshelwood got two goals from 3 shots for 1.41 xG. He was quite overlooked before the season began, including from me, despite how high many of us were on him at the end of last season. De Cuyper played on the wing which is interesting if that carries on. Gross did nothing which made me happy and most man

articles.body: Elche vs Barcelona Predictions & Betting Tips Elche vs Barcelona Predictions and Betting Tips - La Liga Barcelona start the season as the model's champions: 53.8% in our La Liga projection , the best attack in the division, and a first assignment at Elche, who the same model expects to spend the year in a six-club scrap to stay up. You know how this is supposed to go. So does the market, which is the problem with betting on it. Kickoff is 8:30pm UK on Sunday. Numbers from the live Statz match centre Lineups and Player News As with all La Liga fixtures, Statz does not publish a predicted XI the way it does for the Premier League, so the names below are the players our props board expects to be involved rather than a confirmed team sheet. Barcelona 's expected group includes Joan García in goal, Koundé, Eric García and Balde across the back, Marc Bernal and Fermín López in midfield, with Lamine Yamal and Raphinha providing the width. Elche are expected to feature Dituro, Affengruber, Chust, Sangaré and Valera. No confirmed absences have been published for either side at the time of writing. Recent Form Barcelona's closing five read WWLWL, Elche's DLWDD. The projections are emphatic: 2.21 goals to 1.00, with Elche given a 10.9% chance of a clean sheet , one of the lowest numbers on the weekend's board anywhere in Europe. Barcelona win this in 64.3% of simulations. Elche take it in 15.2%, which is a bigger number than a 9.00 price suggests. Statz Team Projections See the live Statz numbers for this fixture Interesting Player Stats Marc Bernal to be carded at 3.75 is the standout, and it is not close: a 32.3% projection is the highest on either side's board. A young midfielder holding the middle of the pitch while his side chases the ball for long spells is a booking waiting to happen, and Elche will be running at him. Eric García at 5.50 is the same argument at a bigger price. Beyond that the board leans on fouls markets from our commentary-parsed data, which are noisier than the cards and shots lines and are worth treating as softer evidence. Statz Bet Builder See the live Statz numbers for this fixture Betting Angles Barcelona at 1.30 implies a 77% chance. The model says 64.3%. Over 2.5 at 1.44 implies 69% against a 62.3% projection. Both teams to score at 1.75 is the closest thing to a fair price in the game, and even that is a shade the wrong side of the line. Which leaves one number the model genuinely likes, and it is the one nobody wants: Elche at 9.00 , where a 15.2% chance is being sold as an 11.1% one. That is a real edge on a bet that loses six times out of seven. Summary The bet: no bet on the result, and a small one on Elche at 9.00 if you must. I am not going to talk you into a 9.00 shot on the opening weekend, and I am certainly not going to talk you into 1.30 about a side that lost two of its last five. Some games are priced so that the honest answer is to watch them. If you want an angle rather than a bet, Marc Bernal's card at 3.75 is the soundest number on the board and has nothing to do with who wins. articles.body: Espanyol vs Real Madrid Predictions & Betting Tips Espanyol vs Real Madrid Predictions and Betting Tips - La Liga Real Madrid begin a season in which second place will not be forgiven. Our La Liga preview has them winning the title in 39.3% of simulations against Barcelona's 53.8%, a gap of less than two projected points across 38 games. In a race that tight, a Saturday night in Cornella is not a warm-up. It is one of the 38 games that decides it. Espanyol are the sort of opponent that has quietly ruined title bids before: awkward, at home, with nothing expected of them. The model gives them 18.1%, which is more than you might think. Kickoff is 8:30pm UK. Numbers from the live Statz match centre Lineups and Player News Statz does not publish predicted line-ups for La Liga the way it does for the Premier League, so treat the names below as the players our props board expects to be involved rather than a confirmed team sheet. On that basis Real Madrid 's expected group is built around Courtois in goal, a back line featuring Alexander-Arnold, Huijsen, Konaté and Cucurella, with Valverde and Güler in midfield and Mbappé and Vinícius Júnior ahead of them. Espanyol 's side is expected to include Riedel, Expósito, Núñez and Álvaro Calatrava. No confirmed absences have been published for either side at the time of writing. Recent Form Madrid closed last season WLWWW, Espanyol LWWDW at home. The projections split them clearly: 1.86 goals to 0.95, with Madrid given a 38.8% clean sheet against Espanyol's 15.6%. That is a comfortable enough read, and it is worth holding onto the gap between it and the price. A 57.9% chance is not the same thing as a formality. Statz Team Projections See the live Statz numbers for this fixture Interesting Player Stats The pick of the board belongs to the home side. Álvaro Calatrava 1+ shot on target at 2.10 carries a 50.8% projection and a last-five line of two, three, zero, two and four. Espanyol will not see much of the ball, but he is the man they aim at when they get it, and a shade over evens for a player who has hit the target in four of his last five is the most sensible number in this match. The braver version is his 2+ at 7.00. For Madrid, Trent Alexander-Arnold to be carded at 5.50 (21.3%) is the one the model rates, and Dean Huijsen at 4.50 carries the higher projection at 25.9% - centre-backs against a side that will be countering all night. Statz Bet Builder See the live Statz numbers for this fixture Betting Angles Here is the thing about this game: the market has taken it away from you. Real Madrid at 1.44 implies a 69% chance. The model says 57.9%. That is not a small disagreement, and it is the wrong way round for anyone wanting to back the favourite. The goals markets are no kinder. Over 2.5 at 1.62 implies nearly 62% against a projection of 53.2%. The only two prices on the board that the model actually rates are under 2.5 goals at 2.30 (46.8% against an implied 43.5%) and Espanyol at 7.00, where an 18.1% chance is priced as a 14.3% one. Summary The bet: Under 2.5 goals at 2.30. Madrid should win. They will probably win without ever going through the gears, which is precisely the shape of game that finishes 2-0 rather than 4-1, and the under is the one price here that the model prefers to the market's version of it. If you want the lottery ticket, Espanyol at 7.00 is genuinely underpriced by the model's reckoning. Just do not confuse underpriced with likely. articles.excerpt: There’s a moment every card player knows. You’re one card away. You need a removal spell, or a fourth land, or literally anything that answers the thing sitting across the table. You draw. It isn’t that. Whether that was bad luck or a bad deck is a question you can actually answer, and it doesn’t … Continue reading Calculating Outs: The Basic Probability Every TCG Player Should Know The post Calculating Outs: The Basic Probability Every TCG Player Should Know appeared first on .

articles.body: Calculating Outs: The Basic Probability Every TCG Player Should Know - Calculating Outs: The Basic Probability Every TCG Player Should Know - Skip to content There’s a moment every card player knows. You’re one card away. You need a removal spell, or a fourth land, or literally anything that answers the thing sitting across the table. You draw. It isn’t that. Whether that was bad luck or a bad deck is a question you can actually answer, and it doesn’t take much maths. Understanding outs is probably the single biggest jump in play quality available to a casual player, and it costs nothing. What an Out Actually Is An out is any card in your deck that solves the problem in front of you. The important word is “any”. Newer players tend to count one specific card, which is why the numbers feel so grim. Experienced players count everything that does the job. If you need to deal with a creature, your outs aren’t just your one removal spell. They’re every removal spell, every bounce effect, every board wipe, every blocker big enough to hold the line, and every tutor that can find one of those. Counting properly usually turns three outs into nine or ten, and that changes the answer enormously. The One Calculation You Need The formal tool is the hypergeometric distribution, which sounds intimidating and isn’t. It answers the question: if my deck has this many cards, and this many of them are what I want, what’s the chance of seeing at least one in the next few draws? You don’t need to compute it by hand. Plenty of free calculators exist, and any of them will do. What matters is developing intuition for the shape of the answer. The rough rule for a single draw is simple division. Ten outs in a forty-card library is a one in four chance. Ten outs in a ninety-card library is closer to one in nine. Numbers Worth Having in Your Head In a 60-card constructed deck, if you run four copies of a card, you’ll see at least one in your opening seven roughly 40 percent of the time. That’s a number worth sitting with, because most players assume four copies means they’ll reliably have it. They won’t. They’ll have it a bit less than half the time. Push it to eight functionally similar cards and that figure climbs to roughly 65 percent. Twelve gets you to around 80 percent. The pattern is the point. Each additional copy helps less than the one before, and getting from “usually” to “almost always” costs far more slots than getting from “rarely” to “usually”. Why Commander Feels So Different In a 99-card singleton deck, you can’t run four copies of anything. One copy of a card is a genuinely unreliable plan, and this is why Commander games feel so swingy compared to constructed formats. Say you want a specific card by turn five, having seen roughly twelve cards. One copy in 99 gives you somewhere around a 12 percent chance. That’s not a plan, that’s a hope. Which explains why good Commander decks look the way they do. They’re built around a commander you can always access, plus a lot of redundancy, plus tutors that turn one card into many. Redundancy Beats Tutoring New players discover tutors and want to jam eight of them. It rarely works as well as expected, because a tutor costs you a card and often costs you a turn. Running eight cards that all do roughly the same job is usually stronger than running four plus four ways to find them. It’s faster, it’s cheaper, and the maths is better. Save tutors for effects that genuinely have no substitute. Mulligans Change the Maths The London mulligan, where you draw seven and put cards on the bottom, is more powerful than most casual players use it as. If your deck needs a specific piece to function, mulliganing to look for it is often correct even at the cost of a card. A six-card hand that does what your deck wants to do beats a seven-card hand that does nothing. The practical version: know before you shuffle up what your hand needs to contain. If it doesn’t, ship it. Players lose far more games to keeping bad sevens than to mulliganing too aggressively. Variance Is Not Bad Luck Here’s the mindset bit, and it matters more than any calculation. If you have a 70 percent chance to find your answer and you don’t, you didn’t get unlucky in any meaningful sense. Three times in ten, that happens. It’s the deck working as designed. Players who understand this stop tilting, and they stop making bad deck changes after single games. One loss tells you almost nothing. Ten games with a pattern tells you something. The whole reason casinos and bookmakers are profitable businesses is that most people badly misjudge how normal a streak of bad outcomes is, and the same misjudgement is what makes people rip apart a perfectly good deck after one rough evening. Betting on trading card games has grown with the competitive scene, as Magic, Pokémon, and Yu-Gi-Oh! tournaments now draw enough viewership to support match odds and outright winner markets. Since results hinge on deck composition, draw variance, and shifting metagames, informed punters study player histories and format trends rather than backing names alone. Markets remain niche, so most action sits with a handful of sportsbooks and the best usdt casino platforms with fast tether deposits and withdrawals that have added esports sections. Stick to licensed operators and set deposit limits before staking. Try It With Your Own Deck Pick one card you always want in your opening hand. Count every card in your deck that does the same job, not just the exact one. Put those two numbers into a free hypergeometric calculator with a draw of seven. If the answer is under 50 percent and your deck genuinely needs that effect early, you’re short. Add more, or add cards that do something similar. That one exercise will improve most casual decks more than any single card purchase. Bring the list down to the shop and someone will happily talk through what else does the job.
